OVERVIEW:

We're looking for a frontend Automation Engineer to join our Quality Engineering (QE) team for our Mobile apps, helping us build and scale automated testing for our iOS and Android apps. You'll add to and maintain the automation framework that catch issues before customers ever see them, working closely with mobile developers, fellow automation engineers, and product teams to keep our releases fast and dependable. 

This is a hands-on, mid-level role: you'll take ownership of automation suites and specific quality areas within mobile, while collaborating with senior engineers on framework direction and best practice.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

  • Adding and maintaining automated tests for our iOS and Android apps in Java using Appium. 
  • Run and scale automated test execution across real devices and browsers using BrowserStack. 
  • Integrate mobile automation into CI/CD pipelines to support fast, reliable, and frequent releases. 
  • Collaborate with mobile developers and QE engineers to define test strategy and identify areas for automation coverage. 
  • Investigate test failures, distinguishing genuine defects from flaky tests, and drive fixes to improve suite reliability. 
  • Maintain and improve the Appium/Java test framework and our BrowserStack test infrastructure. 
  • Contribute to code reviews, share automation best practice, and help raise the overall quality bar across the mobile team. 
  • Report on test coverage and quality metrics to stakeholders across engineering and product. 
  • Explore and adopt AI and agentic tooling to speed up test creation, triage failures, and improve automation coverage.

Essential Criteria:

  • Experience building and/or maintaining full-code automation frameworks with Selenium/Appium. 
  • Solid programming skills in an Object Oriented Programming language, including Java (ideal), C#, Kotlin etc. 
  • Experience with BDD frameworks (e.g. Cucumber, SpecFlow). 
  • Experience running automated tests on BrowserStack (or a similar cloud device platform).

At Gymshark, Finance is about far more than reporting numbers. We partner with teams across the business to help drive better decisions, unlock opportunities, and support sustainable growth.

We're looking for a Commercial Finance Manager - Brand & Marketing to become the trusted finance partner to one of the most influential functions in our business. In this role, you'll sit at the heart of Gymshark's Brand and Marketing teams, helping to shape investment decisions, measure performance, challenge thinking, and ensure we're maximising the impact of every pound we spend.

This is an opportunity for a commercially minded finance professional who thrives on partnering with senior stakeholders, influencing decision-making, and turning data into meaningful business insight.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING.

As the dedicated finance business partner for Brand & Marketing, you'll:

  • Partner closely with Heads of Brand and Marketing, providing financial insight and commercial challenge that supports profitable growth.
  • Analyse and interpret financial performance, translating complex data into actionable recommendations for stakeholders.
  • Develop, monitor and report on both financial and non-financial KPIs to assess the effectiveness and ROI of Brand and Marketing investment.
  • Lead the budgeting and forecasting processes, ensuring plans are ambitious, achievable and aligned to Gymshark's strategic objectives.
  • Deliver regular reforecasts, helping the business adapt quickly to changing priorities and performance trends.
  • Provide clear analysis and commentary on spend performance versus budget and forecast, highlighting risks and opportunities.
  • Hold stakeholders accountable to agreed actions and support departments in managing spend effectively.
  • Challenge investment decisions constructively where plans may place sustainable profitability at risk.
  • Create impactful presentations and insight packs for senior leaders, Directors and Executive stakeholders.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, systems and ways of working, including the application of AI and automation.
  • Contribute to a collaborative, high-performance culture within Finance and across the wider business.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR.

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical finance expertise with excellent commercial judgement and stakeholder management skills.

You'll ideally have:

  • ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent professional accounting qualification.
  • Proven finance business partnering experience within a commercial environment.
  • Experience supporting Brand, Marketing, Creative or Customer Acquisition functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to influence strategic decision-making.
  • Experience working with senior stakeholders and challenging constructively when required.
  • A track record of delivering budgets, forecasts and insightful financial analysis in a fast-paced environment.
  • The ability to communicate complex financial information clearly to non-finance audiences.
  • A proactive, self-starting approach and comfort operating in an environment that evolves quickly.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using financial systems, reporting tools and Microsoft Office.

This is a hybrid role. The successful candidate will be required to attend either:

  • a minimum of three days per week at GSHQ, Solihull, or
  • if London-based, a minimum of two days per week at GSHQ, Solihull and one day per week from our London office.

THE ROLE.

As a Designer in menswear, you'll create and develop world-class product that embodies the Gymshark DNA. Working closely with Design Leadership and cross-functional partners, you'll take ownership of product designs from concept through to execution, delivering commercially successful products that resonate with our global community.

This is an exciting opportunity for a creative, trend-aware designer who is passionate about sportswear, performance apparel and product innovation.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING.

  • Designing and developing Menswear products across multiple categories.
  • Researching fashion, sportswear and consumer trends to identify new opportunities.
  • Creating and maintaining design concepts throughout the product development journey.
  • Collaborating with Product Development and wider Product Creation teams to achieve design and fit intent.
  • Selecting appropriate materials, trims and colour palettes to bring concepts to life.
  • Creating clear and accurate design specifications and technical documentation.
  • Presenting design concepts and seasonal developments to key stakeholders.
  • Supporting and mentoring Assistant Designers and Graduate Designers where appropriate.
  • Working cross-functionally to ensure products are delivered on time, on brand and to the highest standards.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED.

  • Degree in Fashion, Sportswear or Apparel Design.
  • Experience designing apparel within a fashion, sportswear or activewear environment.
  • Strong understanding of product construction, materials, colour and consumer trends.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • A portfolio showcasing creative versatility across apparel categories.
This is an opportunity to help create products worn by millions around the world while working alongside some of the best creative talent in the industry. You'll be part of a collaborative, ambitious team where your ideas can directly influence the future of Gymshark Menswear.

This is a hybrid role and requires the successful candidate to attend at least THREE days a week in GSIQ, Solihull, UK.

OVERVIEW:

We're looking for a Floor Lead to help shape the Gymshark experience at our White City store. Located in one of London's most dynamic retail destinations, our White City store is more than just a place to shop. It's a space where our community comes together, where brand moments are created, and where customers connect with Gymshark on a deeper level.

As a Floor Lead, you'll be at the heart of that experience. Leading from the shop floor, you'll inspire your team, deliver exceptional customer experiences, and create an environment where both people and performance thrive. You'll be a visible leader, setting the standard through your energy, coaching, and commitment to excellence. From driving daily priorities and developing teammates to supporting operational excellence and acting as manager on duty, you'll play a key role in bringing the Gymshark brand to life every single day.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

  • Leading from the shop floor and creating exceptional experiences for every customer.
  • Inspiring and motivating teammates through positive leadership, energy, and example.
  • Running daily huddles, communicating priorities, and setting the team up for success.
  • Providing real-time coaching and feedback to support individual and team development.
  • Helping customers find the right products through genuine conversations and expert product knowledge.
  • Supporting store performance through strong service standards, sales confidence, and commercial awareness.
  • Championing Gymshark Membership and helping customers understand the benefits.
  • Taking ownership of shop floor standards, ensuring the store is always clean, organised, and customer-ready.
  • Supporting stock replenishment, delivery processing, and back-of-house operations when needed.
  • Acting as a keyholder and supporting opening and closing procedures.
  • Managing customer queries and escalations with confidence, empathy, and sound judgement.
  • Stepping up as manager on duty when required, making decisions that support the team, customer, and business.
  • Adapting to changing priorities and helping the store succeed during busy trading periods

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

Essential Criteria:

  • Experience in a leadership or supervisory role with a proven ability to coach, support, and develop others.
  • Experience working within a retail store environment.
  • Previous keyholder experience.
  • A track record of delivering exceptional customer service in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong communication skills and confidence leading and influencing others.
  • A positive, energetic, and people-first approach to leadership.
  • The ability to multitask and maintain high standards across customer service, operations, and store presentation.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to make decisions when required.
  • A collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively as part of One Team.
  • A passion for continuous improvement, learning, and personal development.
  • A genuine interest in fitness, wellness, and community.
  • Valid Right to Work in the UK

OVERVIEW:

This role exists to build and maintain the iOS app that a large share of Gymshark customers shop through, at a standard that holds under peak load. You will turn refined product work into features that are shipped, tested and observable, and improves the quality of the code you touch.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

CRAFT  

  • Writes production Swift confidently. Most new work is SwiftUI; the app still contains UIKit that is being migrated, so both are relevant. 
  • Works effectively in a modular codebase. Understands why a type belongs in one module rather than another, and adds features without crossing module boundaries. 
  • Applies Clean Architecture and MVVM as standard, can explain the separation of concerns, and identifies where a pull request breaks it. 
  • Writes unit tests as part of the work rather than afterwards, and is comfortable building test doubles. Some of the team work test-first, and we want to increase that. 
  • Understands Swift concurrency sufficiently to avoid data races, and raises it when a problem exceeds their experience. 
  • Diagnoses production issues from crash reporting and analytics, and identifies the root cause independently. 
  • Treats performance, accessibility and app size as part of completing a piece of work. 
  • Understands the path their code takes after merge: CI, review, distribution and App Store submission, and the common failure points at each stage. 
  • Uses a branching strategy consistently and writes pull requests that are straightforward to review. 
  • Raises design specifications that conflict with the Human Interface Guidelines rather than implementing them unchanged. 
  • Considers security and dependency risk routinely, and can assess whether a third-party SDK should be added

DELIVERY

  • Contributes actively to Agile ceremonies, and raises when one is no longer useful.

Content Marketing Manager

Duetto  |  Remote-first, United Kingdom / Spain  |  Reports to VP, Growth Marketing

About the role

We have a bold brand voice, a growing library of campaigns, and a product story worth telling — what we need is someone who can help bring all of it to life, day in and day out.

This is a hands-on content role for a versatile writer who's looking to build their craft across formats: one day you're writing campaign copy for a demand gen push, the next you're drafting a social series, the next you're turning a product update into content people actually want to engage with. You'll work from clear briefs and direction, with support from senior content and marketing colleagues, and your job is to turn that direction into content that ships — quickly and well.

This isn't a role about setting content strategy — that sits elsewhere in the team. It's about strong, reliable execution: taking a brief and producing content that's on-brand and ready to go.

If you're a solid writer looking to grow across formats and channels, who takes direction well and enjoys the craft of making content land — this is a great next step.

What you'll work on

Brand and campaign content

  • Help produce content that supports our demand gen campaigns, brand-building efforts, and always-on content calendar — blogs, guides, social copy, email, sales enablement material, and more
  • Apply our brand voice consistently across everything you touch — punchy, smart, and customer-focused
  • Work from briefs set by senior colleagues, asking good questions to make sure the output lands

Product content

  • Help turn product updates and feature releases into content that goes beyond the feature list — finding the customer angle
  • Work with the product marketing team to stay close to what's shipping
  • Support launch communications and update announcements

Social-first content

  • Think social-first on what you make — considering platform, format, and hook
  • Support experimentation with format and style — short-form video, carousels, text posts, customer spotlights

Video and content production

  • Help brief video agencies and creative resources, under guidance from senior team members
  • Partner with design and creative to help produce on-brand content
  • Support individual pieces of content from concept through to publish

AI-enabled content production

  • Use Duetto's AI-enabled content tools to help produce content at pace, without compromising quality
  • Use AI to speed up drafting, iteration, and adaptation of content across formats

User-generated content

  • Help spot and support opportunities to activate customers as content creators
  • Work with the customer marketing function to help surface and share UGC
  • Contribute to a growing library of customer voices and product proof points

Channel and surface coverage

  • Help adapt content for the right surface — social, in-app, customer newsletters, website, sales enablement, partner comms
  • Work with the broader content and growth teams to keep content calendars full
  • Help maintain a steady content cadence

What we're looking for

Experience

  • 2–4 years in a content marketing, copywriting, or brand content role, with a portfolio that shows range across formats and channels
  • Experience with both campaign/brand content and product-related content is a plus
  • Comfortable supporting work with external creative or video resources, under direction
  • Background in B2B SaaS is a plus, but strong writing and a willingness to learn matter more than sector experience

Skills and capabilities

  • Strong writer — able to take a brief and turn it into content that's clear and on-brand
  • Social-first instincts — you naturally think about platform, format, and hook
  • Organised and reliable — you can manage a few pieces of content at once and hit deadlines
  • Good at taking direction — you don't need a strategy explained in detail to run with a brief, but you're not expected to set the strategy
  • Curious and eager to grow your craft across formats and channels

You will lead a small, high-leverage team (a Salesforce Admin and a GTM Engineer) and partner closely with Revenue Strategy & Planning, Sales Operations, Revenue Enablement, Customer Success Operations, Product & Technology, and Information Security.

Your first job is to bring Gong to life, from rollout plan to adoption.

Responsibilities

Gong Rollout

  • Plan and Launch: Define scope, timeline, rollout waves, risks, and success measures. Run the project and keep commercial leadership informed.
  • Integrate: Connect Gong to Salesforce, calendar, email, and conferencing tools, so every conversation lands on the right account, contact, and opportunity.
  • Govern: Set up roles, permissions, recording policies, and consent practices with Legal & Compliance and Information Security. Our clients work in regulated markets, so we get this right from day one.
  • Configure: Build trackers, scorecards, deal boards, and dashboards that reflect our sales process, products, and competitors.
  • Enable: Partner with Revenue Enablement to turn Gong into a coaching engine, including call libraries, onboarding playlists, manager coaching routines, and rep-level insight into ramp time and win rate.
  • Measure: Define adoption and usage metrics, report them to commercial leadership on a regular cadence, and act on what they show.
  • Align the Data: Work with Revenue Strategy & Planning so Gong data matches pipeline, forecast, and reporting in Snowflake and Sigma.
  • Manage the Vendor: Own the Gong relationship with Procurement, including contract milestones, license utilization, and renewal planning.

Revenue Technology Stack

  • Salesforce: Own process, workflows, and governance. Partner with Sales and Marketing Operations on data hygiene and workflows, end to end.
  • Connected Tools: Administer and optimize our data orchestration, enrichment, lead routing, and content management tools. Retire what we don’t use and integrate what we do.
  • Signal-to-Action Workflows: Build workflows that turn signals into Sales rep and CSM actions, and own the signal-routing handoff that sends product usage and CSM insight to Account Management queues.
  • Vendors, Roadmap, and Intake: Manage tech stack vendor relationships and renewals, run one intake and prioritization process for commercial tooling requests, and publish a roadmap that commercial leaders can see and shape.
  • AI and Automation: Evaluate AI tools with a clear build-or-buy view and show the value they create.
  • Documentation and Change: Keep the stack documented, communicate releases, and run training so changes stick.
  • Security and Compliance: Work with Information Security, Legal & Compliance, and Procurement to keep our tools and data safe.
  • People: Hire, coach, and develop the GTM Engineer and Salesforce Admin. Set clear goals and build a team that stays motivated and engaged.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years in revenue operations or sales systems, including 3+ years leading people.
  • A record of implementing conversation intelligence from kickoff to adoption. Gong experience is strongly preferred; experience with a similar CI platform also counts.
  • Deep Salesforce expertise across architecture, data model, automation, integrations, and governance. Salesforce certifications are a plus.
  • Hands-on experience connecting GTM tools through APIs and workflow automation platforms.
  • Working knowledge of a data warehouse and BI tools, such as Snowflake and Sigma, to connect system data to reporting.
  • Comfort with AI-enabled workflows, including LLM-based automation and MCP, and a clear sense of where automation shines and where people still lead.
  • Experience with enablement, lead routing, and sales intelligence platforms.
  • Experience managing vendors, contracts, and budgets alongside Procurement and Finance.
  • Strong change management skills. You can bring skeptical sellers along and make the new tool the easy choice.
  • Experience in B2B SaaS, data, or financial information services is a plus.

You pair process and engineering rigor with seller empathy. You like a clear target and a blank page. You challenge how things have always been done and back your ideas with data. You explain complex systems in plain language, whether you’re talking to a rep, a lawyer, or an executive.

Similarweb makes the digital world measurable: Which markets are growing? Where is demand moving? How do consumers find, engage with and ultimately choose brands?

Global brands including Google, eBay and Adidas use our data to make decisions they would otherwise make on instinct. We are listed on the New York Stock Exchange and recently surpassed $300 million in annual recurring revenue, with more than 470 customers now investing over $100,000 a year with us.

Enterprise is where the next phase of that growth in EMEA comes from, and we are adding an Enterprise Account Executive in London to help deliver it.

Why this role exists

Enterprise new business is our strategic priority in EMEA, and this team is how we win it. We sell directly into the market rather than managing existing accounts. That approach has been built and proven across the region, and the next phase is growing the team behind it.

The timing helps. How people discover and choose brands is changing faster than at any point since search became the default, and most enterprises still have no reliable way to measure it. That is the conversation you open with executives.

The role

You will own a named list of enterprise accounts end to end, in our focus industries of Retail, CPG, Financial Services, Utilities, Telco and Travel. Your market is Tier 1 EMEA: the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the Nordics.

Beyond your named list, inbound demand and Sales Development activity generate qualified conversations across the wider market, and those come to you.

You will typically sell across marketing, strategy, insights and e-commerce. Our strongest engagements are the ones that reach Director or C-level, where the use case is tied to a decision the business is already trying to make. You will carry an annual quota with quarterly milestones.

What you will be doing

  • Meeting quarterly and annual quota by generating revenue from your named accounts and from inbound and Sales Development demand
  • Opening accounts from cold by prospecting with our own data, and qualifying inbound demand properly
  • Running the full cycle: prospecting, discovery, value case, commercial negotiation and close
  • Winning against the incumbent, a competitive bid, or the option to do nothing, by making the clearer commercial case
  • Finding the right champion inside the account, and equipping them to carry the business case when you are not in the room
  • Maintaining an accurate forecast the business can rely on

What we are looking for

  • Five or more years closing consultative, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals in high value SaaS, data or insight sales, with consistent over-achievement against target
  • Credibility at executive level, making a commercial argument rather than delivering a product demo
  • A history of building accounts from cold and turning them into revenue
  • Strong discovery. You open with questions that surface what is genuinely at stake
  • Experience selling data or insight against a broad set of use cases rather than a single point solution
  • Comfort with the procurement, legal and security review that comes with a contract of that size
  • Creativity in how you approach an account, and the confidence to test a half-formed idea on the team before you take it to a customer
  • Curiosity about where digital is going, including AI-driven discovery and changing search behaviour

Five years is a guide rather than a threshold. We are more interested in how you sell and what you have closed than in time served.

The team you are joining

We value drive, ambition and results. The team is led by a former individual contributor who has carried this number and hit it. We use a blend of sales methodologies rather than one, and we measure outcomes, not activity.

We talk about our deals openly, including the ones still in flight. That means bringing problems to the team early and sharing what worked and what didn't. It takes risk out of the pipeline and it sharpens how everyone sells.

You will not be selling alone. Marketing, Sales Development, Solution Engineering, Advisory Services and a wide range of internal support sit behind you to get deals across the line. 

Our sales stack includes Salesforce, SalesLoft, ZoomInfo, Chorus and Similarweb.

The Vercel Startups org exists to help founders navigate the shift to AI-native development with confidence. Startups move faster than ever—what used to take years now happens in days—and the decisions founders make early can either unlock scale or become long-term constraints. We partner with startups at the critical moments where technical, commercial, and strategic support starts to matter most.

We’re a talent-dense team made up of former founders, engineers, and experienced go-to-market operators who bring firsthand experience building, scaling, and supporting modern software companies. Many of us have sat on the other side of the table, making architectural decisions, navigating tradeoffs, and scaling under real constraints, and we bring that perspective into every customer interaction.

We operate with a growth mindset and strong shared ownership. We dig deep to understand our customers, work closely across functions as one team, and find ways to win even when the path forward isn’t obvious. Resilience, curiosity, and a willingness to push through hard problems are table stakes here.

  • Believes that the best revenue outcomes come from deeply successful customers, not transactional selling

  • Thrives in ambiguity and enjoys shaping how a team and motion evolves from early to more structured

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the role

Developers are building faster than ever. Humans and agents are deploying more than 6 million times a day on Vercel, spinning up over 2 million Sandboxes and serving a trillion requests per month. Every single one is powered by our own compute infrastructure.

The Persistence team sits within Vercel's Compute division. This team owns the deep infrastructure within Hive (our compute platform) focussing on storage and state for all our workloads (Builds, Sandboxes and Functions). This work is redefining compute with features like Fluid Compute, Persistent Sandboxes, and Custom Images.

As a Software Engineer on the Persistence team, you'll work on the infrastructure that runs 100s of instances across every region where our customers deploy code, rethinking low-level primitives and contributing to platform features that improve the experience for thousands of developers every day.

This role is based in London, UK. If you're within commuting distance of our London office, the role includes in-office anchor days. If you're located further afield within the UK, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

What you'll do

  • Manage and improve our fleet of clusters, running 100s of instances deployed in every region where our customers deploy and run their code.
  • Write Golang on a daily basis and use Terraform to provision infrastructure; you'll get to know Nomad as our scheduler for managing workloads.
  • Rethink the primitives of our infrastructure — working with virtual filesystems, Linux primitives, and low-level virtualisation.
  • Own the reliability and performance of our compute platform, including on-call coverage for a team where every improvement has outsized impact at scale.
  • Collaborate across teams to drive the convergence of all compute at Vercel.

What you need

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with Golang strongly preferred.
  • Deep experience with virtual machines, file systems and Linux — you like knowing how things work under the hood (tcpdump, strace, and iptables are familiar tools).
  • Experience building and operating distributed systems at scale; you design for performance and reliability.
  • Experience with schedulers and orchestrators for managing containers and non-containerised workloads (e.g. Nomad, Kubernetes).
  • Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, with a genuine enthusiasm for digging into problems that don't have obvious solutions.

Bonus if you

  • Have worked on low-level virtualisation or sandbox execution environments.
  • Have product engineering experience and care about the developer-facing impact of infrastructure decisions.
  • Have experience with on-call operations for large-scale distributed systems.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation package, including equity.
  • Inclusive Healthcare Package.
  • Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills.
  • Flexible Time Off.
  • We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed.

About Level Zero
Level Zero is pioneering next-generation biosensor technology for precise, real-time monitoring of critical endocrine biomarkers. Recognised as one of the top 20 startups across all categories worldwide at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024 - and backed by top-tier organisations like SOSV and Entrepreneur First - we're pushing the boundaries of biochemistry and nanotechnology to revolutionize personalised health.
Founded by two seasoned engineers, we bring extensive experience in R&D, technical innovation, and commercial strategy to transform the way people monitor their health. Our mission is bold: to revolutionise health management by delivering clinical-grade data directly to individuals, wherever they are.
We're seeking driven innovators to join us in pushing the boundaries of biosensing and health tech, making personalised health monitoring a reality for everyone. To achieve this ambitious vision, we're assembling the best team in the world - dedicated to turning cutting-edge science into life-changing, real-world solutions.
About the role
We’re looking for a technician with hands-on experience running label-free biophysical instruments (SPR, GCI, BLI or ITC) to assist with characterising how receptors bind to hormone targets. You’ll focus on ligand kinetics screening, and your results will directly help us select and refine the receptors that go into our real-time, continuous biosensors.
Our targets are challenging small molecules that are hard to handle and tend to stick to surfaces, so careful experimental technique and attention to detail are central to the role. You’ll run established screening methods, troubleshoot day-to-day issues, and work closely with our scientists as methods continue to improve.

About the Role
We are excited to welcome a biosensor scientist with a strong background in electrochemical biosensor R&D and experience in working with aptamers to join our rapidly growing start-up. The ideal candidate is expected to be proficient in bench and wet chemistry techniques. Moreover, they should have sound knowledge and experience in assay development, small molecule detection, and electrode surface modifications. It is essential for the candidate to have extensive experience in aptamer-based electrochemical biosensor R&D, including the designs, operation principles, troubleshooting, and analysis.
This is a full-time, in-person role primarily based in London.
Some examples of what you might do:
- Design, prototype, and optimize electrochemical biosensor systems, focusing on small molecule analytes and aptamer-based recognition.
- Apply surface chemistry and electrode modification strategies to improve sensitivity, selectivity, stability, and biosensor performance in complex biological samples.
- Translate bio-element–target interactions into measurable and reproducible sensor outputs through novel assay design.
- Apply a range of electrochemical methods (voltammetry, impedimetry, chronoamperometry, etc.) to characterize and evaluate biosensor function.
- Apply data-driven approaches including Python-based analysis and Design of Experiments (DoE) to streamline workflows.
- Troubleshoot technical and conceptual challenges systematically and propose innovative solutions to improve performance.
- Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and ensure experimental reproducibility and compliance with quality standards.
- Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams (chemists, biologists, engineers, and data scientists) to advance biosensor prototypes from concept to application.
- Present results clearly through written reports, oral presentations, and scientific publications.
- Attend R&D-related trainings and seminars for continuous updates on the latest trend in hormone sensing technologies.

About the Role
As Director, Product Management, you'll own the strategy and execution for a core area of Matillion's product end to end. This is a hands-on leadership role: you'll carry direct product ownership for a significant area while building and leading a team of Product Managers - roughly 40% of your time in direct product work, the rest on team leadership, stakeholder management and portfolio oversight, and that balance will shift over time.
Success in this role means category-level command of the data landscape, sharp product instincts, and the ability to raise the bar in others, not just in your own output.
You'll partner closely with Engineering and Design leadership to align on technical strategy, and with GTM, Customer Success and Marketing to keep the business ahead of what's shipping and turn what you learn into what you build next.
What you will be doing
•
Own a product area end to end: define the strategy for your area, translate company and product strategy into a multi-quarter roadmap, and make the prioritisation and resourcing trade-offs across multiple workstreams - with accountability for the commercial outcome of the whole portfolio.
•
Stay hands-on: retain direct ownership of a specific product area - write specs, run discovery, and make product calls yourself, not just through your team.
•
Set and enforce the quality bar: define what “good” looks like for the product area, review your team's product decisions and outputs, and hold the line with senior stakeholders when a capability isn't ready to ship - even when it's commercially uncomfortable.
•
Understand the market and the users: maintain a view of user needs across data engineering, analytics and platform personas, and own the competitive and market view of the data and AI ecosystem.
•
Build and lead the team: hire, coach and manage the performance of a team of Product Managers, run the team's operating rhythm, and set the standard for AI-enabled ways of working across the group.
•
Drive cross-functional and executive alignment: partner with Engineering and Design leadership on technical strategy and delivery capacity, keep GTM, Customer Success and Marketing ahead of what's shipping, and present roadmap and trade-offs to stakeholders, leadership and customers.
What we are looking for
•
Typically 10+ years in product management, including 3+ years managing Product Managers directly.
•
A track record of shipping and scaling B2B products end to end, with demonstrable commercial impact.
•
People leadership experience: you've hired, coached and managed the performance of Product Managers directly.
•
Real, hands-on exposure to the data ecosystem - enough to make credible technical trade-off calls.
•
A systems thinker operating at scale, balancing craft, speed and commercial impact across multiple workstreams at once.
•
Deep data literacy, and the ability to hold your team accountable to evidence-based decision-making.
•
A demonstrable track record of using AI tools to accelerate product work, and the ability to model, teach and hold your team to that same standard.
•
Excellent communication, including credibility in front of executive leadership and senior customers.
•
Comfortable holding a line under commercial pressure - on product quality and on team standards - and operating at both strategic and hands-on altitude in the same week.

Are you ready to shape the future of data?
Matillion is the company behind Maia, the AI Data Automation platform.

This isn't BAU engineering – this is high-visibility, high-impact work where your decisions shape the product.
You'll be driving architecture, mentoring engineers, and feeding into strategy. Things move quickly here. Requirements evolve, new opportunities emerge, and we need someone who thrives in that environment. If you have been working on Agentic AI projects and taking them into production environments – and you want to do that at scale in a world-class engineering team – this is the role for you.

Position Summary:

Quotient is seeking a Director or Senior Director of Antibody Discovery. This role will define and lead Quotient’s antibody discovery strategy; leading the delivery of therapeutic antibody projects in addition to Quotient’s antibody drug discovery platform build through the deployment of cutting-edge technologies. This role will require close involvement in the end-to-end process of translating Somatic Genomics screening outputs (i.e. candidate genes and potential drug targets) into initiation of drug discovery programs. This role will also involve senior project leadership, steering drug discovery matrix teams from early conception through to key inflection points such as development candidate nomination and IND submission.

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide balanced expert advice on the feasibility of antibody tractable targets and the conception of high-value drug molecules
  • Present antibody discovery strategies to internal R&D committees to justify capital commitment in new programs
  • Drive decision making on construct design, format and developability for new antibody programs according to Target Product Profile specifications
  • Independently carry out lead sequence and format optimizations utilizing rational, structure-based and in silico/AI/ML design approaches
  • Drive rapid optimization of novel antibody and protein therapeutics through iterative design, build, test, and learn cycles
  • As a drug discovery project leader, develop efficient and balanced project plans for one or more biologic drug discovery programs and lead a cross-functional team to execute through lead generation, development candidate nomination and IND submission
  • Model best matrix leadership behaviours and support an emphasis on enterprise leadership across the company
  • Identify, select, and manage external CROs/vendors, consultants, and academic collaborators to deliver a virtual/outsourced state-of-the-art drug antibody discovery platform for the identification of high-quality mAb molecules at pace
  • Build and maintain networks of external experts to pressure-test hypotheses and refine strategies
  • Serve as a specialist antibody discovery expert within Quotient’s drug discovery team and across the company.
  • Contribute to broader corporate strategy, BD evaluations, and exploratory platform initiatives

Qualifications:

Essential

  • Proven experience advancing protein therapeutics through drug discovery phases to development.
  • Expertise in structure-based protein engineering and design of antibodies including (multispecifics, Fc engineering, fusion proteins etc)
  • Skilled in antibody engineering, including use of in silico, structure-based, and AI/ML approaches to sequence/CDR design, use of display technologies, humanization techniques, sequence liability remediation, analytics, and developability (biophysical) assessment and improvement
  • Project leadership experience in pharmaceutical industry R&D environment across multiple therapeutic areas, with a deep understanding of lead identification and optimization through preclinical development of antibody therapeutics
  • Track record of advocating for acquisition or creation of new technologies for accelerated antibody design, expression, and characterization

Desirable

  • Experience in early-stage or start-up biotech environments
  • Experience working with genetic and genomics platform-driven drug target discovery
  • Broader understanding of protein sciences (expression, developability, and analytical purification and analysis)
  • Experience managing the design and validation of cellular assays for the functional characterization of engineered biologics

Values and Behaviors:

  • Encourage respectful disagreement and cultivate open-minded, ego-free interactions to continuously push each other towards excellence
  • Seek out diverse perspectives; practice active listening and genuine curiosity to ensure all contributions are valued, regardless of source
  • Recognize the impact of your behavior, language and attitudes, and strive for balanced, meaningful exchanges that enhance mutual growth and understanding in all interactions
  • Use a company-first mindset to guide decision-making; prioritize team over individual success
  • Take calculated risks and challenge convention in the quest for exceptional outcomes

Position Summary:

This role will partner closely with Quotient’s drug development project leaders and matrix teams to translate their scientific strategy into robust, integrated drug development project plans, and drive flawless execution of Quotient’s early drug pipeline. This role is accountable for planning, execution, and coordination across functional teams (e.g., drug discovery, translational medicine, biology, drug development strategy, and finance) as well as external CROs and collaborators. The successful candidate will coordinate and run drug development matrix project meetings, maintain governance-ready dashboards and decision logs, oversee budgets, contracts, and resource needs, and readiness for key drug development review milestones. By leveraging subject matter experts across key Research and Development functions to develop end-to-end drug development plans and execution strategies, this role will provide operational and planning leadership to drug development matrix teams, manage risks and interdependencies, consider regulatory and compliance requirements, and support reviews for Quotient’s Executive team and Board of Directors.

This role will also support the development of Quotient’s drug discovery pipeline strategy with scenario-based analyses based on landscape and competitive intelligence data. Given the close integration of Quotient’s proprietary genetics platform into the drug discovery process, this role will interface with research operations and strategy to build a seamless, end-to-end view of Quotient’s R&D pipeline.

This role will report to the Chief Development Officer (CDO). The role could be based at Quotient’s UK or US site.

Responsibilities: 

  • With drug development matrix teams, support the translation of overarching drug development strategy and vision into integrated, detailed project plans (scope, milestones, critical paths, dependencies, risks) across functions.
  • Monitor progress versus plan; proactively identify issues and interdependencies, escalate to project leads as needed, and coordinate cross-functional mitigation plans
  • Schedule, structure, and run project team meetings (set agendas, pre-reads, minutes, action logs), track and drive closure of decisions and actions.
  • Build and maintain governance-ready views (dashboards, status summaries, decision logs) to enable Quotient’s Executive team and Board of Directors reviews
  • Support SMEs in operational execution with external partners (e.g., CROs), ensuring deliverables, timelines, and obligations are clearly understood and met.
  • Support functional heads in forecasting and tracking resource needs (FTE, external partners) across projects and the pipeline, flag constraints and propose options.
  • Coordinate budgets closely with the VP of Finance and track spend vs. plan and contracted scopes.
  • Establish and maintain a structured risk and issue management process (identification, impact assessment, mitigation/contingency, owners, timelines).
  • Support compliance with regulatory and quality expectations by organizing documentation and tracking contributions to regulatory submissions etc.
  • Maintain shared repositories (SharePoint, dashboards, trackers) for plans, data summaries, and decision histories to improve transparency and continuity.
  • Identify and implement continuous operational improvements to increase DD matrix team efficiency and focus on high-value scientific work.
  • Support the development of Quotient’s drug discovery pipeline strategy and, with members of Research Operations and Strategy, develop a holistic and end-to-end view of Quotient’s Research and Development pipeline.

  • Proven track record of applying project management methodologies in complex, matrixed environments; significant experience (typically 5–10 years) in drug development within pharmaceutical, or biotech industry settings
  • Knowledge and experience in drug discovery and an understanding of the principles of clinical development, drug discovery, regulatory strategy
  • Established expertise and hands-on experience with project management tools (e.g. Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent), Microsoft Office applications, and a working understanding of innovative AI and knowledge management technologies (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, CoPilot, Notion etc)

Position Summary:

Quotient is seeking an experienced Scientific Manager to lead the day-to-day execution and delivery of our High Throughput Laboratory.

Reporting to the Head of High Throughput Laboratory, this role is responsible for coordinating laboratory activities across Histology, Flow Cytometry, Molecular Biology and Sample Management, ensuring samples move efficiently through laboratory workflows and disease programmes are delivered safely, on time and to the highest scientific standards.

Working closely with Research Project Management, Scientific Leadership, Genomic Scientists, the High Throughput Laboratory and Assay Development teams, you will translate project priorities into effective laboratory execution, balancing competing demands across multiple programmes while maintaining visibility of sample progression, laboratory capacity and resource utilisation.

This is a highly visible operational leadership role suited to someone who enjoys bringing structure to complex laboratory environments, developing high-performing teams and ensuring laboratory operations run efficiently. You will combine scientific credibility with excellent organisational skills and a passion for coaching others, creating an environment where individuals thrive and operational improvements are successfully embedded into routine laboratory practice.

Success in this role will be measured by your ability to deliver high-quality scientific data whilst maintaining efficient laboratory throughput, developing an engaged and capable team, and ensuring projects progress smoothly through the High Throughput Laboratory.

Key Responsibilities

Laboratory Delivery

  • Coordinate day-to-day laboratory execution across multiple disease programmes, ensuring samples progress efficiently through Histology, Flow Cytometry, Molecular Biology and Scientific Sample Management workflows.
  • Translate project priorities into detailed laboratory work plans and schedules ensuring resources, equipment and personnel are effectively allocated to deliver programme milestones.
  • Partner closely with Disease Project teams, the Head of High Throughput Laboratory, scientific manager peers and Research Project Management to prioritise work, manage competing demands and resolve operational bottlenecks.
  • Monitor laboratory throughput, turnaround times, sample progression and resource utilisation, proactively identifying risks to delivery and implementing corrective actions.
  • Maintain clear visibility of sample status throughout the laboratory workflow, ensuring timely communication of progress, risks and delays to project teams.

People Leadership

  • Line manage and develop direct reports through coaching, regular feedback and performance management.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous learning within the laboratory team.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, training and competency assessment of laboratory staff.
  • Ensure appropriate laboratory cover and resource planning to support changing portfolio demands.

Scientific Delivery

  • Remain scientifically hands-on where required, supporting laboratory activities and troubleshooting technical issues to maintain programme delivery.
  • Provide technical oversight across Histology, Flow Cytometry and Molecular Biology workflows, ensuring high standards of scientific quality and reproducibility.
  • Support implementation and operational adoption of new laboratory processes, technologies and workflow improvements in partnership with Assay Development and Automation.
  • Work closely with scientific leaders to understand future project requirements and ensure laboratory readiness to support programme delivery.

Laboratory workflows supported by the team include:

  • Histology: Tissue fixation, embedding, sectioning, histochemistry (H&E, IHC) and slide preparation.
  • Flow Cytometry: Tissue dissociation, FACS/FANS, cell and nuclei counting, immunostaining and sample preparation.
  • Molecular Biology: DNA/RNA extraction, nucleic acid quality assessment, library preparation and sequencing submissions.

Laboratory Operations & Compliance

  • Ensure laboratory activities comply with HTA requirements, COSHH regulations, quality systems and internal laboratory procedures.
  • Maintain accurate sample tracking and laboratory records using ELN/LIMS systems, ensuring traceability throughout the sample lifecycle.
  • Monitor laboratory KPIs, including throughput, turnaround time, quality and resource utilisation, using data to drive continuous improvement.
  • Build strong working relationships across Research, Project Management, Discovery Partnerships and supporting operational functions.

Qualifications

You are an experienced laboratory scientist with a passion for leading people and coordinating complex laboratory operations. You enjoy balancing multiple priorities, developing others and ensuring high-quality science is delivered efficiently within a collaborative matrix environment.

Essential

  • Bachelor's degree with significant relevant industry experience (typically 6+ years). MSc or PhD considered in combination with appropriate hands-on laboratory leadership experience.
  • Experience working within high-throughput laboratory environments and/or rapidly scaling biotechnology organisations, with the flexibility to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining high standards of scientific quality and operational delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating laboratory workflows across multiple concurrent scientific projects.
  • Experience line managing or mentoring laboratory users.
  • Hands-on expertise in a range of skills across Histology, Flow Cytometry and/or Molecular Biology.
  • Familiarity with ELN and/or LIMS systems for laboratory documentation and sample tracking.
  • Broad understanding of tissue and cell biology, genomics and molecular biology workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate competing priorities whilst maintaining scientific quality and delivery timelines.
  • Strong organisational, communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to scientific quality, safety and compliance.

Position Summary:

Quotient is seeking a highly analytical and scientifically curious Senior Analyst to support strategic decision-making across our growing drug development pipeline. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of analytics, market intelligence, commercial strategy and early drug development in a genetics-based biotech company. 

The successful candidate will combine strong analytical skills and familiarity with scientific and clinical data with commercial curiosity, to turn networks of complex data into meaningful insights. In doing so, the successful candidate will help us better understand where high-value, tractable drug development opportunities exist across our internal pipeline of drug targets, and more broadly across a range of disease areas. Together with other members of the drug development team, this role will help focus which indications, patient segments, and development paths we should consider, and where data can help inform our investment and planning decisions.

This role could be based in our UK or US office and will report to the Chief Development Officer.

Responsibilities: 

  • Across a range of disease/therapeutic areas, build a deep understanding of addressable markets, industry landscape, customer (health care practitioner, payor, and patient) needs, and forecast future states and opportunities for growth in sectors of interest
  • Carry out market sizing, competitive analysis using epidemiology, clinical, and commercial data sets, and validate through research with external experts
  • Partner with clinical, drug development and external experts/customers to further validate specific market segments and develop target product profiles (TPPs)
  • Partner with Finance, Business development, and Drug Development teams to develop asset and disease area valuation models (e.g., rNPV) and support BD and finance discussions with valuation and commercial forecast models as required
  • Design and improve data models, analytical frameworks, and output formats, that support assessments, presentation to stakeholders and internal decision-making
  • Develop dashboards, reporting, and analysis tools to communicate outputs and disease area strategy. Develop and maintain revenue forecasts, pipeline models, and scenario analyses.  
  • Prototype, test, and help deploy AI-enabled tools, agents, and other analytical resources to support all the above analyses; working with end users and internal teams to refine successful solutions
  • Provide insights to drug development, project management, and finance teams to support target-setting and internal development planning.  

Qualifications:

Essential

  • Bachelor's degree in health sciences discipline or a related field
  • 3+ years of experience working in or with pharmaceutical or biotech companies (including via consulting firms) in product planning or commercial strategy teams
  • Experience in at least one of these disease segments: Cardiovascular, renal, metabolic, oncology, autoimmune diseases
  • Familiarity with drug development strategy and regulatory pathways
  • Experience with a range of healthcare or life-sciences databases and market research tools
  • Exposure to valuation, business development, licensing, or investment analysis
  • Strong analytical and research skills
  • Familiarity with and ability to synthesize scientific, medical, and economic data
  • Strong business acumen and problem-solving capabilities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work independently yet collaboratively, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines

Desirable

  • 4-6+ years of industry experience
  • Knowledge of genomic-based approaches to drug target discovery

Reporting to the CFO, this individual will play a critical role in shaping the company's portfolio and business strategy, identifying external opportunities, and executing partnerships that create significant value for the company and its stakeholders.

The ideal candidate combines strong scientific and commercial judgment with demonstrated transaction leadership and the ability to operate effectively in an early-stage, fast-paced, resource-constrained environment. This person will be equally comfortable evaluating an external asset, developing a market landscape, engaging with potential partners, and working cross-functionally with R&D, clinical, regulatory, and executive leadership.

We are looking for someone with a proven track record in Business Development within the biotech or pharmaceutical sectors with significant experience leading collaboration and in-licensing deals and demonstrated strategic thinking and relationship building experience.  On a personal level, Quotients enjoy a fast-paced environment, think like entrepreneurs, are adaptable, accountable, work proactively and look out for each other.

Position Summary:

Quotient is seeking a Senior Engineer in our Data Infrastructure team to design and evolve our cloud, data and AI infrastructure underpinning our genomics-first drug discovery platform.

Working within the Data Infrastructure team, you will lead complex initiatives spanning AWS platform engineering, scientific data systems and AI/ML workloads. You will collaborate closely with cloud engineers, data engineers, bioinformaticians, AI scientists, computational biologists, and experimental scientists to turn evolving scientific needs into secure, reliable and scalable engineering solutions.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with substantial technical autonomy. You will make cross-system architecture and operational trade-offs, establish reusable engineering patterns, and mentor our Cloud Engineers and Data Engineers through design reviews, delivery and troubleshooting. The role does not require formal line management, but it does require clear technical leadership and accountability for platform outcomes.

This hybrid role is based at the Chesterford Research Campus, near Cambridge, and reports to the Head of Data Infrastructure. The successful candidate will normally work from the campus at least three days per week, participate in operational support and incident escalation, and must have permission to work in the UK.

Responsibilities: 

  • Lead the architecture and evolution of our AWS-based infrastructure across cloud services, scientific data platforms and AI/ML workloads, balancing delivery speed, reliability, security and cost.
  • Design and implement reusable infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and environment-management patterns that make production systems easier to build, test, deploy and operate.
  • Own cross-cutting engineering decisions for observability, identity and access management, networking, resilience, capacity, data movement and lifecycle management.
  • Partner with Cloud Engineers and Data Engineers to deliver integrated solutions, providing practical mentoring through technical design, code review, incident response and operational improvement.
  • Work with AI scientists, computational biologists and scientific teams to translate model development, training, evaluation, inference and data requirements into secure, reproducible platform capabilities.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex failures spanning infrastructure, data pipelines, applications and AI workloads; lead incident reviews and ensure corrective actions improve the wider system.
  • Establish and reinforce engineering standards for testing, documentation, release management, operational readiness, security and cost visibility across the Data Infrastructure team.
  • Evaluate new technologies and shape the infrastructure roadmap with the Head of Data Infrastructure, making pragmatic build-versus-buy and sequencing decisions for an early-stage biotech.

Qualifications:

Essential

  • Substantial experience designing, building and operating production cloud or data infrastructure, typically gained through seven or more years of relevant work or equivalent demonstrated capability.
  • Advanced hands-on experience with AWS and ownership of multiple interdependent production systems, including the ability to troubleshoot failures across service boundaries.
  • Strong experience with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, containerised workloads, cloud networking, identity and access management, and production observability.
  • Strong software engineering skills in Python and Linux, including automated testing, version control, code review and maintainable automation or platform tooling.
  • Experience supporting data-intensive life-science systems or workflows, with enough domain understanding to reason about large scientific datasets, reproducibility, provenance and scientific user needs.
  • Experience enabling AI/ML workloads in cloud environments, such as data preparation, model training, evaluation, inference, orchestration or production deployment.
  • A track record of leading complex technical initiatives under ambiguity, making explicit trade-offs and remaining accountable for reliable operational outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and communicate architecture, risk and delivery choices clearly to both technical and scientific stakeholders.

Desirable Experience

  • Genomics, digital pathology, structural biology or other high-volume scientific data modalities and formats.

About Quotient Therapeutics
Quotient Therapeutics is a Flagship Pioneering company that uses somatic genomics to discover drug targets. We use high-accuracy sequencing to find rare somatic mutations in cells from non-cancerous diseased human tissue. Mutations that help cells survive or expand in a disease environment point to causal biology. We use that evidence to nominate and assess targets, and to decide whether a target should be copied (protective mutations) or opposed (disease-driving mutations).

The Role
Quotient is seeking a (Senior) Scientist, Machine Learning to build models and AI agents that turn our somatic mutation data into evidence for target discovery. A central question is what a given mutation does to a protein, and whether that effect explains why cells carrying it are selected in disease. You will build models of variant effects on protein function and connect them to genomic, single-cell, perturbation and phenotype data. You will also develop agentic AI workflows that help scientists analyse data, test hypotheses and make decisions.

This is a hands-on role on a cross-functional team. You will write clear, tested code, use modern AI tools to work faster, and work closely with the computational scientists, experimental biologists, engineers and target discovery leads who act on your results. - A curiosity about sequencing technology and genuine interest in learning and growing within a fast-moving team

Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.
High Growth: We truly believe in investing in our people. We make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice-yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace, and we ensure reward increases with impact.
Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions - so strong that most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike-to-work scheme, life insurance, and more.
We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/adaptyv/b3342c86-3661-4.description_excerpt:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.
We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.
We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.
Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.
We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You work with customers to help them design better proteins and get more out of every experiment, sitting between their design models and our lab.
In London, a large share of that work is with ARIA. Adaptyv has been selected for ARIA's https://aria.org.uk/activation-partners second cohort of Activation Partners, and ARIA, the UK's Advanced Research + Invention Agency, is funding our new automated lab in London: the UK's first AI-native automated wet lab.
ARIA backs ambitious research programmes across areas such as engineering human immunity, protein-based materials and synthetic plants. The teams it funds, called Creators, often need experimental capabilities that do not yet exist. You'll work directly with those teams to define what needs to be built, develop the assays, and bring them onto our automation platform.
Our goal is to help the next 100 UK biotechs and neopharmas get started by the end of 2028.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Lead scientific projects with customers. Translate biological questions into clear protein design and experimental strategies, including targets, success criteria, constructs, controls and assays.
- Guide protein design strategy. Help teams choose the right approaches for the problem, from de novo and diffusion-based design to protein language models, structure prediction and physics-based methods.
- Turn data into decisions. Analyse binding, expression, stability and other assay data with customers and determine what the next round of designs should test.
- Develop new experimental capabilities. When an ARIA programme needs an assay that does not yet exist, work with the Creator team and our scientists to develop it, validate it and bring it onto the automation platform.
- Shape future ARIA programmes. Work with ARIA Programme Directors to understand the experimental capabilities upcoming Creator cohorts are likely to need and help us prepare for them.
- Build long-term scientific partnerships. Become a trusted scientific counterpart to the teams you work with, and bring what you learn back into our product, science and platform roadmap.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- Strong protein science foundation. A degree and/or hands-on experience in protein design, computational biology, biochemistry, structural biology or a related field.
- Biophysical characterisation experience. Deep hands-on experience with SPR, BLI, nanoDSF or related methods is required.
- Fluency in modern protein design. You understand the major approaches used in the field, their strengths and limitations, and how to apply them to real design problems.
- Strong quantitative instincts. Comfortable working with Python, notebooks and basic statistics to analyse noisy experimental data and reach clear conclusions.
- Excellent scientific communication. Able to work closely with researchers, understand what they are trying to achieve and explain trade-offs clearly.
- Comfort with ambiguity. You can take an underspecified scientific problem, form hypotheses, design the right experiments and iterate when things do not work.
- High ownership. You take responsibility for scientific outcomes rather than simply handing work from one team to another.
- Experience in assay development, lab automation or working with external scientific partners is a plus.
DETAILS
- Location: London, UK (on-site), with travel to customers and ARIA Creator sites, and regular time at our Lausanne lab.
- Type: Full time
- Start date: ASAP. Our London lab comes online in 2027.
Application deadline
We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.
The day-to-day:
- Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

- Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results
- Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected
- Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

Responsibilities
- Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.
- Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).
- Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.
- Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.
- Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.
- Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.
- Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.
- Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

- Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.
- Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.
- Commercially driven. You care about revenue, pipeline, and closing deals, not just having interesting scientific conversations.
- Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.
- Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.
- Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

This is a general manager role in the literal sense: if something needs to happen for Adaptyv UK to succeed, it is ultimately your responsibility.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Build the London lab. Take the site from lease to an operational lab: fit-out, contractors, equipment, suppliers, permits, timelines, and budget. You will work closely with the Head of Lab Operations you help hire, but you own getting the site open.
- Build the founding UK team. Hire across lab operations, automation, and science together with the founders. Put the basic people infrastructure in place and create a team that can operate with the same speed and ownership as Lausanne.
- Set up and run Adaptyv UK. Own the UK entity, banking, accounting, payroll, insurance, budgeting, contracts, and the other operational machinery required to run the company properly.
- Own the local customer experience. Work with UK customers from onboarding through experiment delivery, coordinating closely with our commercial and scientific teams in Lausanne.
- Build the local network. Develop relationships with landlords, contractors, vendors, universities, biotechs, partners, and the broader London life-science ecosystem.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- You have built something from zero before. Ideally you have launched a new site, geography, business unit, or physical operation for a fast-growing company. Experience with labs, clinics, manufacturing, hardware, or other infrastructure-heavy businesses is particularly relevant.
- You are an exceptional generalist. You can move comfortably between property, finance, legal, hiring, customers, and operations. You do not need to be the expert in every room, but you learn quickly, ask the right questions, and know when specialist input matters.
- You get things over the line. You negotiate well, make decisions, follow up, and keep complex projects moving.
- You operate with a high degree of ownership. You do not need a predefined process or someone telling you what comes next. You figure out what needs to happen and make it happen.
- You have a strong life-sciences background. A degree and/or professional experience in the life sciences is highly preferred. You will be building a lab, hiring scientists, working with biotech customers, and negotiating with lab landlords and instrument vendors, so familiarity with the industry matters.
- You use AI as part of how you work. We use tools like Claude Code and our own software throughout Adaptyv, including in operations. We expect you to be comfortable using AI to move faster and do better work.
- You are in London. This is a hands-on, on-site role. You are already based there or ready to move.

- Type: Full-time
- Start: As soon as possible
- Target lab opening: 2026

You will own the operational build-out of the lab: fit-out, instrument installation, infrastructure, supply chain, maintenance, safety, compliance, and the lab operations team. The Lausanne team has already built and runs this setup today, so you will have proven systems and playbooks to work from. Once the lab is live, you will run day-to-day lab operations and continuously improve its reliability, capacity, and throughput.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Lead the lab fit-out. Own the operational side of taking the space from shell to working laboratory, including benching, ventilation, power, cold storage, extraction, safety systems, contractors, timelines, and readiness.
- Install and commission the instrument fleet. Coordinate delivery, installation, qualification, and handover of equipment including array-SPR, BLI, and liquid handlers, working closely with vendors and our automation team in Lausanne.
- Build the lab operating infrastructure. Put in place inventory and procurement, shipping and cold chain, maintenance schedules, service contracts, chemical handling, waste management, and the other systems required to keep a high-throughput lab running reliably.
- Own lab safety and compliance. Establish the processes, documentation, risk assessments, notifications, and permits required to operate the London site safely and compliantly.
- Build the lab operations team. Hire and manage the people responsible for keeping the facility, equipment, logistics, and day-to-day laboratory operations running smoothly.
- Run the lab. Once production starts, own the operational performance of the site: uptime, throughput, inventory, maintenance, safety, and continuous improvement.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- You have built or expanded a laboratory before. You have led a fit-out, site move, major equipment installation, or new laboratory launch. Experience running an established lab is valuable, but we are specifically looking for someone who has helped build one.
- You have deep hands-on lab operations experience. Ideally in a high-throughput, automation-heavy biotech, life-science, or similarly technical environment.
- You have a strong life-sciences background. A degree and/or significant professional experience in biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field is highly preferred. You understand the scientific workflows the lab supports and why details such as contamination control, cold chain, calibration, and equipment reliability matter.
- You understand laboratory safety and compliance. You have owned the safety, permitting, and compliance side of a working lab before, and you can get a new UK site compliant from day one — or learn the local requirements fast.
- You are strong with vendors and contractors. You are comfortable managing instrument manufacturers, service engineers, contractors, suppliers, and logistics providers, and keeping complex installation and operational work on track.
- You are highly operational. You build systems, spot problems early, keep track of details, and make sure the lab continues to function as complexity and throughput increase.
- You are comfortable working at startup pace. Priorities move quickly, the team is small, and there will not always be a predefined process for every problem.
- You use AI as part of how you work. We use tools like Claude Code and our own software throughout Adaptyv, including in lab operations. We expect you to be comfortable using AI to move faster and improve how work gets done.
- You are in London. This is an on-site role. You are already based there or ready to move.

- Type: Full-time
- Start: As soon as possible
- Target lab opening: 2026

Human progress runs on a single trade: risk for opportunity. Every venture worth doing - a new business, a new home, an exciting trip - means accepting the chance it goes wrong. - Handle claims end to end: from first notification of loss through to settlement
