- You are comfortable being both strategic and hands-on. You can lead an executive business review in the morning, rethink an onboarding…

jobs.ashbyhq.com/dust/9adcb2e4-ab6e-451e.description_excerpt:
ABOUT DUST
Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.
With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.
With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.
We're serving great customers https://dust.tt/customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.
Dust is backed by Sequoia https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/27/dust-grabs-another-16-million-for-its-enterprise-ai-assistants-connected-to-internal-data/ with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dust-tt_were-honored-to-be-recognized-on-the-generalists-activity-7359284343929741313-Rq04.
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
We are about to hire the people who will define the next phase of this company. Not backfill a plan someone else wrote — define it. The quality of who joins Dust over the next eighteen months is the single highest-leverage variable in whether we build the category or watch someone else do it.
That work needs a recruiter who treats hiring as a craft rather than a queue. Someone who can hold a real point of view on what "great" looks like for a role, defend it with a hiring manager who disagrees, and then go find that person themselves — from a cold start, without a lead gen team, a sourcing pod, or a playbook waiting for them.
You'll be an early member of a small Talent team. That means you own roles end to end, and you also help build the thing itself: the assessment design, the interview loops, the calibration, the data we use to know whether any of it is working.
We're looking for someone who cares about the candidate experience for all parties internal and external. And prioritizes protecting Dust's culture by being thoughtful, thorough and leading by example in being a true team player.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Full-cycle hiring, end to end. You run your own searches from role kickoff to close. Sourcing, outreach, screening, interviewing, offer strategy, negotiation. You are the owner of the outcome, not a coordinator of other people's opinions.
Assessment design, not just assessment delivery. For every role you open, you help define what evidence would actually predict success — then you build the loop that surfaces it. You'll push back on interview stages that exist out of habit and replace them with ones that test something real.
Hiring manager partnership with a spine. You'll spend as much time calibrating hiring managers as you do talking to candidates. When a manager says "not quite the right feel," you'll ask what they mean until there's a defensible answer, and you'll say so when there isn't one.
Market intelligence. You'll know your talent market better than anyone else in the building — who's good, where they are, what moves them, what compensation actually looks like right now — and you'll bring that back into how we scope roles and design offers.
The candidate experience. Our hiring process is the first honest sample of what working here feels like. You'll make it expedient, direct, well-communicated, and worth a candidate's time whether or not they get an offer.
Building the function. Process, tooling, structured scorecards, funnel data, quality-of-hire signal. You'll leave the system better than you found it, and you'll be trusted to change it without asking permission first.
TWO TRACKS — TELL US WHICH ONE IS YOURS
We're hiring for depth in one of two areas. You should have a genuine centre of gravity in one; interest in the other is a bonus, not a requirement.
GTM. Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Marketing, and the leaders above them, across Europe and the US. You know how to assess commercial talent on evidence rather than swagger, and you can tell the difference between a rep who carried a territory and a rep who inherited one.
Technical. Software engineers, infrastructure, product, and design, in a market where the best people are not looking and the second-best are drowning in outreach. You can hold a credible conversation about what someone actually built, and you know why that matters more than where they built it.
HOW WE THINK ABOUT HIRING
We're telling you this up front because if you disagree with it, this will be a frustrating job.
- We don't hire based on pedigree. Logos and school names are weak evidence. What someone has actually done, and what they can demonstrate now, is strong evidence. We design our loops accordingly.
- We hire for evidence, not affinity. "Culture fit" that means "reminds me of me" is how companies get homogeneous and slow. We assess against explicit behaviours tied to how we work, and we write down what we saw.
- Speed and rigour are not in tension. Slow processes are usually a symptom of unclear thinking about the role, not of high standards.
- A no should be as clear as a yes. To the candidate, and internally.
- Some of us came from well-known companies. That's context, not criteria. It isn't why we're here and it won't be why you are. We celebrate everyone's achievements and want to create an environment where diversity of thought and experience of a collective whole makes this place exceptional and lasting.
- Recruiters are operators, not order-takers. If you think a role is wrongly scoped, badly levelled, or shouldn't be open at all, you're expected to say so.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 5+ years in full-cycle recruiting, with meaningful time in-house at a high-growth company. You've hired in an environment with real ambiguity, not just real volume.
- Demonstrable depth in either GTM or technical hiring — you can talk through searches you've run, what made them hard, and what you'd do differently.
- Genuinely strong sourcing. Not "I partner with a sourcing team." You find people yourself, and you write outreach that people reply to because it's obviously written by a human who read something.
- Comfort operating without infrastructure. No playbook, no SDR equivalent, limited tooling to start.
- The judgement and directness to challenge senior stakeholders, and the credibility to be listened to when you do.

Forward Deployed Engineer
About the role
FDEs are how Duvo brings AI to life inside our customers. You sit at the front line, map their workflows on the Duvo platform, improve the underlying processes, and turn the result into running agents that deliver tangible business impact. Scoping, build, debug, handover, expansion. You own the customer outcome end to end and you own the relationship that goes with it.
You won't write the core product. You will write the glue: integration scripts, agent configurations, data transformations, prototypes, whatever it takes to get an agent running against a customer's actual systems. You'll spend real time inside their stack and inside their team.
If you like the messy middle between AI, process, and customer, this is the role.
You will be deployed directly with our clients, mostly in onsite/hybrid mode of work, you will travel a lot.
Location. This role is UK-based. You'll need to be living in the UK, or relocating there before you start, and able to travel to client sites from there.
What you'll do
- Embed with customers from kickoff through go-live and beyond
- Map customer workflows directly on the Duvo platform and decide what's worth automating, what's worth fixing first, and what's blocked
- Improve the underlying processes where it matters. Don't automate broken flows, redesign them
- Translate business logic into agent behavior: actions, decision rules, exception paths, fallbacks
- Configure and ship agents against real customer systems (ERPs, portals, spreadsheets, email, custom tools)
- Write integration code, scripts, and prototypes when the situation calls for it
- Debug live agents in production environments and iterate quickly
- Build and own the working relationship with customer stakeholders, from operators to sponsors
- Run working sessions, hold your own with technical counterparts, and earn the right to push back
- Make AI real for the customer. Move them from pilot energy to measurable business outcomes
- Capture reusable patterns, templates, and runbooks so the next deployment is faster
- Send recurring workflow patterns back to Product and Engineering as real signal
What success looks like
- Multiple agents in production across clients, with measurable business impact
- Customers point to specific KPIs that moved because of your work
- Customers treat you as a trusted operator and want you in the room
- Process improvements you drove are visible in the customer's day-to-day, not just in the agent
- Transformation Managers want you on their hardest accounts
- Accounts you own expand because the relationship and the results are both there
- Each deployment is faster than the last because you've left behind reusable assets
Who you are
Experience
5+ years in roles where you've shipped against real customer environments. We're prioritizing AI-native candidates: people who have been building, deploying, or operating AI and agentic systems in customer-facing settings, not adjacent to them.
Likely backgrounds:
- Forward-deployed engineering or solutions engineering at an AI-first company
- Applied AI / ML engineering with direct customer exposure
- Technical consulting on AI or automation projects where you owned delivery and the client relationship
- Operations or product roles where you've built and shipped AI-powered tooling against messy real-world systems
Retail, e-commerce, or CPG background is a strong plus. Fluency in any operational domain (supply chain, procurement, category management, merchandising, finance ops, supplier management, warehousing) helps you ramp faster on customer accounts. What matters most is that you can pick up a new business quickly, see how to improve it, and build something with AI that actually works.
Skills
- Hands-on with modern AI tooling: LLMs, agent frameworks, prompt engineering, evals, MCP, retrieval
- Strong systems thinking and engineering judgment
- Process design instinct. You can spot waste, redundancy, and bad handoffs and propose something better
- Comfortable in code-adjacent territory: SQL, Python or JS scripting, APIs, JSON, webhooks, light data work
- Familiarity with ERPs and enterprise stacks is a plus
- Able to lead a working session, manage a stakeholder, push back on bad scope, and explain trade-offs without hiding behind jargon
- Fluent English. Additional European languages are a plus
Mindset
- Bias to ship
- Comfortable with ambiguity, half-built systems, and changing requirements
- Low ego, high standards
- Customer-obsessed. You build trust by being useful, not by being polished
- Commercially aware and able to help customers believe in what you're building
- Honest about what's working and what isn't
What we offer
- A small, sharp team that values ownership and candor
- Real product and culture leverage from day one
- Customer-facing impact: your work ships and moves the business
- Competitive comp including equity
- Option to trade cash for equity
HOW WE HIRE
We respect your time and aim to move fast:
1. Screening call.
2. Hiring Manager call (online, 30 min). We'll talk about you, how you think and whether there's mutual fit.
3. Case study ( ~4 hours). Ship something small to production with us and see how we work together. Fully compensated
4. Final interview (online, 30min)
We're not looking for perfection. We're looking for someone who can walk into a customer's operation, figure out what matters, fix the process, ship the agent, and turn AI into outcomes the business can feel.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Duvo helps large enterprises actually finish the operational work that nobody on their team has time to close. The stuff that lives across an ERP, a few portals, somebody's inbox, three spreadsheets, and the occasional phone call. We map it, improve it, and run it for them.
Our customers include one of Europe's largest online grocery retailers, a global beauty e-commerce brand, a Middle East retail group, and a European pharmacy chain. The buyer is usually a Head of Operations, Supply Chain, Finance or IT at a large retailer or FMCG brand. New deals land at €100k–€250k ARR and grow from there.
Duvo's partner ecosystem is live: consultancies signed and engaged, MBB firms inbound, hyperscalers co-selling. We're hiring a Partner Manager to turn those relationships into pipeline and revenue — to own the day-to-day with our partners and make sure they actually sell Duvo.
You'll report to the Founding Head of Partnerships & Ecosystem.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own the day-to-day with signed partners. Consultancies, SIs, tech platforms. Run the account mapping sessions, identify joint target accounts, qualify opportunities, and track pipeline through HubSpot. Clean data, accurate attribution, weekly reporting — none of it glamorous, all of it yours.
Coordinate joint selling. Run the handoff with Duvo sales on partner-sourced deals, support the deals in flight, and join the partner-led pitches that matter. Monitor partner health — engagement, pipeline contribution, satisfaction — and flag risk before it shows up as a missed quarter.
Onboard and enable. From signed agreement to first joint opportunity in under 30 days. Build the enablement materials with Sales Enablement (playbooks, positioning, demo access, objection handling), run training sessions, and make sure each partner can sell Duvo without needing us in the room.
Run the operational engine. Deal registration and rules of engagement. Technical resource allocation with Sales and Pre-sales. Partner QBRs. The KPIs — partner-sourced ARR, partner-influenced ARR, activation rate, pipeline velocity — are yours to report and yours to move.
Scale the channel. Support the growing network of regional partnership reps, lay the foundation for partner certification and tiered programs as the ecosystem matures, and contribute to partner marketing: joint events, webinars, case studies, co-branded content.
WHO YOU ARE
3–5 years in partner management, channel sales, alliance management, or business development at a B2B SaaS or tech company. You've worked with consulting firms, SIs, or tech partners and you know how they evaluate and sell technology.
Operationally sharp. CRM hygiene, pipeline tracking, reporting, process documentation — second nature, not what you reach for in week three of the quarter.
A relationship builder who can hold 10+ partner relationships in parallel without anything dropping.
Comfortable working autonomously and quickly. This is a build, not a maintain. You're joining at the moment the function tips from founder-led to function-led.
Fluent English. Additional European languages are a plus.
NICE TO HAVE
Experience in Retail, FMCG, or CPG verticals, or in enterprise automation.
Time at a Big4, SI, or consulting firm — you've sat on the partner side of the relationship and you know what they actually need from us.
WHAT WE OFFER

jobs.ashbyhq.com/duvo/4774da6e-473c-423b.description_excerpt:
ABOUT DUVO
Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together.
Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result.
Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail.
We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome.
THE ROLE
As a Transformation Strategist, you will own the day-to-day momentum of an enterprise transformation.
You will partner with a Senior Transformation Strategist and Forward Deployed Engineers on a small number of live enterprise accounts. You will be the person who is consistently present with the customer: close to how work happens, accountable for the workstream cadence and able to turn a senior steer into analysis, decisions, materials and change that move the work forward.
The Senior Transformation Strategist owns the executive relationship, overall transformation direction and commercial outcome. You own the operating rhythm and quality of execution, escalating early when a senior decision or intervention is required.
This is a hands-on consulting role for someone early enough in their career to enjoy getting deep into the work, but strong enough to earn trust in a customer room. We are particularly interested in people currently operating from Consultant/Associate through Project Leader/Engagement Manager level at McKinsey, BCG or Bain, typically with around 3–5 years of client-facing consulting experience. You do not need prior operator experience.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
1. OWN THE WORKSTREAM FACT BASE
Get close to the process: interviews, data, handoffs, exceptions and the workarounds people use to keep things running. Build a fact base that shows where cost, cash, service, cycle time or control is being lost.
Turn that work into sharp analyses, decision documents and slides that make the important choices obvious. Be exact about the baseline, assumptions and evidence; do not use presentation polish to hide uncertainty. The materials are a means to a decision and an action, not the output in themselves.
2. RUN THE DAY-TO-DAY DELIVERY RHYTHM
Work with the Senior Transformation Strategist to turn a diagnostic into a practical roadmap: what starts now, what waits, which decisions an agent can make, which controls stay and who needs to own each step.
Run the weekly operating cadence with customer teams: prepare working sessions, maintain actions and decisions, follow commitments through and surface blockers early. Make sure the new process is clear enough for people to use. Work side by side with Forward Deployed Engineers as the solution moves into the live operation, keeping business needs, technical delivery and customer adoption joined up.
3. BUILD THE EVIDENCE FOR IMPACT
Help lock the baseline, target and measurement window before implementation. Track progress, investigate misses and turn the result into evidence a CFO and an operating team can trust.
You will not be asked to own commercial negotiations or the most senior stakeholder relationship alone. You will be expected to build the analysis, materials and follow-through that make those conversations productive—and to own relationships with the customer team at the working level.
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
We are looking for a capable, client-facing consultant who wants to do more than recommend a change. We will assess five things:
- Strong consulting foundations. You are currently operating from Consultant/Associate through Project Leader/Engagement Manager level at McKinsey, BCG or Bain, typically with around 3–5 years of core, client-facing consulting experience. You can structure an unfamiliar problem, find the critical question and make a clear recommendation.
- Excellent analytical and communication craft. You are comfortable working from messy data and incomplete information. You build analyses and slides that are concise, numerate and decision-ready.
- Bias for delivery and ownership. You want to stay close to the work after the deck is finished. You can run a reliable customer cadence, follow through on actions, notice what is not working and help fix it.
- Customer judgment. You can listen well, ask a direct question and communicate clearly with people at different levels of an organisation. You know when to ask for help rather than bluff.
- Early-stage working style. You work well without a large team or a polished playbook. You use AI seriously in your own work, write clearly and take responsibility for the quality of what you put in front of a customer.
Early-stage company experience is helpful, whether through a role, internship, founding project or close work with a startup. It is not required. Experience in retail, CPG, supply chain, logistics, inventory or finance operations is also helpful, but not required.
WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE AFTER 12 MONTHS
- You are the trusted day-to-day owner of defined workstreams across several enterprise accounts, with a clear view of each account’s transformation hypothesis, evidence base, risks and next decision.
- Your analyses and customer materials help teams make better decisions quickly, and your cadence means commitments do not disappear between meetings.
- You have helped take at least one process from diagnosis through live delivery, with a measured view of whether it is working.
- You have made Duvo’s playbook more reusable through better templates, diagnostics, measurement methods or delivery habits.
THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF
- You only enjoy the framing phase and lose interest once the work becomes detailed.
- You need perfectly clean data, a large analyst team or complete instructions before you can make progress.
- You see slides as the final product rather than a tool to help a customer make and execute a decision.
- You want only internal analysis work and do not want visible, day-to-day accountability with a customer team.
- You prefer to stay far from the day-to-day work of the people whose process is changing.
- You want a narrow role with little customer exposure or visible accountability.
HOW WE WORK
- Own it. The bar is not “I flagged it.” It is “I moved it forward.” An 80% fix today often beats a perfect answer next week.
- Stay close to the customer. Know their real day better than the process document. If they ask us to automate something broken, show them a better way.
- Prove it and say it straight. Measure before you propose. Share bad news when you have it. Strong opinions are welcome; defending them after the evidence changes is not.
- Use AI and work…

About Foundation Health
Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.
We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.
THE MISSION: FIXING HEALTHCARE WITH CODE
Healthcare is full of complex, frustrating workflows that haven’t changed in decades. We believe that thoughtfully applied AI can finally simplify these systems, improving both the provider's workday and the patient's experience.
Specifically, we are revolutionizing the pharmacy space. We’re building AI-powered systems that integrate directly with Electronic Health Record (EHR) platforms, helping health systems operate effectively at scale. This isn't a "chatbot on a landing page" - it’s deep, integrated infrastructure that changes how care is delivered.
THE TEAM: AI-NATIVE BY DESIGN
We’re led by a technical leadership team with deep roots in high-scale engineering, including our VP of Engineering (ex-DeepMind/Google). Together, we’re fostering an "AI-native" culture where we don’t just build AI; we use it.
We want engineers who lean on AI tools to maximize their output and automate the mundane parts of their day-to-day work. We’re creating an environment where using the latest tools isn't just allowed - it’s encouraged and championed by leadership.
LOCATION & CULTURE
We have an office in Manchester City Centre, and while we aren't a "mandatory X days in the office" company, we believe in the power of getting together. We’re looking for engineers who are excited to head into Manchester when needed to whiteboard, jam on ideas, and build rapport in person.
WHY YOU’D LEAVE YOUR CURRENT ROLE
- The AI Playground: You’ll get hands-on with OpenAI, Langfuse, and Vertex AI to ship real-world features. We aren't just "researching" AI; we are shipping it into production environments where it actually impacts patient care.
- True Feature Ownership: You won’t just be handed well-scoped tickets. You will own full features end-to-end, driving them from initial ambiguity and architectural design all the way to production.
- Influence the Technical Direction: As an early senior hire, you will have a direct seat at the table. You will collaborate closely with our VP of Engineering to shape our technical stack, establish engineering standards, and influence the product roadmap.
- Pure Product Engineering: We are looking for people who thrive when the path isn't fully paved. If you love the feeling of architecting a feature, shipping it, and seeing it in a customer's hands 48 hours later, you’ll fit in.
- Significant Equity: Because you’re joining in this early window as a senior pillar of the team, you’ll take a meaningful stake in what we are building.
WHAT WE DO CARE ABOUT
- You’re an Owner and Builder: You have a proven track record of shipping production-grade applications from scratch. You can talk deeply about system design choices, trade-offs, and how you've successfully scaled features you owned.
- You Thrive in Ambiguity: You don't wait for a perfect specification. You excel at taking loose product requirements, breaking them down into technical execution plans, and driving the implementation forward.
- Technical Leadership: You are ready to begin influencing technical direction, running architectural spikes, and raising the engineering bar for the team through code reviews and mentoring.
- AI-Native Mindset: You’ve either worked on AI products before or you deeply embed AI tools into your daily workflow to maximize your output. We want people who actively champion efficiency.
We’ve cleared the path. The funding is there, the clients are waiting, and the technical leadership is world-class. We just need the senior builders to help lead the charge.
Ready to build the future of healthcare? Let's talk.

- Procurement & vendor management — sourcing, negotiating with, and managing the tools and vendors that keep the company running — from helpdesk platforms to AI tooling.
- Contracts & legal — supporting responses to RFIs, RFPs and bids from major US health systems, reviewing agreements, and getting comfortable in the commercial detail.

- You actually use AI. It's already part of how you work, or you've tested AI-powered products and know why it's a different problem.
- You care about the outcome. Quality matters to you as a result, not as a process to tick off.
The setup
Hybrid, Manchester city centre, 1-2 days a week in the office. When you're working out what "correct" even means for an AI system, a whiteboard and the right three people in a room beat a Slack thread every time.
Not local? We offer relocation support for the right person.
We're Series A, there's early equity, and the work genuinely changes how people get their medication.

About Foundation Health
Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.
We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.
The team: AI-native by design
Our VP of Engineering comes from DeepMind/Google, and we're building with AI from day one, both in the product and in how we engineer. We use AI tools to move faster, automate repetitive work and spend more time on problems that need real engineering judgement.
What you'll actually be doing
- Designing and building the back-end systems that connect pharmacies, health systems and insurers
- Solving hard distributed-systems problems: event-driven workflows, retries, idempotency, data consistency and failure recovery
- Owning substantial features from the initial problem through architecture, build, deployment and production
- Making pragmatic technical decisions as we scale, without overengineering for problems we don't have yet
- Building AI-powered capabilities into a live product, where reliability and correctness matter as much as speed
- Working directly with product and engineering leadership to shape the roadmap, architecture and what we build next
Manchester: where our core engineering team works
Our core engineering team is based in Manchester city centre. We're in the office together 1–2 days a week to work through hard problems and debate technical decisions. The rest of the week, work wherever you're most effective.
Not in Manchester yet? If you'd consider relocating, we can help with the move.
Why you'd leave your current role
- Your work reaches real users. We're live with enterprise customers, so what you ship gets used, not lost in a backlog.
- Interesting engineering problems. We're connecting fragmented healthcare systems, where data integrity and correctness really matter. This isn't a CRUD app with an AI feature bolted on.
- Real ownership. You'll shape solutions, challenge assumptions and influence the roadmap and architecture. We want you making important technical decisions, not just implementing someone else's.
- No legacy baggage. We're on a modern Node.js, TypeScript and GCP stack. You don't need to know it already. We care far more about the systems you've built than the tools you used.
- Equity. You'll own a stake in the company you're helping build.
What we do care about
- Strong engineering judgement. You can take an ambiguous problem, work out what matters, make sensible trade-offs and deliver without every step mapped out.
- Back-end depth. You've built and operated production systems and know what happens beyond the happy path: distributed systems, databases, performance, observability and failure recovery.
- Ownership beyond the code. You think about how a feature behaves in production, how customers use it and what could go wrong. You've made technical decisions with real consequences and can explain why you made them.
- A builder's mindset. You've taken meaningful projects from idea to reality, at work or in your own time, and can explain the decisions and trade-offs you made.
- Curiosity about AI. You've built AI products, use AI to improve how you work, or are actively exploring what's possible. You don't need to be an ML researcher.
- Strong fundamentals. You reason from first principles and pick up unfamiliar tech quickly. A degree in Computer Science, Maths, Physics or Engineering is useful, but depth of engineering ability matters most.
Interested?
The funding's in place, the product is live and customers are asking for more than we can build. We're hiring engineers in Manchester to help close that gap.

About Teleport
Don't wait for the future of infrastructure. Be part of it.
Teleport is the AI Infrastructure Identity Company. Remote-first and globally distributed, we work with companies like Nasdaq, DoorDash, and Elastic to secure infrastructure for an AI world.
About the Role
We are looking for product-oriented backend engineers to join our engineering team here at Teleport. You will be responsible for designing and implementing backend services and APIs that enable access controls auditing tools, audit logging, session recording summarization, and identity workflows in all aspects of Teleport.
You will be involved in the entire product development cycle, from working with customers to understand security needs, to writing RFDs for your design ideas, to implementing distributed systems in Go. You will work very closely with engineers, product managers, and security researchers to design features that secure and monitor access to infrastructure at scale.
You will play a key role in shaping how modern infrastructure access is secured, audited, and managed at scale.
What You'll Do
- Building backend integrations https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aaws with cloud provider's managed databases.
- Working on scalability and resiliency https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Ascaleof clusters with 10K+ nodes.
- Implementing advanced HTTPS proxy with identity aware access control.
- Building hardened security https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Asecurity for Linux and Mac users.
What We're Looking For
- Go or Rust experience
- Linux systems engineering
- Cryptography engineering experience is a plus
How We Hire
- You will join 30 minute intro call and we will walk you through the compensation, interview process and requirements

You'll have the freedom and autonomy to do what you're great at, alongside teammates who care about doing it right and want to see you succeed. ABOUT FACTORY
Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.
We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.
In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).
ABOUT THE ROLE
Factory is on the cutting edge of software development. We build and deploy AI solutions that accelerate engineering work at the world's most innovative companies. We're looking for Forward Deployed Engineers to make every Factory deployment succeed, whether that means faster developer workflows, large-scale migrations, or accelerated product delivery.
As our customer base grows rapidly, you'll lead Factory's highest-impact customer implementations and special engineering projects. The role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, customer success, and go-to-market. It gives you the broadest exposure to every part of our business.
WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE
- Lead end-to-end implementation and integration of Factory into customer engineering environments, directly partnering with customer teams to design robust, optimized workflows and build successful, long-term partnerships
- Serve as the primary technical lead on customer engagements. You'll be on-site with customers regularly (typically about once a month and mostly within your region) to drive adoption, solve hard engineering problems and reduce time to value.
- Deliver large-scale migrations, modernization and refactoring work in complex production systems, and own the technical outcome with the customer.
- Respond quickly to customer needs. That can mean integrating with new systems, fixing critical issues in unfamiliar codebases or finding new ways to use Factory for a customer's specific problems.
- Learn our customers' use cases deeply, and build the tooling and documentation they need to grow at scale.
- Stay current on software development practices, tools and technologies so Factory stays at the forefront of AI in engineering.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 4–10 years of engineering experience, ideally at companies that deploy complex technical products into demanding customer environments, such as Databricks, MongoDB, Meta, Palantir, Snowflake, Stripe, Cloudflare, Vannevar, Anduril or Scale.
- Experience delivering migrations, refactors or similar changes in complex production systems in a customer-facing role is a major plus
- Demonstrable capability to quickly grasp new technologies, programming languages, and software development practices. Proficiency across a broad tech stack is highly valued.
- Strong problem-solving abilities, including quickly diagnosing, debugging, and resolving technical challenges in customer-facing settings
- Excellent communication skills and a record of building strong relationships with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- An intrinsic motivation to fix customer problems and make every deployment succeed.
- A hunger to learn and keep improving, both your own skills and the product's value to customers. You're proactive and thrive in a fast-moving startup.
- Deep expertise in an industry such as financial services, healthcare or the public sector is a plus. We hire both generalists and specialists.
This is an in-office position (5 days/week) in San Francisco, New York, London or Washington, DC.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/meticulous/d0ea88ba-27f.description_excerpt:
WHAT DO WE DO?
Our mission is to radically accelerate the pace of software development by empowering every engineer to ship at the speed their agents write code. We’re building the last piece of the puzzle to enable this - the part that makes it actually safe to ship.
AI is enabling engineers to write code faster than ever before. But software review and testing hasn’t caught up. Engineering leaders are drowning in long software review cycles and more bugs than ever. The bottleneck isn’t writing code anymore, it’s everything that comes after it.
We spent 3 years building patented foundational technology to solve this. Our CTO, Quentin, spent over a decade at Palantir, where he led the 0 to 1 of core products that insiders credit as the primary value drivers behind Gotham and Foundry. Since then, we’ve grown 5x year-on-year and now work with top engineering orgs - Notion, ElevenLabs, Mercor, Dropbox, Discord, LaunchDarkly, Wiz, CoreWeave, Wealthsimple, and more.
You’ll be joining us at a pivotal time. We’ve raised $20m from Chemistry, Menlo and Coatue, the same investors behind Twilio, Twitch, Intercom and PagerDuty and are backed by angels including the founders of Vercel, Datadog, Segment, Dropbox, the CTO of GitHub, CPO of Adobe, head of engineering at Cursor and many more.
This is an opportunity to join a company going through hypergrowth as we scale from millions of annual recurring revenue to $100m ARR.
If this excites you, come help us build it!
WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?
Join us as a Founding AE hire in London and own the full sales motion end-to-end, from first discovery to strategising pilot deployment to closing the deal.
Most AEs work a narrow slice of the stack, repeating the same sales scripts and motion deal after deal and handing off to a sales engineer the moment a conversation turns technical. Here, you’ll own the sales cycle from discovery to pilot, then stay on as deployment lead to make sure it actually succeeds. You’ll own technical conversations, building real technical authority with engineering leaders and understand exactly what their software development workflow looks like, why they buy and what they’d like to see different about the product.
This is an IC role, there is no team beneath you and no one to delegate work to.
Examples of what you will work on
- Own end-to-end cycles: You’ll build and manage your own sales pipeline, win pilots and close deals, growing to lead a geography or sector or team as we scale
- Lead enterprise sales: Navigate complex sales cycles with the world’s leading mid-market and enterprise tech businesses (up to $XXX BN market cap), initially securing low-six then mid-six figure deals
- Strategise complex deployments: Work alongside our engineers on pilots to figure out how to make them successful, run training sessions and build strong relationships at the user level
- Help steer our roadmap: You’ll become the best person in the company at explaining and pitching the product and can take specific customer feedback back to our product teams
- Events: You’ll network with CTOs & engineering leaders, attend our dinners and conferences across the US, and become well-known in this space
YOU WILL LOVE THIS ROLE IF
- ⭐ You learn fast and want to dive deep into the product - you have strong analytical thinking and can work from first principles; ambiguity / lack of experience in a technical domain doesn’t faze you / you are excited to learn!
- ⭐ You are highly agentic - you have a bias to action, move fast, take ownership without being asked (e.g. if you need sales collateral you build it yourself!)
- ⭐ You’re a hunter - chasing down revenue feels energizing, not exhausting or stressful, you create your own pipeline if there isn’t one!
- ⭐ You want to work with engineers - you will spend most of your time externally and internally with developers, and this excites you!
THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF
- You expect to work regular working hours and to travel infrequently; our teams, customers, investors span SF, London, NY
- You need a team of BDRs, RevOps and Marketing to support you across the sales motion
- You expect to lean entirely on engineers for technical demos and discovery calls
- You expect never to have to build your own pipeline
REQUIREMENTS
- STEM degree
- 3-7 years of work experience outperforming in a B2B SaaS sales, strategic deployment or adjacent role
- Experience with outbound-led sales
- Bonus if you have experience selling a deeply technical product to senior engineering leaders or have been an early GTM hire (< #20) at a fast growing startup
- If you were previously or are currently a software engineer with strong commercial acumen looking to pivot into tech sales, we’d strongly encourage you to apply!
YOU MAY LOOK LIKE THIS
- Ex-STEM: You were always on the STEM track but realised being around people is what drives you! You are currently an AE but want to go back to doing something that is a bit more technical.
- Builder: You are an AE but were previously a founder, have been part of an incubator (YC, EF, Antler) or want to be a future founder. You spike at commercial work but want to build knowledge outside of that to be a more well rounded leader in the future.
- Early-stage operator: You have been or want to be an early founding hire to help shape what sales looks like and work to build up the processes, materials and strategy that will help us win!
- AI lover: You work in b2b sales but feel like AI is developing so quickly you’re being left behind and want to build out a more technical skillset
PERKS ♥️
- Competitive comp + significant equity
- 🍲 Unlimited food & drinks in office - including daily lunch as a team, and your own Amazon business account to buy whatever snacks you want for the office.
- 💻 A setup you’ll love - everyone has a standing desk, brand new Macbook, your choice of ergonomic peripherals, and a £2k WFH budget to make home just as good
- 🏄‍♀️ £300 monthly wellness stipend - Third Space gym, reformer pilates, cold plunge, however you want to keep your best
- 🎁 We celebrate you - £400 in gifts on your birthday and work anniversary every year
- 🌴 Team offsites - we work and play hard, we’ve done offsites in Italy, Abu Dhabi and local 5-star resorts
- 📚 Unlimited book budget - we have a growing in-office library and actively encourage everyone to add to it, whether you want to ramp up your knowledge of software testing, or become a better startup operator!
- 📌 In-person, 4 days a week - at our office in Shoreditch
- many more!
PEOPLE BEHIND METICULOUS
Guillermo Rauch (founder of Vercel), Jason Warner (CTO of GitHub), Calvin French-Owen (founder of Segment), Jared Friedman (YC partner and founder of Scribd), Scott Belsky (CPO of Adobe), Arash Ferdowsi (founder of Dropbox) and many others are all personal investors in Meticulous.

ABOUT MAZE
Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.
In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.
We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.
Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.
That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey https://www.uxtools.co/survey/user-research/user-testing-overview—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.
Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values https://maze.co/about-us/.
Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.
THE ROLE
As a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer on the Product Engineering team, you'll design and deliver high impact features, working closely with product, design, and other engineers to solve complex problems, build scalable solutions, and ensure our systems are maintainable and performant.
You’ll take ownership of projects from concept to production, contribute to architectural decisions, write high quality code, and help raise the technical bar by sharing knowledge and best practices with your teammates.
YOU'LL WORK ON:
- Building elegant features for user researchers to analyze and extract compelling insights from qualitative data, using both classical techniques and large language models
- Expanding audience management to help researchers connect with and reward participants from across the world
- Integrating video and scheduling tools to provide a streamlined experience for managing and booking user interviews
AS A PRODUCT ENGINEER AT MAZE, YOU WILL:
- Partner closely with product managers, designers and other engineers to design, build, and ship new features
- Establish best practices, frameworks, and repeatable processes that enable us to measure the impact of every feature that we ship
- Evaluate and improve the performance, maintainability, and security of applications in production
- Work in a collaborative and open team, which places high value on feedback, continuous learning and trust.
YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:
- You're proficient with modern full-stack JavaScript (Node.js and React) and relational databases (PostgreSQL)
- You're enthusiastic about well-tested code and strive to improve your work environment
- You have excellent written and spoken English skills
- You thrive in a remote environment
BONUS POINTS:
- You have Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, and/or TypeScript experience
- You have experience with AWS and/or Kubernetes
- You're interested in UX, UI design, and the research field
INCLUSIVITY AND PAY
At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.
Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

- Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

- Life and Disability Insurance, 100% of the team member premium paid

- If you don't have dependents to add to your plan, you will still get access to this money to be used at your discretion to get the benefits that matter to you with our flexible a-maze-ing benefits - gym memberships, co-working spaces, food, travel, whatever!
- $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space

- Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.
That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey https://www.uxtools.co/survey/user-research/user-testing-overview—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.
Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values https://maze.co/about-us/.
SENIOR SECURITY ENGINEER
Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re hiring a Senior Security Engineer to take the lead on security at Maze. You’ll own two closely connected areas:
- The corporate IT foundation every Maze employee relies on
- The security controls that keep our cloud, code and SaaS environment secure and auditable
Identity, devices and access sit right at the intersection of IT and security. This is an opportunity to own that space end to end. Your job is to automate the IT side so well that most of your time goes to corporate security engineering. You own the budget and tooling to automate the IT layer, and the helpdesk scope stays deliberately small, so the role stays an engineering role.
You’ll report to our Senior Manager, Platform Engineering and work closely with teams across Maze.
AS A SENIOR SECURITY ENGINEER AT MAZE, YOU WILL:
- Own identity and SSO in Google Workspace, including groups, SCIM provisioning, MFA and access policies
- Run our macOS fleet through Iru, including enrolment, configuration, patching and compliance
- Automate joiner, mover and leaver flows from Rippling so new hires are fully provisioned on day one and leavers lose access within hours
- Own SaaS licensing and app provisioning, while keeping internal support lightweight through automation and self-service
- Own security controls across AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes and our SaaS environment, including role based access, IAM hygiene, cloud guardrails, network boundaries and secrets management
- Run vulnerability management end to end, taking findings from Intruder, Socket and pentests through remediation and verification with clear owners and SLAs
- Run regular access reviews and generate audit evidence through Vanta, making compliance thorough, timely and low effort
- Bring a security perspective to incidents and post-incident reviews, turning what we learn into stronger controls
- Use AI-assisted and agentic workflows to reduce manual work and investigate issues faster
WHAT YOU WON’T OWN
Application code review and threat modelling, sales questionnaires, customer security calls or other customer-facing security work. These sit with our Senior Manager, Platform Engineering today and will move into the Infosec function as business needs grow.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
- You have a strong software, infrastructure or security engineering background and are comfortable using code and infrastructure as code to automate repetitive work
- You’ve owned identity, MDM and joiner and leaver automation at a remote company and can speak to the impact your automation had
- You’ve secured a modern AWS or GCP environment and can explain the trade-offs behind your IAM decisions
- You’ve run vulnerability management or access reviews in an environment with external audits
- You have experience with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls and know how to turn a control into an automated check
- You care about the employee experience and are comfortable saying no when needed while providing context and a better path forward
- You’re excited about AI-assisted development and actively use modern AI tools in your work
OUR STACK
- Identity and people systems: Google Workspace, Rippling
- Devices: Iru (formerly Kandji), macOS
- Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker
- Security and compliance: Vanta, Intruder, Socket, Datadog Security, Riot
- Network: Cloudflare Zero Trust
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions, Depot CI, Argo CD
- Observability: Datadog
- Collaboration: Slack, Notion, Linear, GitHub, Zoom
- Application: TypeScript, Node.js, React
You don’t need experience with every technology in our stack. We care more about strong fundamentals, an engineering approach to both IT and security and excitement about making Maze secure by default as we scale.
INCLUSIVITY AND PAY
At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.
Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.
Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.
WHY MAZE IS UNIQUE
- Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.
- Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before…

- Drive research projects from conception through to deployment, showing initiative and technical depth
- Engage continuously with the latest ML literature, staying current with developments in foundation models, generative AI and scientific machine learning

You'll build and maintain the pipelines that find, enrich and deliver prospect data to our sales team, keep the CRM clean and trustworthy, and connect the tools in our stack so information flows without manual effort. - Building targeted prospect lists across NZ, AU and the UK from the ideal customer profiles the GTM team defines, covering firm type, size, practice area, location and seniority

- Designing waterfall enrichment flows that verify contact details, fill gaps and score leads, keeping bounce and unsubscribe rates low
- Using AI tooling to research accounts at scale, qualify fit, personalise outreach inputs and automate the repetitive parts of list building
- Maintaining data quality, deduplication and consent standards so lists arrive usable and compliant with the Privacy Act, Australian Privacy Principles and UK GDPR/PECR
CRM AND INTEGRATIONS
- Owning the health of our CRM (Attio), including object and field design, pipeline stages, data hygiene, deduplication, ownership rules and reporting views
- Building and maintaining integrations between the CRM and the rest of the GTM stack, including our dialler (JustCall), scheduling (Calendly), billing (Stripe), analytics (Metabase and our product database) and marketing channels (Meta Ads, website forms)
- Writing automations and scripts (Python or JavaScript, webhooks, Zapier/Make/n8n or direct API work) so leads, activities and revenue events land in the right place without anyone re-keying them
- Querying our data warehouse and Metabase in SQL to report on pipeline, conversion, attribution and rep activity, and to reconcile CRM records against source-of-truth systems
- Documenting how the stack fits together and training the team on the parts they touch
ABOUT YOU
- 3 to 5 years in revenue operations, sales operations, growth engineering, data or a similar role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company
- Proven experience building outreach or prospect lists with scraping and enrichment tools such as Clay
- Strong CRM administration on at least one modern platform (Attio, HubSpot, Salesforce or similar), including data model design and hygiene rather than just day-to-day use
- Solid SQL and comfort in a BI tool such as Metabase
- Working proficiency in Python or JavaScript, plus experience with REST APIs, webhooks and automation platforms
- Practical experience using LLMs and agentic tooling in real workflows, with a clear view of where they help and where they don't
- A high bar for data quality and the discipline to keep systems tidy over time
- Clear written communication, translating what sales and marketing need into systems that deliver it
- Experience with accounting or legal firms, or professional body datasets in NZ, AU or the UK, is an advantage
- Familiarity with marketing attribution and multi-touch pipeline analysis is an advantage
- The right to work in the UK
WHAT YOU'LL GET
- No legacy stack to work around and no committee to get through. If you can show a better way of finding customers or running the CRM, you'll ship it
- A small, well-funded team where the systems you build directly determine how well the company grows
HOW TO APPLY
Alongside your CV, include a short note about one data or automation problem you've solved for a sales team and how you did it. Links to anything you've built (repos, Clay tables, dashboards, write-ups) are welcome.

Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup based in London, founded by Guy Podjarny, who previously founded Snyk. We’ve raised more than $100 million from world-class investors, including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. In 2025, Tessl ranked #2 in Sifted’s B2B SaaS Rising 100 and #20 in its AI 100.
We’re building the context layer for AI coding agents and a platform for AI-native software development. As an early member of the team, you’ll help shape how we build and scale a company operating at the forefront of AI and software development.
OVERVIEW OF ROLE
Join our engineering team to build real-time AI Native workflows, tooling, and interfaces that will reshape how developers create and maintain software.
This is a product engineering role with a platform twist. Most of your time, you'll do what every Tessl engineer does: design, prototype and ship product features end to end, collaborating closely with product, design and the wider engineering team in a fast-paced, high-autonomy environment. What makes you different is that when the work goes below the application layer, you light up rather than back away: complex networking scenarios such as site-to-site VPN and private connectivity, multi-cloud and multi-region deployments, observability, and the machinery that makes Tessl straightforward to deploy, operate and support wherever it needs to run.
We expect you to be relentlessly AI native about it: instead of triaging alerts at 2 am, you'll build or deploy the agent that does it. Instead of reacting to scaling bottlenecks, you'll create systems that spot them before they happen. Deep expertise is the foundation, because you can't automate what you don't know, but your ambition should be to make agents do the bulk of the operational work, with you supervising and steering.
We're open on level for this role, from mid-level to senior: trajectory and appetite matter more to us than years.
What success looks like: Within your first year, you're shipping product features end to end like any Tessl engineer. When infrastructure work arises, from deployment architecture to networking to observability, you're the one who takes it on and lands it well, with support where you need it. Our deployment and operational practices are stronger because of you, agentic tooling handles a growing share of the toil, and the infrastructure work you touch is compliant by default, keeping our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 journey unblocked.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
No two days will be the same at Tessl! You'll have a high level of autonomy and be empowered to make decisions based on what you believe will help you deliver the most success. Here's an insight into just a few of the things you would be doing:
PRODUCT ENGINEERING (MOST OF YOUR TIME)
- Design and implement new functionality end to end, from initial design and prototypes to fully scoped production implementations, reviewed with the product team
- Rapidly prototype new capabilities to prove or disprove an idea, then develop a plan for a scalable implementation
- Pair with designers and other engineers to make the experience intuitive and slick, and integrate third-party services so we can focus our cycles on Tessl's core capabilities
- Gather requirements from customers and stakeholders, turn ambiguity into agreed plans, and deliver them
PLATFORM & INFRASTRUCTURE
- Lean into infrastructure work as it arises: our AWS estate (EKS/Kubernetes), infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, and our observability stack (Dash0/OpenTelemetry, Sentry, PostHog)

OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE
We're hiring a Research Engineer to join our AI Research (AIR) team. You'll work on the components that make the outer loop real: how agent harnesses orchestrate model behaviour, how we evaluate what's actually working, how pipelines turn production traces into the next round of improvement, and how we diagnose the failure modes that matter to real users.
These aren't four separate workstreams — they're parts of one system, and we want people who see them that way.
We expect you to sit close to customers — joining calls, watching sessions, reading traces — and to let real workflows shape your research priorities. You'll have meaningful autonomy and the resources to run substantial experiments where the bar for success is shipped impact.
You'll report to our AI Research Lead, and collaborate closely with engineering, product, and design.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
We're explicitly building coverage across four skill areas. You don't need to be strong in all of them — but you should bring depth in at least one:
- Agent harness and orchestration design — how tools, context, and control flow combine to make a useful agent.
- Agentic eval methodology — task and repo-level evals, dataset curation, the craft of measuring what actually matters.
- Outer-loop and pipeline thinking — feedback loops, training-data flywheels, bandit-style optimisation, anything that goes beyond a single agent session.
- Failure-mode analysis — instrumenting agents, reading traces at volume, surfacing patterns engineering can act on.
ESSENTIAL
- 4+ years shipping AI/ML products in a startup or applied industry setting, with recent hands-on experience with LLMs and agentic systems.
- Demonstrated depth in at least one of the four skill areas above.
- Strong product and customer instincts: comfort joining customer calls, watching session recordings, and letting real workflows shape what you work on.
- Sharp evaluation judgement: benchmarks where they exist, vibes and quick prototypes where they don't, and the taste to know which is appropriate.
- Experience building datasets for evaluation or training, including the pipeline work that goes with it.
- Deeply curious about agents and excited about reshaping how software is built.
NICE TO HAVE
- A Masters or PhD in a relevant computational field.
- Direct experience with coding agents or code-generation systems.
- Background in RL, bandits, or other outer-loop optimisation frameworks applied to LLMs.
- Experience building synthetic data, dataset infrastructure, or internal tooling that other engineers actually used.
- A project you can show us (GitHub links welcome) and a thoughtful answer to "Why Tessl?"
WHAT YOU'LL DO
No two weeks will look the same. A flavour:
- Sit in on a customer session, understand how their agents are failing, design an eval that captures it, and drive a fix through to shipped improvement.
- Close a piece of the outer loop end to end: production signal in, dataset out, eval scored, harness change shipped, metric moved.
- Own a slice of our eval infrastructure: dataset curation, harness configuration, runner, analysis, and the comms back to engineering.
- Prototype a new harness or context configuration and measure whether it actually moves the needle on real customer tasks.
- Dig through pages of agent traces, build the tooling you need to make sense of them, and brief the team on what you found.
- Partner with product and engineering on near-term shipping problems by bringing research rigour.
- Pull a recent paper apart, work out what's actually transferable to our platform, and turn it into a concrete experiment.
YOU’LL BE SUCCESSFUL IF…
In your first 3 months, you might have shipped a new eval suite for a real customer workflow, improved an agent harness based on trace analysis, or built a pipeline that turns production failures into reusable test cases.
SALARY AND BENEFITS
Competitive salary commensurate with experience. Health insurance extending to partners and dependents, pension contributions, and the rest of what you'd expect.
Our office is a couple of minutes from King's Cross — pet friendly, with regular team lunches, drinks, and socials. We're hybrid, with Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday as the primary in-office days.
APPLICATION PROCESS
- Intro call to understand "Why Tessl?" and to tell you a bit about us.
- A call with our AI Research Lead to understand your ways of working and how you use agents.
- A 4 hour technical take-home exercise extending our one-shot implementation.
- A half-day on-site session including whiteboarding and hands-on activities.
- Leadership chats with our Head of People, Head of Engineering and CEO.

his is a pure new-logo role. You will win the large, multi-country property owners, operators and facilities management organisations that do not yet work with Singu, running the full cycle from first cold conversation to signature. Once an account is live, Customer Success takes it forward.

Support, Package and Progression

- Build a contract governance model – define document ownership, approval rights, negotiation limits and fallback positions, version control, and a review cadence, and decide clearly what is Group-standard and what is country-specific.

ABOUT MERCOR
Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.
Mercor Safety Research Grants $5M
One of the biggest challenges the industry faces today is addressing whether frontier AI is safe enough to deploy. A model can pass safety checks and still act differently in production. This is why investing today in safety research, evals and verification is critical.
Mercor is committing $5 million to fund safety research. Award size and mix depend on the project. The grant supports:
- Researcher hours
- API costs
- Stipends for event and conference attendance
- The time of experts from Mercor's platform
This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds benchmark and economics work. You can apply to that HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/?ashby_jid=e1f6792d-1aae-4c2e-8edb-e2b91343dbb5.
What we're looking for
We're open to proposals across the full range of safety interests. We're particularly interested in:
- Misalignment: deceptive alignment, goal misgeneralization, reward hacking, scheming, and situationally-aware failure modes
- Sandbox escape: containment failures, privilege escalation, tool misuse, and agents operating outside their intended scope
- Evaluation awareness: models detecting they are being tested and behaving differently under observation than in deployment
- Interpretability: understanding what models are actually doing internally, and whether that can be made legible to a human reviewer
- Oversight and control: scalable supervision, human-in-the-loop reliability, and what breaks when the system is more capable than its reviewer
- Red-teaming methodology: more robust systems for uncovering novel failures
If your work doesn't fit neatly into these, apply anyway. Strong proposals outside this list are welcome.
Why us
- Funding for researcher time, API costs, and event attendance
- Where useful to the work: access to Mercor's expert network for human grading, red-teaming, and annotation: lawyers, accountants, engineers, scientists, clinicians
- Access to Mercor's internal evaluation infrastructure, subject to review
- Introductions to Mercor's network of researchers across frontier labs and academia
Who should apply
- Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.
- People with a specific, well-scoped question: the grant is built around your proposal, not a generic research rotation
- Applicants based in the United States or the United Kingdom
- Background in ML, CS, statistics, or an adjacent field (measurement, psychometrics, HCI, security, social science)
- Bonus: experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, adversarial ML, or systems security
We expect grantees to publish. A paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.
Award terms
Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:
- Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.
- Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.

Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.
🚀 OUR STORY
Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.
Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.
Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/why-partly-exists and AI at Partly https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/ai-at-partly.
THE OPPORTUNITY
Repairers train for years to be on the tools, then spend half their day on quotes, paperwork and finding parts. Partly's product aims to automate the admin so repairers can focus on their craft. The products we've launched this year start with a conversation, and behind it a system generates the interface the moment needs. So we no longer design a set of pages. We design components, and then we design the brain the AI uses to assemble them. Very few designers have done this yet. That's the opportunity: to work out what product design becomes at an AI company, in a domain where a wrong answer is a $1,000 part that can't be returned.
The problems are real and unsolved. How does someone who's never used a chat interface know what to ask when they land on an empty box between phone calls? How does a task you do forty times a day become one tap, not one more sentence to type, with the same result every time? How much of the agent's reasoning do you show before trust turns into a wall of text? Where should the interface be opinionated, and where should it be generated? We don't have the answers yet. You'll own finding Partly's.
🖍️ THE ROLE
Our product teams are organised around a product, each led by a Product Lead (Principal Product Manager) with a Product Engineer and a mix of engineers. Design is not embedded in those teams. We're building a global design team that works across all of our products and is focused on three things: the design system everything is built from, coherence across the whole product family, and the quality of the experience wherever a repairer or supplier meets us. Our customers range from repairers and parts admins in a single independent workshop to multi-billion-dollar repair groups, and the suppliers who provide their parts. The team exists to drive adoption and stickiness through experiences that feel magical, in a way that works for our customers. We work collaboratively with the Product Leads who drive their products.
This is a senior design role for someone with incredible judgement and hands-on experience with AI surfaces and experiences. You lead with design: problem framing, systems thinking, interaction and craft. And you make things real, with working prototypes built inside our design system.
You won't sit in a product team's backlog. Product Leads own their products and what ships. You own the principles, patterns and system they build from, and you set your own agenda for where those need to go next. When something ships below the bar, you're the one who says so.
This role is based in one of our offices: Auckland or Christchurch in New Zealand, London in the UK, or Austin, Texas in the US. The design team works across all of them.
💻 WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own the design system that engineers and coding agents build our AI experiences from. Components, patterns, rules and guidance that read correctly to an engineer and to a coding agent, so the right choice is the default even when you're not in the room.
- Shape and ship the patterns for agentic and generative experiences. Natural language where conversation fits, generated UI where the data is dense, and agents that take on the admin, verification and sourcing around a repair while the person keeps the decisions that matter.
- Define how the product behaves when it's uncertain. When the agent acts, proposes or asks, in line with the cost of being wrong. How it shows its work, how a person corrects it, and who's right when they disagree.
- Give the product its character. How our agents speak to a repairer, their tone, when they're brief and when they explain. A personality people recognise on every surface where they meet us.
- Hold the bar across every product. Notice when the same job looks different in two products and fix it at the source, in the system rather than page by page. Measure adoption and quality, and hold teams to them.
- Work with real prototypes. Build working versions with AI tools inside our design system, test them on real data, and put them in front of repairers and suppliers.
- Pair with engineers, no hand-offs. Work directly with Product Engineers and their teams, polish the details together, and review the UI that coding agents produce from the system.
- Spend real time with customers. In the workshop, on the phone and in the product, running research alongside the Product Leads who hold the deep customer context in each region.
- Write the principles and rules. How the experience behaves on behalf of a person, written clearly enough that an engineer and a model can both follow them.
🥷 WHAT YOU BRING
- Senior experience, evidenced. You've been trusted to run a project end to end and can point to the user behaviour that changed because of it. Typically 5+ years designing complex software; the evidence matters more than the years.
- You've designed agentic experiences, and can show the work. Shipped at work or built seriously on your own time. Tasks, tools, autonomy, human-in-the-loop, evaluation: you've made real calls on what an agent does alone, what it proposes and what it asks, and you can tell us which of those calls were wrong.

You'll become the human face of Partly in repair shops across the UK — someone repairers genuinely trust and enjoy working with.

🪅 WHAT YOU’LL GET
