- Travel and accommodation costs covered
- Real responsibility and customer-facing experience from week one
- A strong reference and genuine insight into how a fast-growing tech company operates

Partly.com http://Partly.com is the infrastructure platform, the B2B layer that powers parts data, cataloging, and procurement across hundreds of integrations globally. Automotive data is scattered around the world in complex, inconsistent formats, and the interesting work is in unifying it into something that drives a customer's business. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.
Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. 🖍️ THIS ROLE
This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.
You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitized, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.
Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.
And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.
You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.
Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.
Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.
Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.
Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.
Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.
Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.
Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is the platform for running reliable AI agents and workflows. Developers use it to build, deploy, and scale production systems with built-in tools for orchestration, scheduling, monitoring, and debugging.

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help us build our Open Source and Cloud product. The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in Node.js, TypeScript, Postgres, Redis, and cloud infrastructure. This role requires both technical depth and the ability to think strategically about our platform's future.

- Designing and implementing SDK and platform features. Shipping new capabilities end to end, from API surface to production rollout.
- Database design. Developing database schemas and data models that hold up as the product scales.
- Query performance and data access. Creating and optimising query performance and data access patterns.

- We're a product-led growth company, so everyone is expected to get involved in creating content like code examples, blog articles, videos, and tweets.

- Expertise in Node.js and TypeScript. We use Remix.
- Expertise with Postgres and Redis. You've designed schemas, tuned queries, and run these in production.
- Cloud infrastructure experience. AWS, GCP, or Azure.
- Comfortable being on call. Reliability is a shared responsibility for the engineering team.
- Open to in-person events throughout the year. If you're remote, we'll arrange these so the team gets real time together.
You'll be an amazing fit if you have:
- A proven track record of contributing to open source projects.
- Previously been a venture-backed startup founder.
- Experience with React, or better still, Remix.
- Worked on a high throughput system.
- Designed SDKs for developers.
- Experience with self-managed Kubernetes.
- Familiarity with Linux.
- OTel or "o11y" experience.
- Worked at a developer tools company.
- Experience with Go.
ABOUT THE TEAM
- We are a small team with a flat hierarchy.
- We encourage continuous learning and personal development.
- Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help.
- We care about our customers and the open-source community.
- Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge.
BENEFITS
- Generous, transparent compensation and equity - We hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity as a way to ensure everyone is invested in the success of the company.
- Async working - Need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!
- Home office - We will help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.
- Generous vacation - We believe it's important to take time off. We encourage you to take your 25 days vacation excluding national holidays, plus sick leave and generous parental leave.
- Training budget - An annual budget to contribute towards learning such as purchasing books, an Audible subscription or online courses.
- Pension and 401k contributions - Enroll in our company pension scheme or we'll contribute directly to your private pension.
OUR VALUES
- We are proud to be open source - We believe in the open source community and building a great free-to-use product. We encourage community contributions and are public about what we are building.
- We ship uncomfortably fast - As a startup, moving fast is key. We are pragmatic about what we build, when we build it, and value iterative development above all.
- Working autonomously - We don't tell you what to do. We decide as a team what will have the biggest impact for our customers and prioritise what we work on from that.
INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Application. We'll review your application, CV, and any code samples or open source contributions you share.
2. Screening call. A chat about your background, the systems you've built, and what you're looking for next.
3. Hiring manager call. A deeper technical conversation about your work and how you'd approach the role.
4. Paid task day. You'll spend a paid day working on a real engineering problem with us, then walk us through your thinking with the team.
5. Final interview. A call with a couple of members of the wider team to answer any remaining questions and align on culture fit.
6. References & offer. If everyone is happy, we'll make you an offer to join us.
If this sounds like your dream job, we can't wait to hear from you. If you're not sure that you exactly fit these requirements, get in touch anyway!

Giving time back to the team. Taking on recruiting coordination and admin as much as possible to unlock the team.

Fluency with engineering roles and stacks. You can hold a credible conversation about backend, infrastructure, or security roles well enough to screen and sell candidates on the role.
Strong sourcing and headhunting skills. You're comfortable building pipelines directly rather than waiting on inbound.
Experience managing agency relationships. You know how to get good work out of external recruiters and where it makes sense to bring hiring in-house instead.
Great written and verbal communication. Candidates and hiring managers alike get clarity and a fast response.

- Experience recruiting for developer tools, open source, or infrastructure companies.
- Experience with Ashby or a similar modern ATS.
- A track record of reducing agency spend by building direct pipelines.
- Previous in-house (not just agency-side) recruiting experience.
- An interest in staying on longer-term - this role has a genuine path to permanent.
ABOUT THE TEAM
- We are a small team with a flat hierarchy.
- We encourage continuous learning and personal development.
- Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help.
- We care about our customers and the open-source community.
- Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge.

3-month fixed-term contract, full time, with a genuine possibility of converting to a permanent role based on performance and ongoing hiring needs.

Generous, transparent compensation - we hire the best talent and pay to reflect that.

ABOUT THE POSITION
We're looking for a backend product engineer who loves security - not a security box-ticker. You'll build and own the systems that let Trigger safely run massive volumes of untrusted user code inside our infrastructure, at scale.
Some of our customers let their own users run untrusted code on top of Trigger - think coding agents executing arbitrary instructions. We have to guarantee that code can never break Trigger's systems, or our customers' systems. That makes this partly a product engineering role: building secure sandbox runtimes is a feature we ship, not something bolted on after the fact.
The ideal person here is a backend engineer with genuine offensive-security instincts - someone who naturally gravitates toward hacking, pen testing, and breaking things, and brings that curiosity into how they build. You'll pair strong backend/product instincts with a hacker's mindset.
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
You'll do a variety of things including:
Sandbox and runtime security. Designing and maintaining the secure execution environments that isolate untrusted user code - the core, product-shaped problem at the heart of this role.
Threat detection and incident response. Building monitoring and alerting for suspicious activity, and leading the response when something needs investigating.
Vulnerability management, end to end. Regular scanning and triage, plus AI-assisted security scans run on a quarterly cadence, and triaging incoming disclosures.
Offensive security. Running internal, AI-assisted pen testing, and potentially bringing in external firms for deeper engagements.
PR security review. Adding a security-specific review layer on top of our normal PR process.
SOC 2 and compliance. Mostly done already - this is about ongoing maintenance, not standing it up from scratch.
Vulnerability disclosure process. Owning our vulnerability disclosure program end to end.
Security culture. Helping the wider engineering team build secure habits - reviews, documentation, and pragmatic guardrails rather than heavy process.
Working at a Commercial Open Source Software company is more than just security work:
- We have an active community on Discord and GitHub. Everyone on the team helps customers, reviews PRs, and creates issues.
- Having great documentation is essential. Everyone writes docs.
- We're a product-led growth company, so everyone is expected to get involved in creating content like code examples, blog articles, videos, and tweets.
REQUIREMENTS
Real backend engineering experience. You can design and ship production backend systems, not just audit someone else's.
Genuine offensive-security curiosity. Pen testing, CTFs, bug bounty hunting, or hacking as a hobby or discipline - this isn't a checklist role.
Comfort owning ambiguous, product-shaped security problems. Sandboxing and runtime isolation are engineering problems as much as they are security ones.
A proactive mindset. This role should take work off the team's plate, not create a queue for others - we're not looking for a security box-ticker.
Comfortable being on call. Reliability and security response are shared responsibilities across the team.
Open to in-person events throughout the year. If you're remote, we'll arrange these so the team gets real time together.
You'll be an amazing fit if you have:
- Experience building or hardening sandboxed/isolated execution environments (containers, microVMs, gVisor, Firecracker, WASM sandboxes, or similar).
- A track record in pen testing, bug bounty programs, or CTFs.
- Experience using AI-assisted tooling for security scanning or workflows.
- A proven track record of contributing to open source projects.
- Worked at a developer tools, infrastructure, or open source company.
- Experience with Node.js and TypeScript, enough to read and review application code.

Generous, transparent compensation and equity - we hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity so everyone is invested in the company's success.
Async working - need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!
Home office - we help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

We are proud to be open source - we believe in the open source community and building a great free-to-use product.

Working autonomously - we don't tell you what to do. We decide as a team what will have the biggest impact for our customers and prioritise from that.

Today, we have over $300B AUM and 30,000 users on the platform, and we have much more left to do.

3. We prioritise talent over tenure. There is no promise of progression without performance – we assess and reward people on impact above all else.

We look for people who match our ambition levels, and then raise it further.

- Own an area of the product, from developing the vision, co-designing with clients, to working alongside a squad of engineers to build and deliver at the intersection of AI and private markets infrastructure
- Drive forward growth topics and special projects, including supporting the enterprise GTM motion, opening a New York office, building out new bets from scratch, and developing Vega’s industry presence with events

- 1 to 4 years’ experience in MBB or top-tier IB/PE firm
- Self-starter with proven track record of excellence
- High agency and comfortable with ownership; ability to make decisions and drive execution independently where you see fit
- Outstanding communication and analytical skills, including with senior external stakeholders
Why join us?
- Get a first-hand view, and real ownership of, everything that it takes to operate a fast-growing business
- You will help define the transformation of one of the most influential industries of our time with AI, working alongside an ambitious and dedicated team
- Competitive salary and equity package
- Benefits including medical insurance, gym membership, learning budget, and more

🌱 ABOUT ZOE
ZOE is a gut health science company. We turn world-leading nutrition research into everyday products that help people feel healthier, including the ZOE app, our at-home Gut Health Test, Daily30+ and the Gut Health Bar. Our scientists run the largest nutrition study in the world, and the ZOE Science & Nutrition podcast is one of the most listened-to health podcasts in the UK. Our mission is to transform the health of millions by giving them the most advanced science and technology.
👥 ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Engineering team https://joinzoe.notion.site/Shape-the-future-of-health-313f5c8e549681a5b26ae626e0875539 sits at the heart of that mission. We're a distributed team of around 40 people across the UK and EU, and we like solving complex problems together. We bring a wide mix of skills, from front-end, back-end, full-stack and mobile engineering to machine learning, data science and analytics, to build the experiences that guide our members through their health journey.
We're proud of the diversity in our team: 39% female and 61% male, with colleagues from many backgrounds, cultures and lived experiences. We believe this makes us stronger, more creative and better able to serve our global community.
Collaboration is core to how we work. Engineers at ZOE partner closely with data scientists, analysts, product managers and product designers to bring new ideas to life. Depending on the project, we also work with marketing, finance, legal and other teams, so the work is highly cross-functional and impactful.
Above all, we value curiosity, openness and empowerment. We encourage everyone to share ideas, keep learning and shape how we work, whether that's experimenting with new technology, improving our ways of working or finding better ways to support our members.

ZOE has built a world-class, science-led health brand, and now we’re taking our physical products into retail. Next year, our Gut Health Bars launch into major UK grocers, and we’re hiring our first National Account Manager to lead it.
You’ll own our relationships with buyers at grocers like Tesco and Sainsbury’s, shape our retail strategy, and build the function from day one, with a growing pipeline of new products to follow. If you’ve personally managed major UK grocers, love a tough negotiation, and want to build something rather than inherit it, this is your opportunity.

This is a genuine zero-to-one role and ZOE’s first commercial hire, with our retail function built around you. We have a clear retail strategy; you’ll bring the major grocer expertise to turn it into reality, challenge it where needed, and build the playbook we’ll scale from across the UK and beyond.
You’ll lead everything from the first pitch and commercial negotiation through to supplier setup, launch, and trading once we’re on shelf. It’s a hands-on role that balances strategy and execution: one day you’ll be shaping which grocer we launch with first, the next you’ll be in a buyer meeting or getting a product live on a supplier portal.

🚀 ABOUT THE ROLE
ZOE is scaling rapidly. We’re broadening our product range, expanding across the EU, and beyond and entering major retail channels. As our manufacturing partner base, retailer requirements, and technical activity grow, we need dedicated internal ownership of our Quality Management System (QMS), product compliance, supplier controls, and quality processes.
As our Quality & Technical Specialist, you will be the guardian of trust in every product we launch. You’ll be the operational engine of our technical function—ensuring documentation is audit-ready, risks are visible, suppliers are governed, products are verified, and international launches have solid technical foundations.
👥 ABOUT THE TEAM
You’ll be joining our dynamic, fast-paced Operations team, reporting directly to the Food Supply Operations Manager. You will work closely with leads across inventory, procurement, and fulfillment within the broader supply chain team. In this role, you sit right at the centre of how ZOE creates, protects, and scales its products.
You will act as the key connector across internal teams and external partners. Internally, you will partner closely with Customer Experience to investigate product feedback, work with Legal and Regulatory to ensure compliance, and sync with Commercial and Marketing to enable seamless product launches. Externally, you will serve as the hands-on technical point of contact for our manufacturing partners, co-packers, independent testing laboratories, and supermarket retail technical teams. You will be the team’s operational expert on quality, with senior technical leadership always available to guide governance, long-term manufacturing strategy, and complex escalations.

- QMS & Compliance: Maintain QMS records, audit schedules, and safety policies in line with BRCGS, HACCP, and UK/EU food regulations.

- Product & Retail Specs: Own finished product/packaging specifications, review artwork for labelling accuracy, and manage retailer technical portals.

- Recalls & Crisis Management: Lead mock recall exercises and own the operational response plan for product incidents, ensuring full supply chain traceability at all times.
- Verification & Testing: Oversee lab testing (microbiological, chemical, sensory), shelf-life studies, nutritional verification, and Certificates of Analysis (CoA).
- Complaints & Risk (CAPA): Lead root-cause investigations into non-conformances (NCR) and consumer complaints, implementing corrective action plans (CAPA).
- Launch & Process Automation: Support NPD and market expansion compliance, using digital tools and AI to streamline quality workflows and tracking.

- Technical & Lab Literacy: Experience reviewing lab data (CoAs, micro testing, shelf-life studies) and writing product specifications.
- Allergen Expertise: Understanding of UK/EU allergen labelling laws and practical experience auditing allergen controls and cleaning validation at third-party manufacturing facilities.
- Traceability or Recall Experience: Hands-on experience conducting traceability audits and executing mock or live product recalls.
- Data-Savvy & Adaptable: Thrives analysing complaint trends and solving quality issues in a fast-paced scale-up.
- Right to Work: Permanent right to work in the UK or EU.
- Willingness to Travel: You are able and willing to travel to our manufacturing partners and supplier sites (primarily UK/EU) approximately once or twice every few months for routine audits, relationship building, and production trials.
👌🏼 THE NICE-TO-HAVES
- Experience supporting physical product launches outside the UK (particularly EU or North America).
- Degree or formal apprenticeship in Food Science, Food Technology, or quality auditing.
- Experience navigating major retailer technical portals and due-diligence questionnaires.
- Curiosity and enthusiasm for using AI tools and digital automation to streamline operations and administrative work.
✨ WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THIS ROLE
- Audit-Ready QMS: ZOE’s quality documentation is current, complete, and easy to navigate.
- Controlled Suppliers: Supplier approvals, certifications, and technical records are structured and up to date.
- Seamless Launches: Retailer due diligence and international expansions are supported by accurate technical documentation on schedule.
- Closed-Loop Quality: Quality complaints, NCRs, and CAPAs are tracked, analysed, and resolved quickly to prevent recurrences

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The Challenge
Wayflyer takes credit risk across every segment we lend into, and that risk needs guardrails that hold up under growth, not just on a slide. Right now, we need someone to own two of Credit Strategy's four pillars, the policies and frameworks that govern how we lend, and the underwriting engine that decides who gets funded and how fast. Get this right and we grow faster with more discipline, not less.
What You'll Actually Do
- Design, own, and continuously improve the credit policies and frameworks that govern lending across all customer segments, built to enable growth, not just guard against it.
- Turn Wayflyer's risk appetite into frameworks people can actually use: underwriting rules, portfolio limits, approval authorities, all of it measurable.
- Design the frameworks that let new products and new markets launch within Wayflyer's risk appetite, not around it, you're in the room for new product development and market entry from the start.
- Sit between Risk, Finance, Legal, and Revenue and make sure policy works for all of them, practical, compliant, and aligned with what our funding partners need.
- Use loss experience and portfolio performance to keep policy current, not theoretical, and bring senior leadership real trade-offs as trends emerge.
- Rebuild underwriting from the ground up where it's slow or manual: find the friction, design new playbooks by segment, fix it.
- Build standardised risk scorecards from design to production, working directly with Decision Science on the model and Engineering on the tooling.
- Bring new data into underwriting, bureau, alternative, whatever moves the needle, and run vendor evaluation end to end.
- Own the override taxonomy and the feedback loop that turns override and outcome data back into sharper policy and better-calibrated scorecards.
- Build the policy architecture for underwriting that's increasingly automated and lower-touch, as more of this function becomes AI-enabled.
- Use AI tools as a default, not a novelty, generating credit packs, underwriting memos, and scenario analysis, then applying your own judgement to validate and finalise them.
- Feed segment-level insight, concentration risk, vintage curves, trends, into the monthly reporting pack and Board materials, partnering with the data team to get there.
What This Role Could Turn Into
This is a new role, we haven't hired for it before, so we won't pretend there's a well-worn path to point to. What we can tell you is the shape of it: own two pillars of Credit Strategy this well, and Director or Head of Credit Strategy is a realistic next step, not a stretch. More broadly, owning policy and underwriting at this level tends to be the kind of experience that opens doors into wider Risk or Underwriting leadership as Wayflyer grows into new products and markets. Where exactly it leads is genuinely up to you and how you build it.
Who Thrives Here
Someone who's built a policy or underwriting process from nothing before, not just operated inside one someone else designed. You spot a gap in a framework and you don't wait for permission to close it, including when a risk event or a regulatory change means you need a fast, well-reasoned answer under real pressure. You think in frameworks, not exceptions, but you're comfortable being the exception when the moment calls for it. You already use AI tools daily as part of how you think and work, not as an occasional shortcut, and you know the difference between AI-assisted output and output you'd actually put your name on.
We Hire for Range
This is a senior, build-and-own role, so we're looking for someone whose trajectory shows it: a history of taking policies, frameworks, or scorecards from first principles to production, working directly with Engineering and Data Science along the way, not just reviewing their output. That trajectory typically comes with 8–10+ years in credit risk, policy design, or risk governance, fintech, alternative lending, or commercial banking backgrounds all count, but we care more about what you've built than how long you've been building it. Exposure to lending in the SME or e-commerce sector with knowledge on working capital and term lending products (MCAs, STLs, RCFs, LOCs) are all a plus. An advanced degree or certification in finance, economics, or risk, CFA, FRM, or similar, is a bonus, not a bar.
Location and Working Policy
📍Dublin or London, hybrid (3 days per week in the office)
The Good Stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and critical illness cover. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental and adoptive leave for primary and secondary caregivers. And 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

Easyship is one of the world’s leading multi-carrier shipping software, built to make global eCommerce borderless. Job Title: eCommerce   Merchandiser (International Returns)
Location: London (Travel to Corby Required Occasionally) 
Reporting to: Head of Programs
Key Relationships: Program Management, Operations & Hub Management, Compliance, eBay

Who We’re Looking For:

Easyship runs eBay’s International Returns programme, and every returned item is an opportunity to recover value. We’re looking for a eCommerce  Merchandiser to own the resale of that returned inventory. You’ll assess and triage returned items, set pricing and resale strategy, list them across resale channels, and keep stock moving so aging inventory stays low. We’re after someone commercially minded and detail-oriented, who enjoys turning returns into revenue and uses data to keep improving the approach.

What would you be responsible for:

  • Assessing, grading, and triaging returned items to decide the best route for each unit.
  • Setting pricing and resale strategy to maximise recovery value, balancing speed of sale against margin.
  • Listing and presenting items across resale channels, with accurate titles, photos, descriptions, and categorisation.
  • Managing stock flow: keeping aging inventory low, clearing slow movers, and prioritising high-value units.
  • Choosing between bulk and individual resale (liquidation lots or piece-by-piece) based on which returns the most value.
  • Tracking recovery rate, sell-through, inventory aging, and margin per unit, and refining strategy based on the results.
  • Working with Program Management, Operations, and Compliance to keep the programme running smoothly.

You Might Be a Good Fit If:

  • You have experience in eCommerce resale, online marketplace selling (eBay or similar), liquidation, or returns and reverse logistics.
  • You have strong commercial and pricing judgement, and you’re comfortable with margin and recovery calculations.
  • You have a sharp eye for detail when grading condition and writing listings.
  • You’re analytical and use data to refine pricing and resale decisions.
  • You’re highly organised and can prioritise high volumes of time-sensitive stock.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment and challenge the status quo to get better outcomes.
  • Bonus: liquidation or B2B bulk-lot selling; cross-border shipping and international returns; knowledge of restricted and prohibited goods; experience with inventory or warehouse management systems.

Why You’ll Love Working at Easyship?

  • Competitive compensation with equity options
  • Comprehensive health insurance
  • Gym & wellness reimbursement
  • Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year
  • Generous vacation policy, duvet days, and mental health days

Headquartered in London with offices in New York, Hong Kong, Singapore, Melbourne, Toronto, and Taipei – our team is global and growing. We encourage you to apply if a challenge excites you. Come and join the Easyship team!

desirable.

 Benefits

Locations: Amsterdam; Chicago; London; New York

 

Scope:

As a software developer at Headlands Tech you will design, engineer and implement the Firm’s trading software in the C++ programming language.  You will work in close collaboration with the research, systems, and operations teams to architect, implement and analyze new automated electronic trading algorithms.  You will play a key role in designing and constructing the Firm’s software infrastructure to support new and existing lines of business.  In addition, you will expand the Firm’s proprietary research platform to improve performance and support new exchanges, products and functionality.

 

Qualifications:

  • Preferred degree in any computing related area (e.g., computer science, computer engineering, etc.)
  • In lieu of this, extensive professional software development experience
  • Well-versed in the fundamentals of software engineering
  • Genuine interest in solving technical problems, along with a strong ability to implement solutions
  • Low ego, able to work both in a collaborative team setting and autonomously
  • Committed to designing and implementing fully automated, scalable, and maintainable solutions with extensive testing
  • Superior ability to write in C++, or experience with other statically-typed imperative programming language
  • Comfortable operating at various different levels of abstraction, from individual machines to large scale distributed systems
  • Strong knowledge of the details of computing all throughout the technical stack
  • Knowledge of Linux a plus
  • Experience in the trading industry preferred but not mandatory

 

Day to Day:

This isn't an exhaustive list, but represents a selection of the types of tasks that software developers at Headlands Tech take on while developing and maintaining a large scale 24 hour automated trading system.

  • Build, maintain, and improve exchange connectivity
  • Leverage existing infrastructure, extending functionality where necessary
  • Build a deep understanding of exchange behavior to integrate into our existing trading system
  • Maintain and extend core research infrastructure
  • Design, implement, and maintain distributed storage systems with various different performance and reliability requirements
  • Address performance limitations within our own software, open source libraries and applications, Linux, etc.
  • Investigate new technologies to improve stability, scalability, and performance
  • Implement new trading strategies in collaboration with research and operations teams
  • Extend strategy framework to enable new behaviors and improve existing ones
  • Investigate signal issues for trading system

Join Us!

People are at the core of who we are and what we do. Your Mission

Our Heat Geek team is excited to bring an Experience Manager into the fold — a brand new role that reflects how seriously we take the people and communities at the heart of what we do.

Heat Geek isn't just about great technology. It's about the humans who build it, install it, and champion it. As our Experience Manager, you'll be the person who makes being part of Heat Geek — whether as an employee, an installer, or a partner — genuinely feel like something special. You'll shape the culture of our office, orchestrate events that people talk about for months, and bring the same obsessive attention to detail to a monthly team social as you would to a flagship installer gathering.

As we expand internationally, this role will grow with us. You'll increasingly bring that same quality of experience to new markets and new communities as Heat Geek takes its mission beyond the UK.

This is a rare role: part events producer, part culture curator, part logistics wizard. It requires someone who doesn't wait to be told what to do, who sweats the small stuff because they know that's what makes the big stuff land, and who takes genuine pride in creating environments and experiences that leave people feeling energised and valued.

If you're reading this and it resonates with you, we know that you are talented and could do this work anywhere. But we want you to do it HERE, with us, because we need persevering teammates who care about making a real difference in the world.

Office & Environment

  • Own and continuously improve the look, feel, and energy of our office, making it a place people genuinely love coming to.
  • Source and manage suppliers, perks, and day-to-day touches that elevate the everyday experience of working at Heat Geek.

Employee Events

  • Plan and run a monthly team social, our annual Christmas celebration, and periodic away days.
  • Brief and manage external agencies on larger events, holding them to a high standard and ensuring everything is on-brand and on-budget.

Installer & Partner Experiences

  • Design and deliver 6-10 installer events per year, a mix of in-office gatherings and external venues, that strengthen our relationships with the engineers who make Heat Geek's mission possible.
  • Own the full event lifecycle: concept, logistics, on-the-day execution, and follow-up.

Executive & Travel Support

  • Provide travel and logistics support to the C-level team, handling the details so they can focus on the bigger picture.
  • As we grow into new markets, support the coordination of international travel and logistics for the leadership team.

 

Candidate Requirements

  • Experience in events management, hospitality, concierge services, or executive support, or a combination of these

The aim is a function that scales on systems, not headcount.

Business partnering. You’ll bring the numbers to life. Quarterly budgeting and reforecasting, cash and runway, scenario modelling with the leadership team on the decisions that actually matter, and strategic support through fundraising and investor reporting. You’ll be a trusted partner to the CEO and COO, not a reporting line.

Team leadership. You’ll build and grow a high-performing finance team, and you’ll do it as a supportive, development-focused manager. Clear expectations, clear roles, real progression pathways, and a culture of ownership, commercial thinking and curiosity about better ways of working.

  • Strong controls instinct paired with a commercial mindset: you care about the numbers being right and about what they mean
  • Sharp analytical instincts: you see the story in the numbers and raise what matters early
  • A manager people want to work for, with a real desire to build and develop a team
  • Comfortable in ambiguity and happy building structure where little exists
  • Motivated by the mission and the shift to low-carbon heating

job-boards.greenhouse.io/insurtechinsigh.description_excerpt:
Are you commercially driven, excited by the idea of building a career in sales, and looking to join an ambitious, entrepreneurial team? Cool, this might be for you!

The role

You’ll be responsible for selling delegate passes to senior professionals attending our international conferences.

This is a high-performance, phone-based B2B sales role. You’ll proactively reach out to prospective delegates, including previous conference attendees and existing leads, build relationships, manage your own pipeline and take opportunities from first conversation through to close.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for someone who genuinely wants to sell and is motivated by targets, performance and winning.

You should have:

  • At least 1 year of B2B sales experience, ideally in a phone-based sales, outbound sales or telesales environment.

  • Experience proactively contacting leads, building relationships and converting opportunities into sales.

  • A strong commercial mindset and motivation to hit and exceed revenue targets.

  • Confidence speaking with new people and the ability to build rapport quickly.

  • Resilience and persistence – you’re comfortable hearing “no” and continuing to push for results.

  • A high level of ownership over your pipeline, follow-ups and performance.

  • A desire to learn, improve and develop quickly.

This role might not be the right fit if...

  • You don't enjoy spending a significant part of your day on the phone, speaking with prospective customers.

  • You prefer a role focused on relationship management rather than actively driving sales.

  • You’re uncomfortable working towards clear sales and revenue targets.

  • You’re looking for a hybrid or remote position – our London team works together from the office five days a week.

What you’ll do

  • Generate new business by proactively reaching out to prospective delegates.

  • Sell delegate passes to senior professionals across Europe.

  • Manage your sales pipeline from initial contact through to close.

  • Work towards ambitious individual revenue targets.

  • Develop a strong understanding of our conferences, audiences and industries.

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary plus an uncapped commission structure.

  • Ongoing sales training, coaching and feedback.

  • Fast career progression with significant responsibility for high performers.

  • International exposure and opportunities to travel to our conferences.

  • 25 days’ holiday plus company pension contribution.

  • Regular team socials, lunches and events.

About us

Insurtech Insights is a global insurance technology community connecting executives, entrepreneurs, investors and innovators. Through our international conferences and media platforms, we bring together leaders shaping the future of insurance, creating opportunities to share insights, explore new technologies and build meaningful business relationships.

Insurtech Insights is part of United Media, a global B2B media and conferences group.

Start date: As soon as possible.

Monday–Friday, we work from our WeWork office in Victoria, London. Due to the collaborative nature of our work, we do not offer remote work.

You must have the right to work in the UK.

job-boards.greenhouse.io/mediahubldn/job.description_excerpt:
HELLO…We’re looking for an Account Director!

 

Who are we?

We’re Mediahub, the industry’s best kept secret. This year we got our first Campaign School Report, coming in at number one for building the most ethnically diverse team in the industry.  COMvergence rank us as the UK's fastest growing media agency for the second year running.

We bring a challenger mindset to everything we do. Brands choose to work with us to disrupt category norms.

We offer the best of both worlds.  A start-up culture backed by Mediabrands.

Just some of the brands we work with – New Balance, Pinterest, FarFetch.

You’ll be joining an agency that is for everyone.

We live by our values:

  • Anticipate tomorrow - we are challengers, we are proactive in thinking about what needs to happen today in order to make tomorrow better
  • Hustle from the heart - we move fast, take ownership, and look out for each other
  • Perform with pride - we take pride and care in what we do and we strive for excellence
  • Believe you can - believe in yourself to make a difference; believe in each other to do great things
  • Stay curious - we have fun on the journey of discovery

 

What will you do?

In this exciting role, you'll be responsible for the overall direction, development, and performance of our clients business in the DIY sector. You will be accountable for the client relationship as well as the performance and development of the team. This role covers full-service media planning and buying across Display, Paid social, TV, press, OOH & radio. 

You’ll be working with a wider team of media strategists, individual channel specialists and our data teams. We plan & buy activity across all channels working closely with specialist teams in IPG to support at key points. 

 

About You

Passionate about media & communications; you see how effective media campaigns make a real difference to a client’s business. You'll have a few years demonstrable experience in a media agency in an account handling role, being a cross channel planning/buying aficionado, with a head for numbers and a heart for creativity.

You are curious about the industry and excited about learning and continued development, bringing the same to your media plans. You'll have the ability to think strategically and look for creative solutions to briefs and commercial opportunities to grow clients. We're looking for an engineering-minded owner of the systems our Sales, Marketing and Revenue Operations teams run on: CRM, marketing automation, CPQ and the tools around them. This is not a ticket-queue role. Business teams will bring you solutions ("add a field", "build me a report"). You'll have an internal engineering team to lean on, and you'll use AI tools daily to build faster.

  • Own the GTM systems as one connected whole: know how CRM, CPQ, marketing automation and sales-engagement tools share data, and design every change with that in view.

  • Remove recurring manual work: measure the effort, then replace it with automation or self-service tools that business users run themselves.
  • Build automations, small tools and integrations, choosing the simplest approach that will hold up.
  • Keep the data model lean and trustworthy: retire unused fields and legacy workarounds, and enforce data quality where data enters rather than cleaning it up later.
  • Keep integrations reliable: use native connectors where they do the job; where something custom is needed, respect API limits, add error handling and monitoring, and keep sandbox and production consistent. Collaborate with our internal engineering team as necessary.

- Own the quality and outcomes of engagements from technical discovery and requirements gathering through solution design, implementation, launch, and handover.

Role Summary 

The Associate Director, Publishing provides strategic leadership for the PLOS journal portfolio, ensuring that portfolio priorities, publishing investments, and journal development strategies align with organizational goals and advance PLOS's mission.

The Associate Director serves as the primary steward of portfolio-wide publishing performance, translating organizational strategy into clear priorities and ensuring effective coordination across the organization. 

The Associate Director uses publishing data, financial information, market intelligence, and research community insight to guide strategic decisions, establish priorities, identify opportunities for growth and innovation, and manage risks. Working in partnership with the Director, Publishing & Publishing Operations, the Associate Director ensures that journal-level strategies collectively support a sustainable PLOS portfolio with a strong value proposition. 

Supervisory Responsibilities 

  • Lead, develop, and support a team of senior publishing professionals responsible for journal and subject portfolio performance. 
  • Establish clear goals, priorities, and measures of accountability that align with organizational and portfolio strategy. 
  • Provide coaching, professional development, succession planning, and performance management for direct reports. 
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, inclusion, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement. 
  • Work with Publishers to ensure effective leadership and development of Journal Development Managers and other publishing staff. 

Responsibilities 

Portfolio Strategy and Performance 

  • Develop and implement a portfolio-wide publishing strategy aligned with PLOS's mission and organizational objectives. 
  • Ensure that journal and subject portfolio strategies collectively support a clear and differentiated value proposition for the PLOS portfolio. 
  • Lead regular portfolio reviews and develop recommendations regarding journal positioning, growth opportunities, performance, and future direction. 
  • Balance the needs of individual journals and research communities with broader portfolio and organizational objectives. 
  • Support Publishers in identifying and responding to changes in research communities, funding policies, scholarly communication, and the publishing market.
  • Develop consistent approaches and decision-making frameworks for evaluating proposals, opportunities, and performance across the portfolio. 
  • Guide the evaluation and development of new journals, products, services, publishing models in line with PLOS’s strategic direction.  

Strategic and Business Leadership 

  • Translate organizational strategy into clear portfolio priorities, objectives, and plans for the publishing team. 
  • Oversee publishing budgets and forecasts in partnership with the Director and Publishers, ensuring responsible decision-making and effective resource allocation. 
  • Act as a thought partner to, and deputize for, the Director, Publishing & Publishing Operations when appropriate. 
  • In close collaboration with colleagues in Editorial, Sales and Global Publishing Development, support publishers in developing impactful relationships with Editors-in-Chief, Editorial Board members, researchers, institutions, societies, and partner organizations. 
  • Build productive partnerships across Editorial, Publishing Operations, Sales & Global Publishing Development, Product, Technology, Marketing, Finance, Research Integrity, and other organizational teams. 
  • Work with Editorial and Publishing Operations leaders to ensure that journal strategies are supported by effective policies, processes, services, and quality standards. 
  • Partner with Marketing and Communications to strengthen journal positioning, audience engagement, portfolio visibility, and demand generation. 

Leadership and Culture

  • Model the culture and behaviors PLOS is seeking to build, actively driving the culture change the organization needs through this transformation.

Preferred

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

Role Summary

The PLOS Publication Ethics team works to uphold the integrity and reliability of PLOS publications and supports PLOS journals in publication ethics-related issues and policy development. The team also engages with external parties and organizations in publication ethics-related discussions and initiatives.

As a Senior Editor, Publication Ethics, you investigate and resolve publication ethics cases for all PLOS journals, provide publication ethics support to PLOS journal teams, and contribute to team-level initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS.

This role is in the Publication Ethics team’s standard case group. This group’s primary case work responsibilities cover a broad array of integrity issues (e.g., image/data integrity, animal/human research ethics, authorship or data ownership disputes, etc.) that typically involve individual articles or research groups. Editors within this group may also be asked to contribute to work involving large-scale cases, as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve publication ethics cases efficiently and in line with PLOS standards and COPE guidance; provide timely support for others’ publication ethics case work; address escalations and queries about publication ethics issues; prevent reputational damage to PLOS journals as feasible.
  • Contribute as requested to tasks, cases, documentation, and other processes needed to support the team’s casework and other objectives.
  • Contribute to team-level and/or cross-functional initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS. (e.g., development of workflows or policy updates; development, trials, and/or implementation of approaches to improve detection, prevention, and/or resolution of publication ethics cases)
  • Support journal staff editors in resolving publication ethics issues that arise during manuscript handling, peer review, or post-publication.
  • Communicate rapidly and effectively about ethics cases with involved/affected stakeholders, including the journal’s editorial leads, Editorial Board members, authors, members of other PLOS teams, and any other parties involved in publication ethics case work.
  • Contribute to internal discussions about publication ethics, research integrity, and related issues in team-level and interdepartmental/cross-team forums.
  • Maintain an awareness of cross-industry issues and initiatives and attend COPE Forums that fall within your working hours.
  • Help with recruitment and onboarding for vacant team positions and help to train staff on other PLOS teams in publication ethics case management and standards. Provide training and feedback for other Publication Ethics team members as needed.
  • Uphold high standards of professionalism in all internal and external communications about publication ethics issues.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and oral
  • Highly organized and efficient self-starter with excellent attention to detail and excellent problem-solving and analytical skills
  • A collaborative team player who is comfortable working with a remote team
  • A commitment to open access and research integrity
  • Familiarity with peer review, publishing, editorial decision-making, and publication ethics issues and standards
  • Prior experience investigating and resolving publication ethics cases
  • Knowledge of Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) standards and guidance
  • (Preferred) Expertise in image forensics; experience delivering trainings

Qualifications

  • A Master’s degree or PhD (or equivalent) in a scientific discipline
  • Experience in an editorial or publication ethics role in science, technical, and medical (STM) publishing
  • First-hand experience resolving publication ethics cases in STM publishing
  • A demonstrated aptitude for critically evaluating scientific articles or publication ethics issues
  • (Preferred) Post-graduate research experience in a scientific, clinical, or social sciences discipline

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

  • Prolonged periods stationary at a desk and working on a computer
  • Some national and international travel may be required
  • Some flexibility to work across time zones

This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK. This is a 12 month FTC.

 

Role Summary

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Product team for a 12-month maternity cover contract. It's an interesting time to join us. 

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades. 

That means there are interesting product problems to solve - not just features to deliver. 

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions. 

Although this is a fixed-term role, it isn't a caretaker role. You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it. 

How we work 

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty. 

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions. 

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them. 

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something. 

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are. 

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll: 

  • Understand the problem. Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them. 
  • Shape product direction. Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities. 
  • Practise continuous discovery. Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data. 
  • Turn uncertainty into learning. Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction. 
  • Make good product decisions. Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue. 
  • Measure whether things are getting better. Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect.

job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io/raisin/jobs/.description_excerpt:
Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing. Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market.

Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns.

Team

We are seeking a strategic, highly commercial and growth-driven Chief of Staff to spearhead commercial expansion and high-priority strategic initiatives in the UK market. Sitting directly alongside the UK CEO, this role bridges establishing high-value institutional partnerships with executive-level project execution.

This is a high-leverage commercial and sales-focused Chief of Staff role - not an internal, project management or administration-focused role. Moving beyond traditional sales or purely operational roles, this position is designed for a strategic partner. You will act as the UK CEO’s right hand contributing to the long-term strategy, originating institutional partnerships and owning cross-functional strategic projects with the CEO end-to-end. A core element of this role is driving commercial growth alongside the UK CEO. This includes fully grasping the broader landscape, market and competitor dynamics, customer behaviour and regulatory context into actionable strategies for Group-level product and executive leadership.


Your Responsibilities

Strategic Business Development & Commercial Growth

  • Market & Commercial Strategy: Act as the local market strategist, translating UK client context, competitive dynamics, and customer feedback into growth opportunities and clear requirements for leadership.
  • Execute on this Strategy and Drive Partner Origination & Platform Growth: Lead business development initiatives to identify and execute commercial partnerships with banks, asset managers, wealth managers and myriad financial institutions across the UK.
  • Executive Sales Support: Partner directly with the UK CEO on complex commercial partnership negotiations.
  • Deal Structuring & Financial Modeling: Evaluate commercial frameworks, conduct quantitative modeling, and negotiate terms for strategic accounts and commercial initiatives.

Strategic Operations & Cross-Functional Execution

  • Strategic Project Management: Own and drive end-to-end execution of CEO-led strategic initiatives, ensuring cross-functional alignment across local teams and the wider Raisin Group.
  • Executive & Board Preparation: Draft strategic presentations, business cases, and commercial proposals for the UK CEO, Boards (local and Group), and Group executive management.
  • Product Roadmap Alignment: Collaborate with Group product and operational teams to champion UK commercial priorities and integrate required features into the product roadmap.
  • Structured Execution: Maintain rigorous documentation, project cadences, and operational alignment across all UK strategic priorities while navigating Risk, Compliance, and Legal clearance for new commercial structures.

Your Profile

Qualifications & Experience

  • A background in Investment Banking (especially FIG), M&A Advisory, Corporate Finance, Consulting or Strategic BD experience in financial services/fintech is highly desirable.
  • Highly analytical and proactive mindset, avoiding reactive "firefighting" in favor of methodical, structured, data-backed execution and strategic planning.

Essential Skills & Core Competencies

  • Strategic acumen: strong commercial instincts and a thorough appreciation for UK market dynamics.
  • Commercial & Financial Rigour: Strong financial modeling, valuation, contract negotiation, and analytical skills honed in high-pressure environments.
  • Stakeholder Management & Influence: Proven ability to influence, challenge, and align internal Group stakeholders, C-suite executives, and external partners.
  • Versatility: Comfortable pivoting seamlessly between financial modeling, client-facing sales meetings, and internal project coordination.
  • Communication: Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills suited for Board level interaction and external partner pitching.

 

Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us!

At Raisin, we care about each other and it is one of our top priorities to foster an open and caring environment in which everyone feels welcome and comfortable. Our culture is strongly driven by our ambitious team, which connects more than 75 different nationalities.

As part of our team, you will benefit from:

  • Employee Development Budget of £1,700 and 4 full training days per year.
  • Always hungry? Breakfast, snacks, daily fresh fruit and drinks are at your disposal around the clock.
  • We are hybrid working, we are in the office twice a week, giving the team the opportunity to collaborate and spend time together. Wednesday is our core day in the office.
  • We offer 28 days + Bank Holidays of holiday a year.
  • One day birthday leave to celebrate your birthday.
  • We offer you a company stakeholder pension with a minimum employer contribution of 5%.
  • The opportunity to experience our annual retreats in exciting European cities and other team building events.

Team

Join our team of Relationship Managers and become part of an impactful and dynamic environment. Our team plays a central role at Raisin, responsible for fostering partnerships with our platforms’ partner banks. 

As a Partnership Manager, you'll play a crucial role in driving Raisin's growth across Europe and the UK. Your primary mission is to cultivate and oversee daily interactions with Raisin's partner banks, and to lead or support managing key accounts. Beyond that, you'll spearhead the launch of new products,  integration of new banks into Raisin's and our B2B partners' marketplaces, and improving their technical integration with us to ensure scalability and the growth of the banks’ assets under management and ultimately the Raisin platform. 

With our far-reaching impact and diverse stakeholders, we have a comprehensive view of platform-wide evolutions, and others depend on your ability to communicate these changes and their broader implications. We are ultimately accountable for owning and managing our partner banks, taking direct responsibility for the performance and reporting of those partners and bringing new savings products to the consumer market.

To excel in this role, you should be adept at managing senior stakeholders, both internally and externally. We’re a high growth fintech business, so the ability to work on multiple relationships and ad-hoc projects concurrently is key.

Your Responsibilities

As a Senior Partnership Manager, you will serve as a commercial lead and strategic advisor for our portfolio of partner banks in the UK and Europe. Moving beyond traditional relationship management, this role requires a consultative, balance-sheet-first mindset to help executive banking leadership solve liquidity, capital, and deposit-funding challenges using Raisin's platform technology. 

  • C-Suite Advisory & Partner Ownership: Act as the primary strategic contact for Treasury Heads, Chief Financial Officers, and C-suite banking executives, aligning Raisin's platform capabilities with their balance sheet, liquidity, and cost-of-funding objectives.
  • Commercial Strategy & Portfolio Expansion: Proactively structure, negotiate, and execute commercial growth strategies to scale partner Assets Under Management (AUM) and launch new deposit product lines.
  • Structured Problem-Solving & Execution: Lead complex, multi-stakeholder workstreams across internal cross-functional teams (Solutions Engineering, Legal, Compliance, Operations) to ensure seamless bank onboarding and technical integrations.
  • Strategic Market Expansion: Drive priority commercial initiatives across the UK and EEA markets, identifying opportunities to launch adjacent financial products and expand strategic partner coverage.

What Success Looks Like: 

  • Executive Positioning: Establish yourself as a trusted commercial advisor to executive leadership across your assigned bank portfolio.
  • AUM & Portfolio Growth: Deliver measurable deposit growth by optimizing bank partner pricing, funding targets, and market positioning.
  • Flawless Program Execution: Successfully lead complex bank integration and product launch milestones on schedule.

Your Profile

  • Education: Top-tier Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related quantitative discipline.
  • Professional Background: 3–6+ years of experience in Management Consulting or Investment Banking (FIG background) or Strategic Partnerships within a B2B Fintech/BaaS scale-up.
  • Financial & Commercial Acumen: Strong command of bank balance sheets, deposit mechanics, regulatory frameworks, and commercial deal structuring.
  • Structured Communication & Executive Presence: Exceptional capability to translate complex financial and technical concepts into structured executive presentations for bank leaders.
  • Project & Stakeholder Ownership: Demonstrated track record of leading complex, multi-variable projects autonomously in fast-paced environments.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Direct experience with UK/EEA banking regulations (FCA, BaFin), liquidity coverage ratios (LCR), or BaaS/Open Banking infrastructure.
  • Transaction, M&A, treasury, or advisory experience working directly with UK and European retail or commercial banks.

AI runs through how our teams work, and we help clients adopt it into their own workflows too.

We're building out data as a first-class practice at YLD, and we need someone in London who can be the credible technical voice in front of clients and prospects, not just describing what we could do, but backing it with real delivery experience.

This is a senior role, reporting to our Head of Engineering. You'll sit alongside our commercial and client services leadership in meetings where technical credibility matters, help shape and win new engagements, and stay close enough to client work to guide it and step in yourself when an engagement needs you. Alongside, we expect you to build our external reputation in data through events, writing, and the wider community.

About you:

You've been a strong data engineer or data lead for years, and you're comfortable in front of a client as well as in a pull request. You know what good data work looks like well enough to spot it, or its absence, in the first ten minutes of a client conversation. You've probably led a team before. Consultancy background is a strong plus, but not essential if you've got real client or stakeholder exposure elsewhere.

Your day-to-day responsibilities will look like this:

Hands-on delivery (core, from day one)

  • Doing hands-on data engineering work directly, pipelines, transformation layers, models, and the infrastructure around them, not just guiding others
  • Adapting to different client contexts: legacy warehouse migrations, greenfield lakehouses, transformation layers that need rescuing
  • Guiding the wider team and unblocking hard technical problems as your remit grows beyond your own delivery
  • Defining and evolving our internal standards for data work: testing, documentation, project structure, code review
  • Mentoring and growing data engineers across the company

Client and commercial (core, from day one)

  • Joining client and prospect meetings as the technical authority on data, alongside our client services and commercial leads
  • Shaping proposals and pitches, translating client problems into a credible data approach and a defensible scope
  • Acting as the escalation point on live data engagements when technical judgement calls need weight behind them
  • Travelling to client sites for workshops, discovery sessions, and in-person relationship building, and representing YLD at external data events

Practice, talent, and external profile (growth, over the first year)

  • Owning the growth of YLD's data practice: capability, reputation, and headcount over time
  • Contributing to attracting and hiring strong data engineers into YLD
  • Representing YLD at data events and in the wider community as your standing in the market builds
  • Supporting our sales team so that data becomes something we can proactively sell, not just respond to

You'll have the following skills and experience:

Leadership and commercial

  • Consulting or agency experience is a strong plus, but real client or stakeholder-facing exposure elsewhere is acceptable
  • A track record of technical leadership: leading a team or function
  • Comfortable presenting to senior client stakeholders and holding your own under commercial pressure
  • Cross-functional fluency: you translate engineering constraints into business terms and negotiate realistic commitments
  • Appetite to build a public presence in the data community over time, even if you don't have one yet

Technical

Not theoretical, evidenced by things you've actually shipped, and deep enough to set the bar for a team and answer a sceptical client:

  • SQL as engineering: read and review SQL that performs at scale, and understand query planning, engine quirks, and how materialisation choices affect cost and performance well enough to guide a team's decisions
  • Python for data: built and maintained production data systems in typed, testable Python, not just notebooks, and can set that standard for others
  • Data modelling: made deliberate choices between dimensional, Data Vault, normalised and denormalised designs, and can explain the trade-offs in flexibility, query performance, and maintainability to both engineers and clients
  • Transformation architecture: design transformations that are idempotent, incremental, and dependency-aware. You think in DAGs, not scripts
  • Pipeline design: weigh batch, streaming, and micro-batch trade-offs against latency, complexity, cost, and reprocessability, and pick the right approach for the problem
  • Data testing: know what to catch at build time (schema contracts, assertions, transformation logic) versus defer to observability, and can make that call for a team
  • Data observability: treat data reliability like site reliability, with measurable indicators, alerting, incident response, and root cause analysis
  • CI/CD for data: version, test, and deploy pipelines like software, with environment promotion, rollback strategies, and infrastructure as code
  • Data governance: implemented lineage, cataloguing, sensitive data classification, or access control, and can hold a client to account on making data auditable and secure
  • Cost-conscious: optimised warehouse spend, storage strategies, or job efficiency, and treat compute as a resource to manage, not ignore
  • Platform fluency: worked across orchestration (Airflow, Dagster), warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), ingestion (Fivetran, Airbyte, custom), and transformation (dbt, Spark)
  • AI Native: experienced in agentic coding workflows (context, harness, loop, and graph engineering), and able to embed AI Engineering constructs into pipelines (RAG, semantic search, evals, guardrails, etc)

You should apply if:

  • Confident and credible in front of clients and prospects, without needing a script, and comfortable holding a firm technical or commercial line when a client or prospect pushes back
  • Still able to hold up in a deep technical review today, architecture, data modelling, pipeline design, not just talk about decisions you made a few years ago
  • Self-motivated, and want to own building a practice, not just execute a workstream…
