job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io/tavily/jobs/.description_excerpt:
The Team

Forward Deployed Engineering owns how Tavily shows up technically in the field. The team sits at the intersection of customers, Product, Engineering, Sales, Partnerships, and Customer Success. 

The Enterprise FDE motion focuses on Tavily’s highest-value customers and strategic enterprise opportunities — from technical discovery and solution design through proof of concept, production rollout, adoption, and expansion. 

The role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, Enterprise, you’ll work directly with Tavily’s largest and most strategic customers to design, prototype, and deploy production-grade AI systems powered by Tavily’s API. You’ll own the technical relationship across the customer lifecycle, helping enterprise teams move from early use case exploration to deployed, scalable agentic applications. 

You’ll be deeply hands-on: building RAG pipelines, agent workflows, evaluation loops, reference architectures, and custom integrations alongside customer teams. You’ll also serve as a critical bridge between the field and our Product and Engineering teams, translating enterprise needs into roadmap signal. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Work directly with enterprise customers to understand their AI use cases, technical architecture, success criteria, and deployment requirements. 
  • Lead technical discovery and solution design during pre-sales and expansion conversations. 
  • Scope, build, and deliver proofs of concept that demonstrate clear business and technical value. 
  • Design and implement production-ready integrations using Tavily’s API, including RAG pipelines, agent workflows, internal tools, and industry-specific GenAI applications. 
  • Partner with customer engineering, data, product, and AI teams to move use cases from prototype to production. 
  • Monitor customer API usage patterns and recommend improvements to increase reliability, latency, coverage, and overall value. 
  • Translate recurring customer needs, blockers, and technical patterns into clear product and roadmap input. 
  • Create reusable enterprise assets, including reference architectures, integration templates, deployment guides, demo environments, and technical documentation. 
  • Represent Tavily in customer architecture reviews, executive technical conversations, implementation check-ins, and post-deployment reviews. 
  • Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering to drive adoption, retention, and expansion across strategic accounts. 

We expect you to have: 

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, ideally in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Sales Engineer, or Technical Consultant. 
  • Strong hands-on engineering ability, especially with Python, APIs, backend systems, and production software development. 
  • Experience building with LLMs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, agent architectures, context engineering, and modern AI application stacks. 
  • Experience working with enterprise customers, including technical discovery, POCs, solution design, stakeholder management, and production rollout. 
  • Strong understanding of how enterprises evaluate, deploy, secure, and scale AI systems. 
  • Ability to communicate clearly with both technical and executive stakeholders, including engineering leaders, product teams, AI teams, and technical decision-makers. 
  • High autonomy, strong ownership, and comfort operating in a fast-moving startup environment. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex technical concepts into clear recommendations. 

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

  • Experience working with major agent or LLM orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, or CrewAI. 
  • Experience with vector databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Qdrant, or similar systems. 
  • Experience with enterprise AI use cases in financial services, legal, consulting, enterprise SaaS, sales, marketing, or internal knowledge management. 
  • Track record helping large customers move from POC to production. 
  • Experience building internal tools, technical playbooks, demos, or reusable customer-facing assets. 
  • Prior experience at a high-growth AI infrastructure, developer tools, or enterprise SaaS company.

The role

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.

We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.

When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.

The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.

The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week. Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Set the quality bar and release criteria for search: what good means per use case, and what a change has to clear before it ships. Our evaluation team owns the measurement, and you work closely with them on what to measure and why.
  • Own the depth, latency, and cost tradeoffs across our search products, and make them explicit and defensible.
  • Shape the direction of our index: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what quality bar it has to meet.
  • Build a point of view on where search infrastructure is going as agents, rather than people, become the main consumer, and turn that into a roadmap.
  • Know how we compare to the alternatives customers evaluate, and drive the work that closes the gaps that matter.
  • Work with customer success and directly with customers to understand where our results fall short in real workflows, and turn that into quality priorities.
  • Partner with the data and vertical product owners on what our corpus needs to contain and how results should be shaped per industry.

We expect you to have: 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion spent on high-scale search or ranking systems: web search, feed ranking at a large social platform, or a large ad engine.
  • A background as an engineer, ML engineer, or researcher on a production system in one of those areas. This is a requirement rather than a preference. You will be making tradeoff calls alongside senior search engineers, and you need to have built something at that scale yourself.
  • Direct experience shipping a search or ranking change end to end, including how it was evaluated and what happened after it shipped.
  • A strong data foundation: you can design an experiment, read eval results critically, and tell a real quality improvement from noise.
  • Product judgment to match the technical depth: you can decide what to build and what to leave, and defend it to both engineers and customers.
  • Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how retrieval fits into agentic workflows.
  • Comfort with ambiguity, moving between strategy and execution without losing the thread.
  • The ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

  • Depth in information retrieval, NLP, or applied machine learning beyond what the role requires.
  • Experience with index tiering, sharding, freshness pipelines, or cost-per-query optimisation at scale.
  • Experience with hybrid retrieval, semantic and lexical search, re-ranking, or human evaluation programs.
  • Experience in API-first or developer-platform businesses running both self-serve and enterprise motions.
  • Experience in a high-growth technology company, especially post-acquisition or startup-within-a-larger-org environments.

The role

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.

Vertical search is where we combine public sources with premium vertical data and shape the result into a product for a specific use case. This role owns that layer end to end. You decide which industries and use cases we productize. With the data team, you find and evaluate the public and premium data providers behind each one. You shape the product surface that sits on top.

You will sit with customers in these industries, learn how they actually work, and turn their needs and pain points into clear specs. You will build with engineering, ship it, and make sure go-to-market knows how to sell it. You own the outcome, not just the handoff: from the first market call through to adoption and revenue.

The hard part is choosing. There are more verticals worth building than we can build, and the difference between a good year and a wasted one is knowing which ones to invest in and which to walk away from, even when a large customer is asking for another.

In your first year, we expect you to know our top use cases better than anyone here, ship a product built for one of them that customers will pay more for, and have a defensible view of what comes next.

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership. You will work within a small PM team reporting to the Director of Product, alongside engineering, research, data, and go-to-market.

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Own the vertical roadmap. You decide where we invest, what we ship for each, and when a vertical is not worth it.
  • Shape the product surface on top of the data, so a customer gets something built for their job.
  • Find and evaluate the data behind each vertical, across public sources and paid providers, and decide what is worth investing in.
  • Sit with customers in these industries until you understand their workflow, then turn that into specs engineering can build.
  • Set what a good answer looks like in each use case, working with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it.
  • Work with customer success to learn what customers ask us for and what makes them leave.
  • Partner with the search owner on how results should be ranked and shaped for each use case.

We expect you to have: 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion in search, data, or industry-specific AI products.
  • Experience building products for a specific industry or use case, combined with enough technical depth to work directly on the data underneath: where it comes from, how good it is, and what it takes to make it usable.
  • A track record of real customer discovery: you have gone deep on how a particular kind of team works, and shipped something because of what you found.
  • Experience in API-first or developer-platform businesses.
  • Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how search and retrieval systems fit into agentic workflows.
  • A technical background, through a degree in computer science or engineering or equivalent hands-on experience, with the ability to engage deeply with technical architecture and tradeoffs.
  • The ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

  • Domain experience in market intelligence, news, financial research, or another data-heavy industry.
  • Background at a data provider, enrichment vendor, market intelligence platform, or vertical search company, or experience building vertical data products in-house.
  • Experience evaluating and working with external data providers, including judging quality and negotiating what you actually need.
  • Leadership experience in a high-growth technology company, especially post-acquisition or startup-within-a-larger-org environments.

About Tavily 

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. By connecting LLMs to high-quality, trustworthy web content, we help developers build agents that are not only intelligent — but also informed. 

We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI — from small startups shaping the ecosystem to the largest enterprises deploying AI at scale. Whether it's powering sales assistants, research copilots, or internal knowledge tools, we're the missing link between LLMs and the real world. 

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the web access infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on making our access to public web content reliable and efficient. You will investigate how modern websites and browsers communicate across the full request lifecycle, find the root cause when a request fails or returns something unexpected, and build the fixes into production systems operating at internet scale. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the crawling, indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

  • Diagnose failed or degraded requests at the right layer: network and IP, TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, headers and session state, client-side scripts, or browser characteristics
  • Analyze how websites verify and classify clients, including how client-side scripts and protocol-level behavior shape what a site serves to different clients
  • Build clients and tooling that behave consistently and compatibly with standard browsers across all of these layers, using a real browser where a lightweight client is not enough
  • Monitor access quality as websites change: detect regressions, find the cause, and measure success on real content rather than on status codes
  • Build the tooling to do this at scale: traffic capture and comparison against real browsers, per-site and per-method success tracking, and the cost of each successful fetch
  • Choose the fetch method for each host, from a lightweight HTTP client to a full browser, balancing quality against cost

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

The request lifecycle

  • HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, TLS handshakes and TLS fingerprints (JA3/JA4), and header behavior
  • What a server can observe at each step of a request, and what a client controls at each step
  • A debugging method, not guesses: replaying captured browser traffic, comparing against a real browser on the same network path, and changing one variable at a time

Client-side analysis

  • Reading and analyzing complex or obfuscated JavaScript, and observing what a script measures by hooking browser APIs
  • How browser, device and network characteristics are measured (canvas, fonts, WebGL, screen and window metrics) and how consistent they are across layers
  • Browser instrumentation and the Chrome DevTools Protocol, used as tools for investigation

Running it for real

  • Have run this in production and can give numbers: requests per day, sites or hosts, and the success rate and how you measured it
  • Strong programming in at least one of Go, Python, Rust or C++

Strong candidates may also have experience with

  • Working at a web data provider, a browser or web-security company, or a company that collects data from complex sources
  • Contributions to browser networking or fingerprinting-related open-source tooling, or public write-ups of how client verification works
  • Building or maintaining a patched browser
  • Networks, proxies and IP reputation
  • Internet-scale distributed systems, Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure

The kind of problems you will work on

  • A site returns a different response to our client than to Chrome on the same network path. Find out why, and fix that cause.
  • A site changes how it verifies clients and success drops across a group of sites. Find what changed, adapt, and make the next change cheaper to catch.
  • Switching to a browser-like network profile makes results worse on some hosts. Work out what no longer matches.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

About Tavily 

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. By connecting LLMs to high-quality, trustworthy web content, we help developers build agents that are not only intelligent — but also informed. 

We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI — from small startups shaping the ecosystem to the largest enterprises deploying AI at scale. Whether it's powering sales assistants, research copilots, or internal knowledge tools, we're the missing link between LLMs and the real world. 

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the rendering infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on loading modern web pages in a browser that we patch and build ourselves, so that content is rendered completely and reliably at a cost that works across billions of pages. You will work inside Chromium to remove what we do not need, make the rest faster and cheaper, and keep our build current as Chromium moves. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

  • Change Chromium in its heavy core (Blink, the V8 integration, the compositor, the network service) to cut CPU, memory and startup cost per page
  • Strip Chromium down for agent workloads: skip what nobody needs, such as image and media decoding, web font downloads, and rasterization and GPU work where no one needs pixels, while keeping what page scripts depend on to run correctly (style, layout, animation frames, observers), and work out what breaks, or renders differently, when you do
  • Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render
  • Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling
  • Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser

  • Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)
  • Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service
  • Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems

  • Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs
  • Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management
  • Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with

  • Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine
  • Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for
  • Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol
  • Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)
  • Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on

  • Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?
  • Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?
  • A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?
  • Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?
  • Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

Yondr Group, a global developer, owner and operator of hyperscale data centres, is seeking an experienced lawyer to support its growing EMEA business. Reporting to the Legal Director EMEA, the successful candidate will act as the primary legal adviser to Yondr's design, construction and operations teams across the EMEA region.

The role will support the full project lifecycle, from development, procurement and financing through construction, completion and operations. The successful candidate will work closely with project delivery, commercial, procurement and operational teams, supporting projects involving a range of delivery models, funding structures and stakeholders, including customers, lenders, investors, contractors, consultants, utility providers and suppliers.

The role will be expected to operate independently on day-to-day matters, leading legal support across Yondr's EMEA construction and operations portfolio whilst managing legal risk and stakeholder requirements. This includes ensuring project documentation appropriately reflects contractual, leasing, funding and other stakeholder requirements.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Qualified solicitor with 6+ years' PQE with significant experience in primarily non-contentious construction, infrastructure, energy or data centre projects (preferred).
  • Have trained at a reputable law firm or within the legal function of a reputable data centre, construction, infrastructure, energy or technology business.
  • Experience negotiating and managing complex procurement, construction. supply and services agreements, including familiarity with FIDIC-based contracting.
  • Experience advising on complex projects involving multiple stakeholders, funding structures and jurisdictions, including management of external counsel where required.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Act as the primary legal business partner for Yondr's design, construction and operations teams across EMEA, leading legal support across the procurement, construction and operation of Yondr's data centre portfolio.
  • Attend and lead weekly project, commercial, procurement and operational meetings and provide practical legal support on live matters.
  • Lead negotiations of Heads of Terms, D&B and other works agreements, consultant appointments, framework agreements and other key project and commercial documentation (including PCGs, Bonds, CWs).
  • Coordinate investor, lender, customer and other stakeholder contractual requirements (including funders' requirements around ancillary and security documents such as collateral warranties, PCGs and bonds) with internal stakeholders and external counsel, ensuring that project documentation appropriately reflects upstream obligations, leasing and project-specific requirements.

  • Support the development of legal processes, governance standards and risk management frameworks across the business, including driving contract lifecycle automation and the continued implementation and utilisation of Ironclad as Yondr's contract management platform.

Requirements

  • Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a complex and diverse workload under tight and competing deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to deliver clear, concise and actionable legal advice.

Strength in Trust 

OneTrust’s mission is to enable innovation through the responsible use of data and AI. We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‑Ready Governance Platform™, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society. 

The Challenge

We’re looking for a Senior Principal Solutions Engineer to shape and lead technical strategy for OneTrust’s most strategic and complex opportunities in the UK & Ireland. Reporting to the Solutions Engineering Manager, you will bring broad portfolio fluency, deep enterprise technology expertise, executive-level customer engagement, and commercial judgement to help customers solve business-critical challenges with OneTrust.

You will partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Engineering and partners to build deep account alignment, progress complex buying decisions, and create measurable customer and commercial outcomes. You will be a trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders and a force multiplier for the Solutions Engineering organisation: setting s high bar, developing reusable approaches, and coaching others to raise the quality of our work. AI Governance is an important area of expertise for this role, alongside the breadth to lead opportunities across OneTrust’s entire platform.

Your Mission

  • Lead technical strategy for the highest-impact, most complex opportunities across OneTrust’s solutions portfolio, aligning the customer’s business priorities, technology environment, risk posture, architecture and decision process to the right OneTrust solutions and measurable outcomes. Bring particular depth in AI Governance where relevant to the customer’s needs.
  • Build deep account alignment with Account Executives, Customer Success and other partners. Map the buying group and executive sponsors; understand account priorities and whitespace; and shape a coordinated, multi-stakeholder motion that advances the opportunity and contributes to sustainable ACV growth. Partner with the commercial account owners on expansion strategy; this role does not replace their ownership of the customer relationship.
  • Engage credibly with executive and practitioner stakeholders—including CIO/CTO, CISO, Chief AI and Data leaders, Privacy, Legal, Risk, Security, Procurement, and AI/ML Engineering—to connect governance requirements with business value and delivery realities.
  • Lead discovery and solution design for complex enterprise programmes across relevant OneTrust solution areas, translating fragmented requirements, regulatory obligations and technical constraints into practical, scalable operating models, architectures and workflows.
  • Bring deep technical expertise in OneTrust’s solutions, enterprise integrations and the technology ecosystems relevant to each opportunity. Advise on APIs, data flows, identity and access, cloud and platform architecture, and—where relevant—AI/ML lifecycles and operational controls; identify risks and dependencies early; and recommend implementable designs.
  • Lead tailored demonstrations, technical evaluations, proofs of concept, RFP responses and executive presentations across the portfolio. Set clear success criteria, prove technical fit and business value, and use evaluation outcomes to build stakeholder confidence and progress the sales motion.
  • Articulate OneTrust’s differentiated value and position solutions thoughtfully against alternatives, connecting customer requirements to the most relevant solution capabilities, integrations and roadmap—including AI Governance where applicable—without overpromising.
  • Act as a strategic bridge between the field and Product, Engineering, Marketing and leadership. Bring structured customer and competitive insight to inform product direction, positioning, packaging and go-to-market strategy.
  • Create reusable solution patterns, account-planning practices, demos, technical guidance and field assets that improve consistency and outcomes beyond an individual opportunity.
  • Coach and mentor Solutions Engineers and cross-functional partners in portfolio knowledge, strategic discovery, technical storytelling, executive engagement and complex deal execution, sharing AI Governance expertise where relevant.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity strategy, technical risks, evaluation plans and next steps in Salesforce, in partnership with the account team.

What Success Looks Like

  • You are a trusted technical and strategic partner on the business’s most consequential opportunities across OneTrust’s solutions portfolio, improving deal progression and technical win outcomes.
  • You build durable alignment across customer executives, practitioners and the OneTrust account team, connecting the right OneTrust solutions to funded priorities and demonstrable business value—including AI Governance where relevant.
  • Your work contributes to healthy ACV growth by helping account teams identify, shape and win the right strategic opportunities.
  • Customers see a credible path from their business priorities to operational outcomes, with connected, secure, scalable and realistic recommendations across the relevant OneTrust solutions.
  • You raise the capability of the wider organisation through thought leadership, repeatable approaches, coaching and actionable customer insight.

You Are

  • A strategic, customer-led thinker who starts with outcomes and discovery, navigates ambiguity, and exercises sound judgement rather than defaulting to a product pitch or a standard playbook.
  • Commercially astute: you understand how complex enterprise buying decisions are made, how technical strategy affects deal outcomes, and how to create mutual value without compromising customer trust.
  • An executive-level communicator who can move from technical depth to a concise business narrative, influence senior decision-makers, and adapt to different audiences.
  • A broad portfolio strategist and a credible AI Governance expert, with a strong, current point of view on the AI landscape, associated technologies…

Location: UK (Hybrid)
Practice: Data & AI

About HSO

HSO is a Business Transformation Partner with deep industry expertise and global reach. As one of Microsoft's leading partners, we help organisations unlock the full potential of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure, Data and AI technologies to deliver meaningful business outcomes.

With operations across Europe, North America and Asia, HSO combines industry knowledge, technical excellence and a people-first culture to help customers modernise their businesses, transform operations and embrace innovation with confidence.

As demand for Data & AI solutions continues to accelerate, we're expanding our Data & AI practice and looking for experienced Cloud Solution Architects to help shape the next generation of customer transformation programmes.

The Role

As a Cloud Solution Architect - Data & AI, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping and qualifying customer opportunities across the Microsoft cloud ecosystem.

This is a highly visible role that sits at the intersection of sales, enterprise architecture and delivery, combining technical leadership with commercial thinking. You'll work closely with customers, Microsoft and internal stakeholders to understand business challenges, identify opportunities, design compelling solutions and create clear pathways from initial discovery through to successful delivery.

You'll help organisations transform the way they use data, analytics and artificial intelligence, translating business ambition into practical, costed and deliverable solutions.

Success in this role requires more than technical expertise. You'll need strong consulting and stakeholder management skills, the confidence to challenge assumptions, and the commercial awareness to ensure opportunities are both valuable for clients and aligned with HSO's delivery capability.

What You'll Be Doing

Opportunity Qualification & Solution Shaping

  • Lead Data & AI opportunity qualification alongside Account Managers, Business Development teams and Enterprise Architects.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical capability with exceptional commercial awareness.

You'll be equally comfortable discussing board-level business outcomes with executive stakeholders as you are diving into architecture decisions with technical teams.

Deployment Strategist

About HSO

HSO is a global Business Transformation Partner with deep industry expertise and a long standing strategic relationship with Microsoft. We help organisations unlock the full potential of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure, Data and AI technologies to modernise operations, accelerate innovation and deliver meaningful business outcomes.

In 2026, HSO achieved Microsoft Frontier Partner status, recognising our advanced capabilities across Microsoft Cloud and AI and our ability to help customers move beyond AI experimentation into secure, governed, enterprise scale production.

With operations across Europe, North America and Asia, we combine industry knowledge, technical excellence and a practical, people first approach to transformation.

As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we’re building a new generation of customer facing talent to help organisations identify where AI can create genuine business value and turn that potential into measurable outcomes.

About the Role

AI is creating significant opportunities for organisations, but identifying where it can genuinely transform a business is often harder than building the technology itself.

That is where the Deployment Strategist comes in.

Deployment Strategists combine elements of management consulting, product management, business analysis and technology strategy. Their primary responsibility is to understand a customer’s business deeply enough to identify where the greatest value can be created, where the most important problems exist, and where AI and agentic technologies can realistically help solve them.

You’ll work closely with senior customer stakeholders to understand strategic priorities, operating models, processes and performance challenges before translating them into focused opportunities that can be delivered and measured.

You will also need a strong understanding of the Microsoft technology platform and its evolving AI stack. This is not a hands on engineering role, but you should understand how capabilities across Microsoft Azure, Data, AI, Microsoft Fabric, Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform and Dynamics 365 can be applied to business problems and how those technologies fit together.

This technical understanding will allow you to identify realistic opportunities, challenge assumptions, work credibly with technical teams and help customers make informed choices about where Microsoft technologies can create the greatest value.

Deployment Strategists work side by side with Forward Deployed Engineers. The Deployment Strategist owns the why and the what, identifying the opportunity, defining the desired outcome and establishing how success will be measured. The FDE owns the how, designing and building the production solution.

Together, you will take opportunities from discovery through to production and demonstrate the value they create.

A critical part of the role is proving impact. jobs.ashbyhq.com/epistemix/5577f373-38c4.description_excerpt:
Our software engineers at Epistemix show a clear passion for quality and love to bring software to life. You are energized by the idea of building something new and want to work on problems that matter.
In order to do this job well, you must be a curious and eager problem solver with a hunger for building well-designed, high-quality solutions. You have a passion for great work and strive to produce simple solutions to complex problems. Knowing there are always multiple answers to a problem, you know how to engage in a constructive dialogue to find the best path forward.
ABOUT EPISTEMIX
The most consequential decisions in public health, life sciences, insurance, and enterprise strategy share a common problem: they involve human behavior, network effects, and downstream effects that cannot be safely tested before action is taken. Traditional analytical techniques built on historical data were not built for this. Epistemix was.
We build simulation and data-driven modeling tools that let leaders visualize how strategies will unfold across populations and systems before they commit resources. By clarifying which variables drive outcomes, where leverage exists, and how they interact, we help organizations move from uncertainty to conviction. Getting these decisions right means faster interventions, better-allocated resources, and measurable improvements in human and economic outcomes. We exist to make that possible.
Our platform gives organizations access to realistic, high-resolution population data and the modeling infrastructure to run scenario planning at scale. Together, these capabilities let decision-makers stress-test strategies in a controlled environment before deploying them in the real world across healthcare, consumer industries, insurance, and government. We are approaching our Series B and actively building the team that will define what comes next.
RESPONSIBILITIES
As a Senior Back-End Software Engineer, you will be at the forefront of our product's evolution. Your key responsibilities will include:
- Design, develop, and maintain clean, testable, and highly maintainable code, ensuring top-tier performance and reliability.
- From initial requirements gathering to deployment and ongoing maintenance, take full ownership of the software development lifecycle, ensuring seamless delivery and operation.
- Design, build, test and deploy a highly scalable and resilient system architecture that supports current needs and future growth.
- Define the technical direction for engineering solutions, actively collaborating with internal teams to ensure technological advancements are perfectly aligned with the company's strategic goals.
QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related field, or equivalent work experience
- 7+ years of back-end software development experience,with a significant portion in a senior role.
- Expert proficiency in Python, particularly with FastAPI.
- Strong experience with TypeScript for backend development (Node.js/NestJS experience is a plus).
- Deep hands-on experience with AWS cloud services, including but not limited to EC2, EKS, Lambda, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, CloudWatch, and IAM.
- Proven experience designing, building, and operating microservices architectures.
- Extensive experience with Kubernetes for container orchestration.
- Expertise in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform.
- Hands-on experience with Atlantis for Terraform pull request automation.
- Demonstrated experience or strong understanding of data science orchestration platforms, such as Prefect.io http://Prefect.io.
- Solid understanding of relational and NoSQL databases, including advanced querying, optimization, and data modeling.
- Experience with API design principles (RESTful, GraphQL) and security best practices (OAuth2, JWT).
- Strong understanding of distributed systems concepts, asynchronous processing, and message queues.
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins).
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, agile environment.
WHY JOIN EPISTEMIX?
By joining Epistemix, you will become part of a collaborative and rapidly growing team that values curiosity and creativity. We are fully remote, with team members in the United States and Europe. Benefits include:
- Equity & Incentives – Participation in our stock option program.
- Flexible Time Off – Autonomy to manage your schedule and work-life balance.
- Health, Welfare and 401(k) Programs – Eligibility for benefits (for U.S. employees).
- Meaningful Impact – Apply your creative talents to revolutionize data-driven decision-making and make a real-world difference.
This is a remote position open to applicants located in the United States. Candidates must possess the legal right to work in their intended work location, as we are currently unable to sponsor or transfer employment visas for any country, including the United States.

As an Account Executive, you’ll join our Sales team and run full-cycle sales across your territory in EMEA. This is your chance to help build a category-defining company at an exciting point in its evolution. jobs.ashbyhq.com/ravio/e10e443b-57c8-445.description_excerpt:
ABOUT US
Compensation is one of the key levers for attracting and retaining great talent, yet most companies are struggling to get it right. They simply have no choice but to rely on poor data and unsophisticated tools for their pay decisions. That's why we created Ravio.
We help some of the world's most innovative and ambitious companies build stronger teams and reach their goals through better compensation. Our goal is to bring compensation into the modern age by building the ultimate real-time compensation solution. We're passionate about ensuring everyone is paid what they deserve, no matter their background or circumstances. We believe that when compensation is done right, everyone wins.
Ravio is growing fast, which means you can too. Joining a startup in the early days and scaling it into a global product is one of the most challenging and rewarding experiences a career can offer. If that sounds exciting to you, you're in the right place.
THE ROLE
We're hiring Ravio's first dedicated Legal Counsel, someone who brings strong privacy expertise. You'll own our core legal documentation, from customer contracts to data processing terms and privacy notices, and be the main point of contact for our external legal support. You'll be a key stakeholder for Ravio's senior leadership team, advising on a wide range of legal and regulatory matters, and you'll work closely with our Commercial, Product, People and Data teams to keep Ravio's legal position current as the product and business grow. You'll also be a named contact in governance processes such as our whistleblowing framework.
Alongside the core legal remit, you'll roll up your sleeves on some of our compliance operations too, including supporting our annual SOC 2 audit and other compliance projects as they come up. This suits someone equally comfortable drafting a contract and working through the details of an audit.
This is a broad, hands-on role for someone who wants ownership from day one. You'll work independently for a lot of it, backed by an external law firm retainer for specialist and overflow work, and you'll have real scope to shape how the legal and compliance function grows at Ravio as we scale.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Contracts and commercial
- Oversee Ravio’s corporate actions (shareholder and investors matters, board documentation, stock plan admin, M&A/licensing deals, etc)
- Handle employment-related legal matters
- Keep our Service Agreement, DPA and Custom Data Terms current against live operations, product changes and bespoke customer requirements, acting as a thought partner to the commercial team
- Own the Contract Amendments Tracker, logging liability and exposure on bespoke terms
- Provide legal review of the corporate and commercial sections of our contracting workflow, and sense-check bespoke order forms
Data protection and privacy
- Confirm our Technical and Organisational Measures (TOMs) and Data Processing Provisions (DPPs) stay accurate against live data flows and product changes, working closely with the tech team
- Keep our Privacy Policy current as the website and platform evolve
- Update candidate and employee privacy notices as our recruitment and HR processes change
- Review and maintain our DPIA and ROPA as the product evolves
Governance and external relationships
- Act as a named recipient for Ravio's whistleblowing process
- Maintain our trademark records
- Own the relationship with our external legal counsel for ad-hoc and ongoing legal support
- Confirm ICO registration renewal each year
Compliance & audit support
- Coordinate our SOC 2 (and ISO, where relevant) certification cycle: line up the auditor and timeline, and manage Vanta audit access
- Own day-to-day Vanta administration: policy reviews, joiner/leaver checks, vendor and risk reviews
- Triage due diligence and security questionnaires from Sales beyond our self-serve materials
- Support other compliance projects as they come up, such as our data deletion and anonymisation process improvements
ABOUT YOU
- Qualified solicitor (England & Wales) or equivalent, with a few years' PQE: not fresh out of a training contract, but this isn't a senior or lead position either
- Strong working knowledge of UK/EU data protection and privacy law (UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018) and how it applies to a B2B SaaS product
- Genuinely happy to work on hands-on compliance and audit operations alongside legal work, not just advisory work
- Comfortable drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial contracts, DPAs and customer terms with minimal oversight
- A pragmatic, commercial approach: you know when to push back and when to find a workable middle ground
- Confident managing an external counsel relationship and getting the most out of a retainer
- Strong stakeholder management skills; you can translate legal and compliance risk into plain terms for non-legal teams
- Comfortable being the sole in-house legal hire, at least initially, and happy to build process rather than inherit it
NICE TO HAVE
- Familiarity with SOC 2/ISO frameworks or GRC tools such as Vanta (or a fast willingness to learn them)
- A recognised privacy qualification (e.g. IAPP CIPP/E), though not required
- Experience with DORA or other cross-border regulatory frameworks
- In-house experience at a SaaS or technology business
COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
- £65,000 – £85,000

About Antithesis
We've been quietly reinventing how the world thinks about software reliability, and we're just getting started! At Antithesis, we start at the foundations – we run entire software systems inside a deterministic simulation and break them in every way imaginable. Every issue then comes with a perfect reproduction, so you can identify root causes fast instead of spending days trying to recreate what went wrong.
The rise of AI-generated code has made this work more urgent than ever. Agents can write code faster than any human, but speed doesn't matter much when the output is buggy, stuck in review, or slipping through undetected. The verification bottleneck is real, it's growing, and solving it is one of the most consequential problems in software right now. That's what you'd be working on.
We're well-funded and deeply technical, the kind of place where the hardest problems get the most attention and the best ideas win regardless of who has them. If you want to do work that actually moves the needle on how reliable software can be, keep reading.
About the Role
We're looking for engineers in the Senior to Staff levels to build the future of autonomous testing. No matter your particular field of experience, if you've been ambitiously building complex software and think you could be a fit; drop us a note.
In this role you will be part of the team that maintains our open-source project Bombadil (https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil). This includes working with the specification language and verifier, Chromium automation, advanced property-based testing, frontend development, and much more.
Must have for this role:
- Proficient in Rust development
- Experience with property-based testing or fuzzing
- Comfortable with web technology (browsers, HTTP, HTML, Javascript, CSS)
Experience that would be a plus:
- Chrome Devtools Protocol, Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium
- Formal specification languages (e.g. TLA+ or some LTL)
- Implementing parsers, type systems, and interpreters
About Our Team
Our team spans CS degrees, philosophy, mathematics, and everything in between, or nothing formal at all. What everyone shares is a high bar for engineering quality. We work in-person because it's how we build trust and tackle hard problems together.
Location: This position is full time in the office in London, UK.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/antithesis/59bf67f1-78d.description_excerpt:

We’re on a mission to redefine how modern distributed systems are tested and released. Our platform is trusted by engineering teams who demand rock-solid reliability, scalable performance, and deep technical visibility. Our platform doesn’t just assure system correctness and reliability, it exists because developers need something better. jobs.ashbyhq.com/slingshotai/994b40ca-31.description_excerpt:
Slingshot AI
Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.
We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.
Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.
We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.
The role
We are seeking a Creative Strategy Lead to join the Slingshot AI marketing team. Reporting to our head of growth, your job is to identify, create, test, and scale our D2C creative motion. Millions of people already use general purpose AI as a therapist, and millions more are on a waitlist or priced out of care. Demand is not our problem. Getting Ash in front of the people who need it is. Creative is the biggest lever we have on that, and this role owns it.
This is a hands-on role by design. You own the loop, coming up with creative copy, producing visuals and tag-lines, and iterating quickly to dial in on what works. You are building the engine that gets Ash in front of people. You create and test fast, trust your instincts, and want to develop the playbook that puts proper mental healthcare at the world's fingertips.
Key responsibilities:
- Own the weekly experiment loop: hypothesis, A/B test, read the result, identify winners, iterate. This is the spine of the role and where taste shows up.
- Build the system that makes it repeatable. Testing cadence, angle library, naming and tagging, and a bank of real user language pulled from communities, reviews, and our own conversations.
- Create winning concepts and then raise the hit rate of winning concepts so paid has more to scale behind. The bar is quality, not volume, and you manage what we spend proving things out.
- Write the hooks, headlines, overlays, and scripts, in the voice of the person scrolling.
- Brief at volume: one brief that many creators each interpret their own way, built for what each network rewards rather than resizing one idea for all of them.
- Coach creators with sharp feedback, one to many. You brief and evaluate and if required can do creator ops, supporting in producing the content yourself.
- Work with media buying on a weekly cadence. You read media buy KPIs and go into the buying tools yourself to check how tests performed, and you know buying well enough to challenge the buyer on their own ground.
- Develop the product and audience understanding that decides what works. When AI makes output cheap, this becomes the deciding factor in paid.
- Set the visual and verbal point of view for Ash in market. We do not look like the rest of this category, and we do not intend to start.
About you:
- You produce assets yourself on the AI stack, Figma, CapCut and the rest. Not in front of the camera, but you make the creative for testing, not just brief it.
- You come from the paid side moving into creative, or creative moving toward paid. Both work. What matters is turning product and audience understanding into creative that wins.
- Experienced in writing performance copy; have taste and can quickly iterate
- Consumer only, ideally subscription. If your background is SaaS, this is not the role.
- You can set up a clean test, say in advance what would prove you wrong, read the result honestly, and defend your taste with an argument rather than a mood board.
- You want to work on mental health for a reason you can say out loud.
Nice to have:
- You can challenge our media buyer on their own ground, because you have done the buying yourself.
- You have built or reshaped web funnels and landing pages to match the creative that drove the click.
- You have built or run a creator or UGC pipeline, including sourcing, briefing, and quality control.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/slingshotai/657d1a1d-4b.description_excerpt:
Slingshot AI
Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.
We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.
Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.
We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.
THE ROLE
We are hiring a Product Psychologist to sit inside our machine learning team to elaborate on and help further build processes that answer: what does a great Ash conversation look like, and how do you measure it?
Reporting to our Clinical R&D Lead and partnering closely our ML conversation team lead, you'll own the definition of quality for Ash's conversations and turn it into something the ML team can train and evaluate against through benchmarks, evals, and a distributed team of expert human reviewers.
We think optimizing for clinical protocols is the wrong lever. We believe the core driver of outcomes in mental health support, AI or human, is more amorphous: the things that set individual practitioners, rather than individual practices, apart. This role exists to build a science of that belief into something iterable.
This is not a role about designing conversations turn-by-turn. Ash is more grown than built. It's not a management role, though you'll coach a growing team of reviewers. And it's not a research role in the traditional sense. While you'll draw heavily on the literature, your aim is product outcomes, not papers published (though some of your work may become a paper in collaboration with our research team).
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own the definition of "great" for Ash conversations, and make it measurable.
- Make hypothesis-driven calls on how Ash should behave, globally and in specific situations. Change your mind quickly and openly when the evidence tells you to.
- Partner with the Safety team to define Ash's constraints and how it should handle difficult edge-case conversations.
- Recruit, scale, and coach a distributed team of human reviewers: set the bar, teach people what "great" looks like, and keep the group calibrated with each other.
- Be a source of clarity for the conversation and ML teams when the path forward is ambiguous.
ABOUT YOU
- You have a PhD in Clinical or Counseling Psychology, or related field, or a license-eligible Masters degree with clinical training and supervision
- You’re an experienced clinician with a history of working with systems, technological and otherwise, to scale up engaging and effective health products
- You have deep, hands-on experience with interpersonal skills. You can personally facilitate emotional expression well, and you can also see it in someone else's work: flexibility, warmth, honesty, confidence, and attunement, not just credentials.
- You're pragmatic and decisive under real uncertainty. You can make a call with incomplete information, defend it, and drop it fast when new evidence shows up.
- You're oriented toward the user, not toward an external clinical ideal. You won't push an agenda that matters more to you than it does to the people using the product.
- You've worked on measurement before, ideally in digital mental health, and you know how to build a rating system and keep a team of raters calibrated.
- You have some comfort operating close to an ML team. You don't need to train the models, but you should be curious about how evals and benchmarks actually get used to change model behavior.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/slingshotai/029c1d63-71.description_excerpt:
Slingshot AI
Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.
We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.
Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.
We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.
THE ROLE
We’re hiring a leader to help shape how we approach trust and safety at Ash, in our model and in our product.
People bring deeply personal things to Ash. That creates difficult questions about how the product should behave, how we respond when something goes wrong, and how we protect people while respecting their privacy and autonomy. You’ll work alongside psychologists, researchers, and machine learning engineers to develop novel systems for AI in a sensitive domain.
You’ll help us answer hard, ambiguous questions about our model’s policy, investigate, research, develop new policies, and implement them, and communicate clearly about them to both internal and external audiences.
The role combines strategy, hands-on operations, and communication. You might spend one day working through a difficult safety decision with our clinical and legal teams, the next building a process for handling user reports, and the next writing an explanation of our approach for the public.
We’re looking for a thoughtful generalist who learns quickly, makes things happen, and cares deeply about getting this right.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Develop our principles and policies. Work through questions where safety, privacy, user autonomy, and product usefulness pull in different directions. Research the problem, seek expert input, and make a reasoned recommendation. You’ll work with our team, our advisors and experts and others to build principles for how to handle decisions.
- Turn ambiguous issues into clear decisions. Investigate user reports, emerging risks, and new requirements. Establish what we know, what remains uncertain, and what we should do next.
- Make the response work in practice. Build clear processes for triage, investigation, escalation, and follow-through. Define who does what, create the tools and documentation they need, and handle the operational details yourself.
- Turn learning into product improvements. Work with engineering, machine learning, clinical, and legal colleagues to translate findings into changes to Ash and the systems around it.
- Build, test, and improve quickly. For new systems, put a useful first version in place, learn from real cases, and refine it. Match the pace and level of review to the consequences of the decision.
- Write clearly, internally and externally. Produce policies, practical guidance, and public explanations of our safety approach. Help communicate our evaluations and findings, including their limitations. You’ll build initiatives or benchmarks we can share with the outside world to help us and the industry at large do better.
- Represent our thinking. Explain and defend our approach with partners, clinicians, and other audiences. Engage seriously with criticism and bring what you learn back into the work.
ABOUT YOU
- You have strong judgment. You can reason through a difficult question, weigh competing considerations, and recommend a course of action without pretending every answer is certain.
- You’re an excellent writer and communicator. You can turn complex thinking into clear, precise prose. You enjoy doing the research and developing the argument as much as writing the final piece. You can present well and understand how to communicate what we’re doing to the outside world.
- You’ve built something and made it better. It could be a product, an operational process, a program, or an independent project. You can show how you moved from an unclear problem to something people used, then improved it through feedback.
- You’re resourceful and hands-on. You’re willing to investigate individual cases, coordinate people, write the checklist, and follow up until the work is done.
- You seek out expertise without needing someone else to supply every answer. You know when to consult a clinician, engineer, lawyer, or researcher, and can turn their input into a practical decision.
- You’re intellectually curious and willing to change your mind. You can explain a time when evidence challenged your assumptions and changed your approach.
- You handle sensitive information with care and stay thoughtful under pressure. You recognize that this role will involve handling difficult topics on a regular basis including abuse, eating disorders, suicide and death. You can handle these topics maturely and know how to manage your own mental health, seeking support for yourself as needed.
- You care deeply about people’s mental health and the opportunity in front of us. You want more people to have access to good support, and you take responsibility for the trust that requires.
You might come from product, operations, consulting, law, policy, psychology, cognitive science, or another field that has taught you to think rigorously, write well, and execute. Clinical qualifications and previous trust and safety experience are useful, but neither is required.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/aspora/051457c0-84d6-42.description_excerpt:
ABOUT ASPORA
People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.
Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.
We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.
About the Role
This role exists to unify Aspora's entire design output under a single vision. Product, brand, and marketing design have each been built independently. That era ends here.
As Head of Design, you'll lead three design disciplines: product design, brand design, and marketing design. You'll set the direction, build the team, and ensure everything we put in front of customers — from onboarding flows to campaign creative — is coherent, considered, and world-class.
You'll partner directly with Product, Engineering, Growth, and Marketing leadership. Roughly 60% of your time is leadership and direction-setting; 40% is hands-on, in the Product Design domain.
What You'll Own
- Lead and scale all three design functions: product design, brand design, and marketing design, including hiring, structure, and culture.
- Define Aspora's unified design vision across every surface: app, web, brand identity, and growth creative.
- Drive the evolution of Aspora's design system so it serves both product and marketing teams without friction.
- Shape cross-functional design direction alongside Product, Engineering, and Growth, from early concept through to launch.
- Establish design quality standards, critique culture, and operating rhythm across all three disciplines.
- Own Aspora's brand integrity globally, ensuring visual and tonal consistency across all markets and channels.
Who You Are
- 8+ years in design with 3+ years in leadership, with hands-on experience spanning product design and at least one of brand or marketing design.
- Built and led multi-disciplinary design teams. You know how to structure for scale, not just for now.
- Strong product design foundation: UX flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and design systems (Figma or equivalent).
- Fluent in brand and marketing design: visual identity, campaign creative, and the discipline of making both feel like one thing.
- High ownership. You treat problems as yours until they're solved. You don't wait for a brief to make a call.
- Comfortable with ambiguity. You build structure, not wait for it.
- Strong advantage: experience in fintech, regulated industries, or multi-market consumer products.
Why Aspora
- Build the design function that defines how a global fintech looks, feels, and behaves, across every product surface and market.
- Own the full design remit from day one: product, brand, and marketing — rare scope at this stage of company.
- Work at the intersection of design, growth, and product in a team shipping real products to real users across multiple geographies.
- Shape how design earns its seat at the table in a company where execution is currency and craft is taken seriously.
- Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora's long-term vision.

ABOUT THE ROLE
People build lives across borders, and Aspora moves their money with them. Aisha is our next bet: an AI finance agent for NRIs that does the work end to end. Most agent companies build the intelligence and hope the rails come later. We already have the rails. This role exists to build the intelligence NRIs will trust with real money.
You will own Aisha completely: product, roadmap, team and results. You’ll report directly to our CEO. You’ll work closely with compliance, legal and our payments teams across the UAE, UK and India. The hard calls are yours: what to build, buy or partner on, and when the agent is ready to act.
WHO YOU ARE
To you, an AI agent is only worth building if it finishes the job. You’ve built consumer products people rely on every day, and you’ve shipped AI that holds up in the real world.
- You’ve built consumer before. You founded or ran a product people used daily, and you know what users forgive and what loses their trust for good.
- You’ve shipped AI that works in production. You have operated evals, orchestration, tool use and failure modes yourself, not just read about them.
- You bring money-grade judgement. You’ve worked where mistakes move other people’s money, or you can show you learn regulated domains fast.
- You lead by doing. You stay close enough to the product and the code to make the call yourself.
- You’ve moved quickly everywhere you’ve been. Your track record shows people kept trusting you with more, sooner than expected.
- You’ve been tested. A failed launch, a company that died or a regulatory wall. You made sound calls under pressure and followed through to the end.
Most importantly, you want to prove that AI can be trusted with people’s money.
WHAT YOU’LL OWN
This role comes with a founder’s mandate, inside a company that already has licences, partners and customers.
- Own Aisha end to end. Take it from early build to a product NRIs trust with real money tasks.
- Shape the agent stack. Decide what to build, buy or partner on across models, orchestration, data connections and agent payment rails.
- Make reliability the product. Build an agent that completes long, multi-step tasks, with evals, guardrails and failure modes treated as core features.
- Ship consumer-grade experiences. Own onboarding, activation and retention, starting with a hundred research sessions a week that you recruit yourself.
- Build the founding team. Hire senior engineers first, then add design and data as the product earns them.
- Act safely on licensed rails. Partner with compliance and legal so the agent can move money without ever becoming the incident.
What you build will decide how far Aspora goes beyond payments, and how fast we get there.
WHY ASPORA
- You’ll define what a trustworthy AI finance agent looks like, and own the outcome it delivers.
- You’ll work directly with our CEO, with compliance, legal and payments as partners from day one.
- You’ll build on licences, bank partnerships and live corridors that most agent startups spend years chasing.
- You’ll own product, roadmap, team and results from the day you join.
- Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

ABOUT THE ROLE
People build lives across borders, and their finances should move with them. We’re building Aspora for the global diaspora, starting with Indians abroad. Regulation sits at the centre of that ambition. This role exists to turn a complex set of requirements into a practical way to build and run the business. One global framework, local differences only where the law needs them, and decisions made by clear frameworks rather than daily escalations.
You’ll lead licensing, regulator engagement, product advice, safeguarding oversight, customer protection and operational resilience. You’ll report to our COO, working alongside our Global MLRO. You’ll partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and local compliance owners to turn requirements into working controls. You’ll own the regulatory calls on launches, changes and the commitments we make to regulators.
WHO YOU ARE
You don’t see regulation as a reason to say no, or as something to work around. You know a hard boundary from a choice, and your depth goes well beyond AML or licensing paperwork.
- You’ve scaled fintechs before. You’ve helped a payments, remittance or e-money business grow, in house or as a consultant, and can show what you changed.
- You turn expertise into execution. You’ve translated payments and e-money requirements into customer journeys, controls and processes, with fewer failures and less friction to show for it.
- You get permissions over the line. You’ve owned licensing or variation work and regulatory reporting, and kept applications, governance and operating reality consistent throughout.
- You speak regulator fluently, and you’ve been tested. You’ve handled supervisory questions, inspections or a hard remediation, made sound calls under pressure and stayed until it was fixed.
- You’ve set standards at HQ level. You’ve built shared standards across markets and distributed teams, and you know where local law needs a difference and where duplication is habit.
- You’ve seen controls work in practice. You go deep on UK payments, e-money, safeguarding and customer protection, and you’ve followed gaps through to a verified fix.
- You’re on the way up. Your career shows quick progression, growing ownership and real depth. We’ll judge the work you’ve done, not the title you hold.
Most importantly, you want to build a global regulatory framework from the ground up and see it work in practice.
WHAT YOU’LL OWN
This is a role with a genuinely global mandate, with UK payments and e-money regulation as the depth anchor.
- Own licensing and regulator engagement. Lead permissions, perimeter analysis, applications and variations, with accurate filings and a clear register of every commitment we make.
- Shape products before they launch. Assess launches and changes against UK PSRs, EMRs and FCA rules, and turn horizon scanning into owned implementation plans.
- Hold safeguarding to a high standard. Challenge the design, test the evidence and keep us audit ready, partnering with Finance on reconciliations and governance.
- Make customer protection measurable. Drive Consumer Duty, fair value, vulnerable customers, complaints and partner oversight, using outcome data to spot harm and assign action.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/aspora/674a8e53-59e4-41.description_excerpt:
ABOUT ASPORA
People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.
Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.
We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.
ABOUT THE ROLE
People build lives across borders, and their money should move with them. Every product, corridor and payment rail we add opens a new door for fraudsters. We want to be the least attractive target on our corridors, without adding friction for good customers. This role exists to own how we detect and deter fraud across every rail and geo.
You’ll lead fraud detection and deterrence end to end, from exposure mapping to rules, limits and customer protection. You report to our Head of Financial Crime and work alongside the fraud recovery and chargebacks lead. You partner with Product, Payments, Engineering, Customer Support and Compliance on every launch. You decide what ships on day one, and you own the trade-off between fraud caught and friction added.
WHO YOU ARE
You don’t see fraud as a dashboard to watch. You see it as a live contest, won or lost in seconds, and you’ve been in it.
- You’ve done multiple rodeos. You’ve worked fraud at more than one fintech or high-velocity regulated platform across the UK, EU or US. That could be a neobank, payments company, gambling operator, gaming platform or crypto exchange. You know how attacks, rails and rules differ in each.
- You’ve built controls from scratch. At a B2C fintech, you built fraud controls that didn’t exist before, while protecting consumer money at scale.
- You’ve worked the floor. You started as an investigator and worked alerts and cases by hand. You spot a pattern before it shows on a dashboard.
- You’ve been baptised by fire. You’ve handled a real fraud attack or loss spike and made fast calls under pressure. You stayed on it until the fix held, and learned from every case.
- You own the approach. You decide how to tackle a problem and see it through end to end, without waiting to be told.
- You see every launch as a new door. You map where fraud can get in before go-live, not after the first losses land.
- You protect good customers too. You stop fraud without adding friction for the people we serve, and you can show the numbers behind it.
Most importantly, you’d rather build the right controls once, on our own decisioning platform, than tune vendor defaults forever.
WHAT YOU’LL OWN
This is a role with a mandate across every rail, product and geo we operate in.
- See the exposure, everywhere. Map where fraud can hit us on every rail, product and geo, and own the observability layer that lets us watch it live.
- Build rules that hold. Stand up rule building and governance on our decisioning platform, with every change back-tested before it ships.
- Tier exposure by risk. Design progressive access to payment rails by risk tier, so trusted customers move freely and limits grow with trust.
- Measure every trade-off. Track each control change in fraud caught against friction added, and retire the rules that no longer earn their place.
- Protect customers in the moment. Put vulnerable-customer education and in-the-moment verification on every rail, without slowing good customers down.
- Launch with controls from day one. Make sure every new product, geo or rail has a signed-off exposure map before it goes live.
Your calls will shape how fast Aspora can open new corridors, and how safely customers move money once we’re there.
WHY ASPORA
- Define how Aspora detects and deters fraud across every rail and geo, and set the playbook every launch follows.
- Work directly with our Head of Financial Crime, and partner with Product, Payments and Engineering on every launch.
- Build controls on our own decisioning platform, across high-volume cross-border flows at significant scale.
- Own fraud strategy from day one, from exposure mapping through to customer protection.
- Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

- Strong technical acumen: you can hold your own on model serving, GPU infrastructure, latency, and API architecture
- Experience selling into large digital natives or regulated industries (financial services, healthcare/life sciences, insurance, government)
