jobs.ashbyhq.com/founders-factory/e5320c.description_excerpt:
About Founders Factory
Founders Factory is a venture studio and accelerator backed by some of the world's leading corporations. We combine capital investment with deep operational expertise to build and scale tech companies from scratch. With a portfolio of over 300 companies and $900M+ in follow-on funding, we offer a unique opportunity to shape the future of tech and entrepreneurship - working at the intersection of corporate innovation and startup building.
About the Role
Venture Design at Founders Factory is how we create new venture concepts on demand, not by chance. Working closely with our corporate partners, you'll take high-level investment themes and turn them into validated, venture-backable concepts through a structured three-month sprint.
This is the earliest and most exploratory stage of our venture building process. You'll dig into markets, uncover gaps, conceptualise solutions, and pressure-test them with real users - all before a founder is ever hired. The concepts you validate and present to our Investment Committee become the ventures we go on to build. It's high-impact, high-autonomy work that directly shapes our portfolio.
What You'll Do
You'll own the end-to-end venture design sprint, working across research, strategy, prototyping, and validation. Specifically, you will:
- Take investment themes developed with our corporate partners and break them down into explorable problem spaces and opportunity areas.
- Conduct deep market research to understand where sectors are heading, identify structural gaps, and map the competitive landscape.
- Generate multiple potential venture concepts from each theme, applying human-centred design principles to conceptualise solutions that address real user needs.
- Design and run rapid experiments — including A/B testing, prototype testing, and user interviews — to validate or kill concepts quickly.
- Synthesise research and testing into clear, evidence-backed recommendations, narrowing from many ideas to a shortlist of the strongest concepts.
- Present validated concepts to the Investment Committee (comprising decision-makers from our corporate backers and the Founders Factory CEO), making a compelling case for which ventures to greenlight.
- Collaborate across the studio — working with other Venture Designers, Venture Builders, investors, and functional specialists — to sharpen your thinking and leverage collective expertise.
- Stay close to emerging technologies, tools, and market shifts so you're always bringing fresh thinking to each sprint.
What We're Looking For
- Proven experience in 0→1 concept development, venture design, or similar roles where you've taken ideas from fuzzy opportunity spaces through to validated propositions — ideally across multiple industries or verticals.
- Strong strategic thinking combined with a bias for action. You can zoom out to see the big picture and zoom in to run a scrappy experiment in the same afternoon.
- Deep comfort with market research and competitive analysis. You know how to find signal in noise and develop a point of view on where a market is going.
- Experience designing and running rapid experiments (A/B tests, landing page tests, concierge MVPs, user interviews) to validate assumptions with real users.
- Excellent communication and storytelling skills. You'll need to present complex findings and recommendations clearly to senior stakeholders with diverse backgrounds.
- A curious, creative mind that also brings discipline — you generate lots of ideas but know how to prioritise ruthlessly based on evidence.
- Comfort with ambiguity and pace. The sprint format means things move fast and the brief is often wide open. That excites you, not intimidates you.
Nice to Have
- Fluency in German language
- Background in innovation or a venture studio/builder environment.
- Experience working with or alongside corporate partners and navigating stakeholder dynamics.
- Familiarity with rapid prototyping tools (Figma, no-code/low-code platforms) to bring concepts to life quickly.
- Understanding of business model design and unit economics at the concept stage.
- Experience across multiple sectors (fintech, healthtech, sustainability, consumer, etc.).
What We Offer
- The chance to shape ventures from the very beginning — the concepts you validate become real companies.
- A collaborative, high-energy studio environment surrounded by builders, investors, and operators.
- Exposure to a diverse range of industries and corporate partners.
- Desk space in our London office with a fully-serviced workspace.
- Support across marketing, legal, finance, fundraising, growth, and recruitment.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/founders-factory/7ecaef.description_excerpt:
ABOUT FOUNDERS FACTORY:
Founders Factory is a venture studio and accelerator. We build technology companies from scratch, working with leading corporate partners to identify opportunities, develop new products and businesses, and build the founding teams that turn them into independent companies.
Unlike a traditional VC, we don't just invest in companies that already exist. We help create them. That means our approach to talent is different too. We believe the right founder can fundamentally change the trajectory of a company.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
As a Talent Investor, you'll sit at the intersection of venture, talent and company building, helping us identify the exceptional people who will build our next generation of companies.
Our ventures often start with a problem or opportunity, rather than a founder. Your job is to find the person who can turn that opportunity into an excellent business.
You'll work closely with our Venture Builders, Studio Leads and founders to:
- Identify exceptional founders across our global network and beyond.
- Build talent maps and develop a point of view on where the best founders and operators sit.
- Assess individuals for founder-market fit, looking beyond CVs and conventional credentials to understand their potential to build a company.
- Build relationships with exceptional people who aren't necessarily looking for their next role.
- Convince them to take the leap into entrepreneurship and build with Founders Factory.
- Help founders identify and recruit their early founding team across product, technology, commercial and growth.
- Develop our approach to founder sourcing, assessment and talent intelligence as we build more ventures.
This isn't traditional recruitment. You won't be given a list of vacancies to fill. You'll be given venture theses and asked to work out who could build them.
You'll have significant autonomy to experiment with how we identify, assess and attract exceptional people, and your work will directly influence the quality and trajectory of the companies we build.
ABOUT YOU
At your core, you're obsessed with exceptional people and curious about how great companies are built.
You might come from VC, executive search, strategy consulting, investment banking, a high-growth startup, venture building or talent. You don't need to have worked in venture before.
What matters is that you can:
- Spot exceptional people and develop a strong point of view on their potential.
- Understand businesses, markets and what makes founders successful.
- Build genuine relationships and influence people to make high-stakes career decisions.
- Source talent creatively, particularly people who aren't actively looking.
- Operate with limited information, ambiguity and a high degree of autonomy.
- Balance instinct with evidence and be willing to change your mind.
- Move quickly without compromising your judgement.
- Communicate clearly and challenge assumptions when needed.
You don't need to be a founder or have a traditional career path. We care more about your judgement, curiosity, ambition and ability to identify exceptional people.
WHAT YOU'LL BE MEASURED ON
- Founder quality: Exceptional founders joining our ventures.
- Founder-market fit: The quality of our decisions around who should build which company.
- Speed: Moving from venture thesis to founder commitment quickly.
- Founding teams: Helping founders build the teams they need to succeed.
- Talent intelligence: Building a proprietary network and understanding of exceptional founders and operators.
- Repeatability: Making our approach to talent investing better and more scalable over time.
A CAREER IN VENTURE
Talent Investing sits at the intersection of people, company building and venture capital.
You'll develop an investor's perspective on founders and companies at the earliest possible stage, often before there is a company to invest in.
Over time, there is scope to develop into broader venture-building and investment responsibilities across Founders Factory, depending on your performance, interests and the needs of the business.
OUR CULTURE
Working at Founders Factory is very different from working at a traditional company. We are resilient business builders, passionate about what we're creating and comfortable operating in uncertainty.
We:
- Think big, act small, move fast
- Value momentum over perfection
- Embrace uncertainty and remain decisive
- Suggest solutions, not problems
- Prioritise diversity to strengthen our collective intelligence
- Are polite, generous and show empathy to others
WHAT WE OFFER
- Competitive salary
- Shares in the Founders Factory global portfolio
- Hybrid working — typically Tuesdays and Thursdays in the London office
- Up to 5 weeks working abroad each year
- 25 days annual leave
- 1 additional mental health day per quarter
- Monthly calendar freedom day
- Travel opportunities across our global Founders Factory offices
- Access to our network of founders, investors, operators and corporate partners
Founders Factory is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where people can authentically be themselves, challenge assumptions, take risks and think creatively.

Stage: Pre-seed. Location: Cambridge/London, UK. Comp: Competitive + Equity
ABOUT SUBTLE
Most families find out something's wrong too late: a fall, a missed check-in, a change no one noticed until it became a crisis. We're building ambient sensing for the elderly and vulnerable at home, technology that quietly looks out for the people we love without asking them to wear anything or change how they live. We're early. We're validating with real customers, building the first hardware, and looking for the person who'll help turn this from an idea into a product families can trust with something this personal.
We are building this from scratch inside Founders Factory's studio, with a dedicated pre-seed investment, hands-on studio support across product, design, talent and growth, and a six-month build programme to get from concept to a fundable, in-market product. This venture has secured a major European technology partner. The founding CEO is already in place. We are now looking for the technical other half of the founding team.
THE ROLE
You'll be our first engineering hire, working directly with the founder(s) and carrying real authority over what we build and how. It's a hands-on role that spans hardware and software, and a leadership one too, since you'll grow the team that follows you.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own hardware validation and bench testing end to end, and lead our manufacturing path. Whether that ends up being an outsourced partner or in-house, you're the one validating the sensor platform yourself and making sure whatever we ship has been properly tested before it reaches someone's home. This is safety-relevant, so you'd rather catch a failure on the bench than have it happen in someone's home.
- Build the software that turns sensor data into something useful. Detection logic, alerting, and the escalation decisions that sit behind them, tested and monitored with the same rigor as the hardware.
- Navigate the regulatory and security requirements that come with this territory. Certification requirements for embedded systems (software and hardware), and data protection for Personally Identifiable Information (PII), from day one rather than retrofitted later.
- Grow the team. As we scale past this hire, you'll hire, mentor and lead the engineers who join under you.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Must have's
- Early-stage hardware experience. You've taken a hardware product from 0 to 1 in a startup environment, and you're comfortable spanning embedded systems and software.
- Experience using AI to accelerate how you work, across engineering, prototyping, and the day-to-day operations of running a startup.
- Experience leading or building a small engineering team, or clearly ready to step into that.
- A proactive, evidence-first way of working. You're comfortable with ambiguity, and comfortable being told (including by yourself) that a result doesn't hold up.
- Experience with regulatory, security, or compliance requirements in health tech, medical devices, or another safety- and privacy-regulated space. You understand that building for vulnerable people and their data changes what "done" means.
- Lead vendor and manufacturing negotiations, securing the right partners, terms, and production capabilities to bring the product to market.
- Any direct experience taking a regulated product through certification (CE/UKCA, FDA, or equivalent) is considered a major plus.

As a Business Development Representative, you’ll be the first point of connection between Happl and future customers. You’ll identify and engage forward-thinking companies, open meaningful conversations with HR and Finance leaders, and build the pipeline that powers our expansion.
You’re not just generating leads, you’re creating opportunities, building relationships, and helping organisations discover a better way to support their people. Your work will directly shape Happl’s growth and play a key role in scaling a new category of employee benefits infrastructure.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/happl/0396ba88-7ad6-426.description_excerpt:
We’re building the next generation of employee benefits infrastructure.
At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.
Happl is backed by leading investors such as YCombinator, 6Degrees Capital, and more, known for backing leading companies such as Deel, Rippling, Airbnb, Coinbase, Dropbox, and most recently was awarded a place in the UK’s top 100 startups for 2026.
About the role
As an Employee Benefits Technical Implementation Manager at Happl, you'll be the person customers trust to turn their benefits strategy into a working reality. You'll own the setup of Happl across a portfolio of accounts - configuring the platform, building the eligibility and allowance logic, mapping the data, and making sure what launches actually reflects what the customer set out to deliver.
This role sits at the intersection of customer success and product. You'll work directly with HR, Reward, and Finance stakeholders to understand the strategy behind their programme - who's eligible for what, how allowances flex by grade or country, what payroll needs to see, where the exceptions live - and translate it into a clean, scalable configuration on Happl. You'll be equally comfortable walking a Reward Director through how their scheme will behave in the platform, unpicking a messy HRIS export, and building the rules logic that makes a complex global programme run without manual intervention.
We're still building this function. That means there's no rigid playbook to follow - you'll help write it. If you're energised by that kind of ownership, and want to shape how a category-defining product gets deployed across the world, this is the role for you.
What you’ll be doing
- Leading end-to-end customer implementations, from discovery and scoping through to go-live and long-term optimisation, taking full ownership of the setup throughout
- Running structured discovery sessions to understand each customer's benefits strategy in detail - eligibility populations, grade and country variations, allowance structures, joiner/leaver treatment - before a single rule is configured
- Building and owning advanced rules logic: eligibility criteria, allowance tiers, pro-rating, life event triggers, approval flows, and the edge cases that make real-world benefits programmes messy
- Owning data mapping between customer HRIS, payroll, and Happl - defining the field-level mapping, handling messy or inconsistent source data, and making sure every downstream output (payroll deductions, P11D treatment, insurer census files) is right
- Configuring multi-country programmes with the local nuance intact - different providers, currencies, tax treatments, and enrolment rules sitting under one coherent setup
- Testing rigorously before launch: building test populations, validating rules behave as intended across every scenario, and catching the problems that would otherwise land on an employee's payslip
- Building and automating implementation workflows using AI tools, reducing manual effort and raising the consistency and quality of every deployment
- Acting as the escalation point during and after go-live, diagnosing root causes quickly and partnering with Engineering to drive permanent fixes
- Translating what you learn across implementations into reusable assets - configuration templates, mapping libraries, and playbooks - that make every future launch faster and smarter
- Partnering with Customer Success to ensure adoption and take-up are strong post-launch, identifying configuration gaps and opportunities that drive retention and expansion
- Feeding implementation insight back to Product and Engineering with clarity and evidence, directly influencing the roadmap - particularly where the platform can't yet express what customers need
- Analysing configuration and usage data across your portfolio to spot patterns, flag risks early, and surface opportunities to improve customer outcomes
- Championing AI-first ways of working - actively exploring tools like Claude and ChatGPT to accelerate delivery, automate repetitive tasks, and bring smarter thinking to every customer engagement
- Staying genuinely curious about the benefits market, HR tech, and the evolving AI landscape, bringing ideas that keep Happl and its customers ahead of the curve
What we’re looking for
- 3+ years working in employee benefits - at a brokerage, consultancy, insurer, benefits platform, or in-house benefits/reward team - with real exposure to how schemes are administered, not just designed
- A track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end-to-end — with the technical depth to design robust solutions and the communication skills to bring customers with you
- Hands-on experience with APIs, webhooks, and data integrations; comfortable diagnosing issues, building elegant solutions, and documenting them clearly for customers and internal teams
- Truly AI-native: you use tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and modern no-code platforms in your day-to-day work, and you’re excited about what they unlock in implementation and customer delivery
- Strong analytical and problem-solving instincts — able to take ambiguous requirements and turn them into clear, well-structured technical plans
- An excellent communicator who adapts naturally — as confident presenting a solution architecture to a CTO as troubleshooting a configuration issue with an HR admin
- Highly organised and self-directed, capable of managing multiple concurrent implementations without compromising on quality or customer experience
- Excited by the prospect of helping build a function from the ground up — you’re energised by defining how things should work, not just following an established path
- Genuine curiosity about HR technology, employee benefits, and the role AI is playing in reshaping how companies support their people
If you don’t meet every requirement but feel this role fits your trajectory, we’d still love to hear from you.
What to expect
Happl is growing fast, and the pace reflects that. You’ll be working on things that don’t have established answers yet, building processes that don’t exist, making decisions with incomplete information, and iterating quickly when things change. That’s not a caveat; it’s the nature of building something totally new.
Some weeks will be brilliant. Some will be genuinely hard. Customer needs will evolve, priorities will shift, and you’ll occasionally be asked to figure out something nobody at Happl has had to figure out before. You’ll need to be resilient, resourceful, and direct, with customers, with the team, and with yourself when something isn’t working.
What you’ll get in return is real. The access, influence, and ownership available here wouldn’t exist in a larger company. Your work will be visible, your ideas will land, and the people around you will be…

jobs.ashbyhq.com/happl/9da5bbdd-434d-472.description_excerpt:
We’re building the next generation of employee benefits infrastructure.
At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.
Happl is backed by leading investors such as YCombinator, 6Degrees Capital, Haatch, Portage, and more, known for backing leading companies such as Deel, Rippling, Airbnb, Coinbase, Dropbox, and most recently was awarded a place in the UK’s top 100 startups for 2026.
About the role
As Financial Controller at Happl, you’ll own the financial engine of the business — everything from the cash in the bank to the numbers our board and investors use to make decisions runs through you. You’ll run the monthly close, the full revenue cycle, the compliance calendar across two jurisdictions, and our treasury position, and you’ll decide how all of it gets built, systemised, and automated.
This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role with a direct line to leadership. You won’t be managing a process someone else designed — you’ll be deciding what good looks like across revenue, cash, compliance, and reporting, then making it happen. You’ll work closely with the CEO, the board, our investors, and our outsourced bookkeeping, audit, and tax partners, holding all of it to a standard that matches the product we’ve built.
We’re FCA-regulated and YCombinator-backed, having raised $11m to date, and we give global employers a single place to design, deliver, and manage benefits across 160+ countries and 70+ languages — which means the finance function behind the product has to be just as sharp as the product itself. We’re entering our next phase of growth, with an ambitious revenue trajectory and an expanding international footprint, and this role sits at the centre of it.
What you’ll be doing
- Owning the monthly close on a fixed timetable — management accounts, balance sheet integrity, accruals, prepayments, and the revenue and cost reconciliations that sit behind them
- Writing the commentary that explains what’s actually happened in the business, not just what the numbers say
- Producing the monthly investor reporting pack and the financial sections of board materials — ARR and revenue analysis, cash and runway, burn efficiency, unit economics, cohort and retention metrics, and budget versus actual
- Owning the full revenue cycle — invoicing, collections, aged debt, and revenue recognition across a multi-currency, multi-contract subscription base
- Leading the rollout of automated billing and revenue recognition tooling, moving us from manual tracking to a system that scales without adding headcount
- Managing our two legal entities — a US TopCo and a UK operating company — including statutory accounts, audit preparation, intercompany accounting, transfer pricing mechanics, and FX exposure between them
- Owning the compliance calendar end to end across both jurisdictions — UK VAT returns, corporation tax, US federal and state filings, sales tax where applicable, and payroll taxes
- Supporting our FCA regulatory reporting obligations and the financial controls that sit behind them
- Running monthly payroll across jurisdictions, pension and benefits administration, employee expenses, and the finance side of onboarding and offboarding
- Owning the cash position and treasury strategy — cash flow forecasting, working capital, FX management, and structuring how we hold company funds to earn a sensible return without taking risk we shouldn’t
- Managing our outsourced bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners — holding them to deadlines and quality, and pulling work in-house where doing so makes us faster
- Owning the finance tech stack and having a strong opinion on it, actively replacing manual work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across reconciliations, invoice processing, variance analysis, and reporting drafts
- Leveraging AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to speed up your own work and build the systems that let finance scale without adding headcount
- Acting as the financial conscience of the business, with a direct line to the founders and a real say in how we grow
What we’re looking for
- Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA), or qualified by experience with a track record that stands up to scrutiny
- Genuine ownership of a monthly close cycle and management reporting pack, start to finish
- Strong technical grounding in revenue recognition, accruals accounting, and balance sheet control
- Comfortable with tax and compliance across VAT, corporation tax, and payroll, ideally spanning both the UK and US
- AI-native in your approach — you already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and can talk specifically about what you’ve automated and what it saved you
- Exceptional attention to detail, alongside the judgement to know when precision matters and when speed does
- A clear communicator — you can explain a number to a non-finance audience without patronising them or losing them
- Ideally, SaaS or subscription business experience, particularly ARR reporting and deferred revenue, and familiarity with modern billing infrastructure like Xero or Stripe
- Comfort with SQL, Python, or low-code automation tools is a bonus, not a requirement, but it will make your life here significantly easier
What to expect
Being Financial Controller at Happl is not a maintenance role. You’ll be building the finance function as you run it — choosing the systems, designing the controls, and deciding how billing, revenue recognition, and reporting should work as we scale into new markets and currencies. That’s not a caveat; it’s the role.
Some weeks will be genuinely rewarding — a reporting pack you built gives the board real clarity, a manual process you automated saves the team hours every month, a treasury decision you made puts real value on the table. Some will be hard — closing the books on a fixed timetable, holding partners and advisors to a deadline, and making judgement calls across two jurisdictions with incomplete information.
What you get in return is real scope. You’ll own the whole picture — revenue, cash, compliance, treasury, and reporting — across two jurisdictions and 160+ countries of operations, with a direct line to the founders and reporting that goes straight to the board and our investors. This is the foundation of a finance function that will grow with the business, and the right person grows with it.
Why join Happl
- Be part of building something that genuinely matters — the future of how companies support their people
- Competitive salary that reflects the impact you’ll have
- Real equity — a meaningful stake in what we’re building together
- Hybrid working from day one, with the trust and flexibility to do your best work
- Your own Happl account — use the platform you’re helping to build and shape
- Private Health Insurance, because we genuinely care about how you’re doing
- Dental insurance,…

AT GRADIENT LABS, WE'RE BUILDING THE AI CUSTOMER OPERATIONS PLATFORM FOR FINANCIAL SERVICES.
Founded in 2023, we now work with some of the biggest names in banking and fintech. Our platform runs specialist agents, purpose-built for financial services, to eliminate manual work across customer support and back-office operations. Together, they give product and operations teams the visibility and control to trust every outcome.
We're a team of builders from companies like Monzo, Wise, Revolut and Google. If you're excited to tackle some of the hardest problems in AI and help shape the future of customer operations, we'd love to hear from you.
🎯 HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT
This is a build-and-ship role. You'll turn ambiguous customer support problems into reliable, observable AI agents that handle live conversations for real users. You'll work close to production - designing prompts and tool flows, building eval suites, shipping changes, watching what breaks, and iterating fast.
- Build and operate AI agents in production: Design, implement, and maintain agentic systems powered by LLMs - handling tool calling, multi-step reasoning, and integration with customer APIs and data sources. You'll own these systems end-to-end: reliable, observable, and auditable from day one.
- Translate business problems into agentic workflows: Take on ambiguous, open-ended problems (like "help our agent handle conversations in multiple languages") and turn them into scoped, shippable projects.
- Strong product mindset: Prioritise product thinking over pure ML technique, optimising for customer and business value rather than model performance for its own sake.
- Build robust evaluation infrastructure: Create and maintain eval suites drawn from real-world scenarios and edge cases. Go beyond vibes-based testing: structured evals measuring accuracy, safety, and latency, tied to clear business outcomes, used to drive systematic improvements to prompts, tools, and behaviour.
- Enhance our agent: Develop, evaluate, and optimise the skills that make up our agent. Curate datasets, iterate on improvements, test changes, and ship successful approaches into production.
- Shape our internal AI platform: Contribute to shared libraries, patterns, and standards for how we build, evaluate, and deploy agents across customers. Help define how we approach prompting, tool orchestration, retrieval, and monitoring.
- Experiment and prototype: Keep up with the latest in NLP, agentic systems, and generative AI. Prototype against our hardest problems with a bias toward shipping experiments quickly rather than long research cycles. Our agents already handle tens of thousands of real customer conversations every hour, so your work has immediate, visible impact.
- Analyse data: Work across customer queries, support tickets, and related data to find patterns and identify what our agents could automate next.
- Drive technical decisions: Scope your own work, push back when the framing is wrong, and tell us when the plan needs to change.
💡 WHAT YOU’LL BRING
- Professional software engineering experience, with a meaningful focus on Machine Learning, NLP, or applied AI. At this time, we need the ML/applied AI experience as a non-negotiable requirement for this role.
- Experience shipping products to real, live customers, not just internal tools or prototypes, ideally at meaningful scale.
- A strong product mindset - you can take a vague problem, break it down from first principles, and know how to get to a valuable first version. You have a preference for fast iteration over long research cycles.
- Hands-on experience building with LLMs, whether in a previous role, at a startup (even one that didn't work out), or on a small, scrappy team.
- Comfort with ambiguity, and the confidence to say "I don't understand" and work through it rather than guessing. You can take open-ended problems (like "help our agent handle conversations in multiple languages") and turn them into scoped, shippable projects.
- Strong communication skills - you can explain the reasoning and trade-offs behind your decisions, not just describe what you built, you communicate clearly and often, and you flag early when you’re stuck.
- A pragmatic, tech-agnostic approach - no specific tech stack required, just good judgement about what's right for the problem.
WHY JOIN GRADIENT LABS?
This is a unique chance to be part of a team working with cutting-edge technology to reshape how businesses will operate in the future. Over the next 10 years, every company will need to embrace AI-powered operations to stay competitive, and this role puts you right in the middle of that transformation.
You’ll tackle challenging and new problems, work with some of the most exciting brands across different industries, and be surrounded by a passionate, smart team that’s driven to build something groundbreaking.
BENEFITS & LOGISTICS 🧡
- We’re still at early stages of building out our compensation bandings, whilst we continue to shape this, we’re open to chatting with people who have a range of salary requirements
- Our compensation package has two key components - base salary & meaningful equity
- Private medical & dental insurance
- 25 days holiday + bank holidays (or bank holiday opt out for 32 days holiday)
- Team socials and offsites
- Flexible working - we have an office in central London and a hybrid working approach. This role is open to London based or remote in the UK folks - please note, we'd be looking for the person in this role to be able to come into the London office twice per week
THE INTERVIEW PROCESS 📝
- 30 mins Talent Screen with our Founding People & Talent
- 45 mins First Stage interview with one of our AI Engineers to talk through a complex AI project you've worked on
- Take Home Task
- 1hr Mid-stage Interview to discuss the take home task you've completed with our Chief Scientist
- 1hr Final Interview focusing on product thinking

jobs.ashbyhq.com/ddn/664bc1e8-6d51-4a73-.description_excerpt:
We’re looking for a Senior People Business Partner to help build and deliver the People agenda across our growing EMEA organization.
This person will be based out of our Madrid office and will help drive the People and Organizational agenda across all business units across Europe and the Middle East. You’ll partner closely with regional leadership, and work cross functionally with Global HRBP'S to translate global talent organizational priorities across the region.
The role is best suited for strategic operator who identifies as a builder. Our future People operating model is still taking shape, and particularly at first, this person will move between strategic partnership and hands-on execution. They’ll help solve today’s problems while building the practices that mean we don’t have to solve them the same way tomorrow.
The best person for this role knows how to navigate complexity without creating more of it. They understand the realities of operating across multiple European markets, have exceptional doer energy, and are equally comfortable advising a leader and figuring out how something actually needs to work on the ground.
What You’ll Do
- Partner across EMEA. Support leaders and teams across G&A, Sales and Engineering, working closely with Global HRBPs and People leadership to translate global talent and organizational strategies into the EMEA context.
- Bring real multi-country expertise. Help navigate the realities of operating across many many different European employment environments, cultures and ways of working. Know when a global approach works, when local adaptation is necessary, and when specialist expertise needs to come into the room. Advise on benefits, contracts, and regional nuances.
- Own performance and employee relations across the region. Coach managers through performance issues, investigations and complex employee situations from early diagnosis through resolution, partnering with Legal and local counsel where needed.
- Help build DDN’s People playbook. You won’t just consume People programs—this role will help create them. Partner across the People team to build and continuously improve global practices like performance management, onboarding, manager enablement, talent reviews and other foundational People programs. Bring what you learn from the business back into how DDN operates globally.
- Help execute the talent agenda. Support talent reviews, succession, performance management, engagement, leadership development and organizational effectiveness across EMEA. Bring regional insight into global talent conversations rather than simply executing decisions made elsewhere.
- Build as you go. Help establish the processes and infrastructure required to support a growing EMEA organization—from onboarding and employee lifecycle practices to new locations, employment models and other operational needs.
- Turn strategy into execution. Take global People priorities and make them actually work across the region. Build the plan, identify dependencies, coordinate stakeholders and drive through to completion.
- Be an exceptional cross-functional partner. Work closely with People Operations, Compensation, Talent Acquisition, Finance, Legal, IT and regional leaders. In a matrixed global company, getting the right answer often requires connecting a lot of dots—and people.
What You Bring
You’re comfortable being both a trusted People partner and someone who gets things done and more importantly, you don’t need every problem to fit neatly into a job description before taking ownership of it.
- Significant HRBP experience in a genuinely multi-country European/Middle East environment.
- Broad knowledge of European and Middle East employment practices and experience navigating complex employee and employment matters across multiple jurisdictions.
- Experience supporting multiple functions—ideally some combination of Sales, G&A and technical organizations—in a matrixed global company.
- Strong grounding across performance management, employee relations, talent management, organizational effectiveness and change.
- A builder mentality in a truly 0->1 or 1->2 organization. You’ve worked in environments where processes were evolving, ownership wasn't always obvious and sometimes the first step was simply figuring out what needed to happen.
- Exceptional execution skills. You create structure around ambiguity, love a good project plan, keep track of the details and reliably close loops.
- Strong cross-functional instincts. You know how to bring together Legal, Finance, Operations, regional expertise and business leaders rather than trying to solve everything yourself. You’re an exceptional partner to your People Team counterparts
- Strategic range to understand the broader business and talent implications of the work—not simply execute the task in front of you.
- Comfortable being hands-on. Particularly as we build, there will be work that eventually belongs somewhere else but for now, you might need to roll your sleeves up! “That’s not my job” doesn't belong at DDN!
- Strong judgment, curiosity and the ability to operate independently while knowing when to pull others in.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/latentlabs/2abcd613-81e.description_excerpt:
THE OPPORTUNITY
We are looking for a highly skilled machine learning researcher with significant experience in generative modeling. You will join an interdisciplinary team of machine learners, protein engineers and biologists, jointly working to change the way that we control biology and cure diseases. In your role you will architect novel generative models with the goal of designing new proteins that are functional in wet lab assays.
WHO YOU ARE
- You are a strong ML researcher with experience in generative modeling. You have led or worked on notable machine learning projects, as documented by your contributions to widely used open source libraries, significant product launches or high impact publications, e.g. at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR or Nature venues. You have a proven track record of deep expertise in generative modeling.
- You are a skillful ML developer. You write ML code that is robust, tested and easy to maintain. You have experience using version control and code review systems. You are a fast prototyper and hacker who can also write beautiful production code. You have experience running training and inference on cloud hardware, parallelizing data and models across accelerators.
- You are a data engineer. You have experience building ML data pipelines for the training and evaluation of deep learning models. You are able to analyze the raw data, construct appropriate dataset splits and build pipelines that perform and scale.
- You are passionate about model performance. You have an intricate understanding of how ML libraries interplay with hardware and data and love to optimize deep learning models for training / inference speed. You have a deep knowledge of best principles and tricks in architecting deep learning models and use it to optimize how they perform on validation metrics.
- You are mission driven and curious. You are passionate about making a positive impact on the world, whether it's for patients, customers or beyond. You are motivated by the end goal and are flexible in adapting to different approaches and methodologies. You are curious about problems, however small or big they appear.
You thrive in a dynamic environment. You work well in a fast-paced setting where goals must be achieved efficiently and urgently.
WHAT SETS YOU APART
- You have experience in computational biology or protein design. You have worked on ML-driven projects in biology.
- You have a natural science background. You are academically trained in physics, biology, chemistry or other related fields.
YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES
- Build machine learning models that work in the physical world [~90% of your time]:
- Contribute to a careful curation of our training and evaluation data.
- Propose and build ML evaluation metrics that align with real world success and company goals.
- Quickly prototype generative models against our lead metrics and perform deep analyses of improvements.
- Collaborate in a joint codebase with other research scientists, engineers and protein designers, maintaining highest code standards.
- Contribute to the maintenance of our compute and ML development infrastructure.
- In collaboration with the bio team, plan wet lab testing campaigns and carry out model inference against biological targets to enable their testing in the wet lab.
- Quickly learn from wet lab results and feedback data to our models.
- Self development [~10% of your time]:
- Stay on top of the latest developments in ML.
- Gain a strong working understanding of protein and cell biology.
- Participate in knowledge sharing, e.g. organize and present at our internal reading group.
- Attend and present at conferences.
APPLY
We offer strongly competitive compensation and benefits packages, including:
- Private health insurance
- Pension/401(K) contributions
- Generous leave policies (including gender neutral parental leave)
- Hybrid working
- Travel opportunities and more
We also offer a stimulating work environment, and the opportunity to shape the future of synthetic biology through the application of breakthrough generative models.
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and we are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

Member of Technical Staff, Applied AI

We are looking for a Member of Technical Staff with deep expertise in generative modelling to work at the interface between our frontier models and the customers who depend on them. You will join an interdisciplinary team of machine learners, protein engineers and biologists, jointly working to change the way that we control biology and cure diseases. In your role you will develop an in-depth understanding of our proprietary generative models and apply that knowledge to deploy, adapt and optimise them within customer environments - particularly in the pharmaceutical and biotech sectors.

At Latent Labs you will be working with some of the brightest minds in generative AI and biology.
Our team is committed to interdisciplinary exchange, continuous learning and collaboration. Team offsites help us foster a culture of trust across our London and San Francisco sites.

Build the AI therapist that delivers end-to-end CBT to patients in the US: live, clinically supervised, and measured on whether people actually get better.
About Limbic
Limbic’s vision is to ensure the highest quality therapy is accessible to everyone, everywhere.
Limbic has supported more than 820,000 patients across the UK and the US. We are used in over 50% of NHS Talking Therapies services, which makes us the largest-ever deployment of generative AI for direct patient care, and our AI now delivers end-to-end therapy to patients in the US under the supervision of licensed clinicians.
Safety and science come first. We are the only AI mental health chatbot with UKCA Class IIa medical device certification, and the first AI-led mental healthcare company selected for the FDA’s TEMPO pilot. Our results are published in leading scientific journals: in a randomised, double-blind trial published in Nature Medicine, our AI agents scored higher than licensed CBT therapists on a standard measure of therapy skill.
The Role
As an AI/ML Engineer, you will sit at the intersection of computational psychiatry, clinical science, and software engineering. You will join the product team building our AI therapist: a voice agent that delivers structured, evidence-based CBT over the phone to adults with depression and anxiety, with licensed clinicians overseeing every patient’s care.
The product is live and growing week on week, so your work reaches real patients quickly. You will own problems end to end: frame them with clinicians and product managers, ship a change, measure whether it helped, and iterate. Our AI products are built on shared platforms for agents, evaluation and safety, so what you build here is reused across Limbic.
What You’ll Do
- Improve how our AI therapist runs sessions, from session structure and case formulation to therapeutic techniques and continuity across a course of treatment, working closely with clinicians.
- Strengthen the safety systems that protect patients in real time, including risk detection and how the agent responds when risk is disclosed.
- Build evaluations and LLM-as-judge autolabellers, validated against clinician labels, so we know quickly and reliably whether a change made care better or worse.
- Make voice conversations feel natural: responsive, well-paced, and able to recover gracefully when a conversation goes off script.
- Help patients stay with their treatment long enough to recover, through AI features such as well-timed session reminders and clear expectations about what therapy involves, and test what works with experiments.
- Optimise how we collect outcome measures such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7, including the methods, timing and predictive modelling of recovery.
- Ship changes safely through incremental rollouts, automated testing and a clinical sign-off process built for a regulated medical device.
What You’ll Bring
- You must meet one of the following educational and experience backgrounds:
- A PhD in Computational Psychiatry or a related field, coupled with demonstrated industry experience in Data Science, Product, or ML engineering.
- OR A BSc/MSc in a Computational Psychiatry related field (research focus) plus 2 years of experience in ML engineering or Data Science within an Engineering/Product Development environment.
- Proficiency in either Python or TypeScript/JavaScript.
- Experience building LLM-powered features and a track record of eval-driven development.
- An expert approach to hypothesis-driven work, with a track record of balancing product development with scientific rigour.
- Experience using Machine Learning in a production environment or via high-impact scientific publications (e.g., predictive modelling, reinforcement learning).
- Experience modelling text/language data, including building LLM classifiers and using vector-based methods.
- Experience modelling longitudinal data and working with databases (SQL or NoSQL).
- A strong understanding of evidence-based mental health care (such as Cognitive Behavioural Therapy) and a deep interest in the causal mechanisms that drive therapeutic benefit.
- A bias to action: you break big problems into pieces you can ship within a week, and you are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information.
- Proficiency with version control systems, preferably Git.
- Ideal but not required: Experience building an LLM agent harness or real-time voice AI.
- The ability to work from our London (Spitalfields) office on Tuesdays and Thursdays, with the flexibility to work remotely or from the office on other days of the week.
Benefits & Wellbeing
- Competitive salary and equity share options.
- An amazing office in central London (Spitalfields) for our collaborative team days on Tuesdays and Thursdays, paired with a flexible/hybrid working model on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.
- 25 days PTO plus bank holidays.
- Company pension scheme (UK).
- Enhanced parental leave packages (UK).
- Support with purchasing work-related books and materials.
- Quarterly Life Days: Enjoy 4 paid days off per year (one each quarter) to use whenever you choose to relax, recharge, or take care of personal matters.
- Mental Health Support: Access to dedicated mental health support services.
We encourage women and individuals from diverse backgrounds to apply and join our team. We believe in creating an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone can contribute their best.

ABOUT NETBOX LABS
At NetBox Labs, our mission is to make it easier to build and manage complex networks and infrastructure. We provide the leading network infrastructure management platform used by enterprises, data centers, and network practitioners worldwide.
WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW
Foundations is the platform software team at NetBox Labs. It owns the set of shared services, standards, and tools that all applications and delivery methods use: UI, Auth, Secrets, Customer Usage Monitoring, Entitlements Management, etc
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
The Foundations service catalog contains our core platform offerings. You will contribute to decisions on what goes into the catalog and what stays off it. You and your team will release each service as a finished artifact - software or documentation - that application teams use. Examples of catalog offerings:
- Identity and access: user management, authentication and authorization (including PAS), the organization, tenant, and user model, and customer secrets.
- Shared application services: the UI platform and shared frontend components, customer usage telemetry.
- Platform standards: Kubernetes, Postgres, Redis, cloud infrastructure, and customer environments in collaboration with the needs of the Delivery Teams
- Developer experience: the local development environment, and the integration of new components into that experience.
- Contracts across delivery methods: NetBox Cloud and NetBox Enterprise can implement a catalog service in different ways. You make sure that each difference is documented. Where possible, you put the difference behind one consistent interface.
- The service catalog lifecycle: You review catalog services every quarter and when application teams give feedback. You approve an exception only with a documented reason and an exit plan.
- Technical leadership of the team: You lead and mentor the Foundations engineers through daily technical work. The engineers do not report to you.
WHAT YOU WON'T OWN
This is a hands-on technical lead role, not a people management role.
People management
The EM owns hiring, performance management, and team process. You work closely with the EM and give input on all three.
Product priorities
The Foundations Product Manager owns priorities. You align technical plans with those priorities. You challenge a priority when its technical cost is high.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (12 MONTHS)
- Each high-priority catalog service is DONE: an application team uses it and gets value from it.
- Application teams do not re-implement a concern that the catalog covers.
- For each catalog service, all differences between Cloud and Enterprise are documented.
- Foundations makes technical decisions without escalation to the Director.
- You and the EM run the team together, with a clear split of responsibilities.
COMPLEXITIES OF THE ROLE
Scope
Many shared concerns can move into Foundations. If too many move in, delivery stops and ownership becomes unclear.
Adoption
A catalog service that application teams do not use has no value. You must design services that teams want to use. You must also get the teams to adopt them.
Cloud and Enterprise differences
Catalog services run in NetBox Cloud and in customer environments for NetBox Enterprise. Customer environments give less observability and slower feedback. A difference that nobody records becomes an operational or customer problem later.
Access control is a security boundary
An error in access control is a security incident. PAS changes need a security review before release. You must design for this from the start.
Decisions already made
Many catalog services have design decisions in place. You must decide quickly what to keep and what to change.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

NetBox Labs is seeking a Full Stack Engineer to join our rapidly expanding engineering team. We have multiple positions open at different seniority levels across several teams.
About NetBox Labs
NetBox Labs builds the next generation of network automation tools for modern infrastructure teams, with NetBox as the network source of truth at the center. The Observability team builds the products that connect that source of truth to what is actually running on the network:
- NetBox Discovery finds devices, interfaces, and other network entities.
- NetBox Assurance brings discovered data into NetBox and helps operators spot drift between intended and actual state, review changes, and decide what to accept.
- Fleet Management and the Orb agent deploy, configure, and manage the agents that collect discovery and telemetry data from customer networks. These agents use SNMP, gNMI, and other device interfaces.
- Diode is the ingestion pipeline that moves that data into NetBox reliably.
We're hiring a Full Stack Engineer who can work across the whole path, from the agents and services that collect network data to the interfaces operators use to understand and act on it.
Role overview
You'll join the Observability team and take ownership of features end to end. That covers:
- Go and Python services and gRPC APIs in the control and data planes.
- The data flows that carry discovery and telemetry results into NetBox.
- The React dashboards and interfaces where customers monitor network and device health, explore telemetry, review discovered data, and manage their agent fleet.
You'll work closely with product, design, and other engineering teams, and you'll help run the services the team owns in production.
This role is hands-on. You'll ship features across the stack, improve reliability and performance, and help define the architecture and practices needed to scale network discovery and assurance to large, complex customer environments.
What you'll do
- Design, build, and operate backend services in Go and Python for discovery, assurance, fleet management, and data ingestion.
- Define and evolve gRPC and REST APIs with clear, versioned contracts using Protocol Buffers and OpenAPI.
- Build React and TypeScript monitoring and telemetry dashboards that show device, interface, and network health in real time, with time-series charts, status views, and drill-down from fleet to device to interface.
- Design dashboard experiences that help operators spot problems fast: sensible defaults, time-range and filter controls, thresholds and alert states, and clear links from a metric to the underlying device in NetBox.
- Work with backend engineers on the query and aggregation APIs that power dashboards, so they stay fast with large fleets and high-frequency telemetry.
- Build type-safe integration between frontend and backend using generated API clients, shared schemas, and consistent error and auth handling.
- Participate in the team's on-call rotation for the services it owns.
- Add automated tests across the stack (unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end) and enforce quality gates in CI.
- Collaborate with product managers, designers, customer-facing teams, and other engineering teams. The goal is for features to solve real network operator problems.
- Use AI-enabled development tools and agentic workflows day to day to speed up design, coding, testing, code review, and incident triage, and help the team adopt them effectively and safely.
- Review code, mentor teammates, and share best practices for service design, API design, and frontend engineering.
- Participate in planning processes and help shape the roadmap.
What we're looking for (minimum qualifications)
- Experience: 5+ years of professional software engineering, with meaningful production experience on both backend and frontend.
- Backend:
- Production experience with Go and Python: strong in at least one and working proficiency in the other.
- Hands-on experience designing and operating gRPC services with Protocol Buffers, including schema evolution and backward compatibility, streaming RPCs, deadlines, interceptors/middleware, and error handling.
- Experience building distributed, event-driven systems, including message queues (e.g., RabbitMQ or Kafka), asynchronous job processing, and idempotent data ingestion.
- Frontend (monitoring and telemetry dashboards):
- Strong React and TypeScript skills, including component composition, state management, and typing best practices.
- Proven experience building monitoring, observability, or analytics dashboards: time-series charts, heatmaps, status and health views, and drill-down navigation.
- Hands-on experience with data visualization libraries (e.g., D3, ECharts, Recharts, uPlot, or Visx).
- Experience rendering large or high-frequency datasets performantly, using techniques such as downsampling, virtualization, and canvas or WebGL rendering.
- Experience handling real-time data in the browser via WebSockets, server-sent events, or gRPC-Web streaming, along with caching and refresh strategies (e.g., TanStack Query).
- Modern CSS (TailwindCSS or similar utility-first frameworks), responsive layout, and practical accessibility (WCAG), including color-blind-safe palettes and accessible charts.
- Automated frontend testing with Jest and React Testing Library, including visual regression testing for charts and dashboards.
- AI-enabled development:
- Practical, regular use of AI coding assistants and agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) across the development lifecycle: writing and refactoring code, generating tests, reviewing changes, and writing documentation.
- Good judgment about when to trust AI output, including verifying generated code, keeping changes reviewable, and protecting sensitive data such as customer network information and credentials.
- Familiarity with prompting and context techniques that make AI tools effective on a real codebase, such as project instructions, specs, and structured workflows.
- Ways of working:
- Good communication skills and a proven ability to work collaboratively in small, cross-functional teams.
- Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment and contributing to product and technical decisions.
Nice to have
- Networking protocols and device interfaces:
- Familiarity with networking protocols and concepts such as TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, BGP, OSPF, VLANs, and LLDP/CDP.
- Experience with network management and telemetry interfaces such as SNMP (MIBs, polling, traps), gNMI/gNOI, streaming telemetry.
- Network automation: Experience with NetBox, network automation frameworks (e.g., NAPALM, Nornir, Netmiko), or building agents that run in customer environments.
- Telemetry and observability: OpenTelemetry/OTLP, Prometheus, or time-series databases (e.g., Mimir, InfluxDB, ClickHouse), including query languages such as PromQL.
- Dashboard tooling:
- Grafana panel or plugin development, or embedding third-party dashboards in a product.

- You handle the full ticket flow for all K-Pro clients with SLAs met

- You have shipped at least one automation that measurably improves support

Job Description
At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Generative AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn’t just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.
We're looking for a Security & Trust Specialist to join Pencil at a pivotal moment of growth. This is a hands-on, technical role for someone with a background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role who is now building a career in security. You'll own the day-to-day security operations that keep Pencil safe — endpoints, identity and access, cloud and SaaS security — and you're happy to lend a hand with practical IT and device issues where needed. You'll work directly with our Head of Security & Trust, who will support your growth into the audit, compliance and vendor-risk side of the role over time.
Key responsibilities:
- Administer and secure endpoints (MDM/Intune, patching, encryption, device compliance), and be willing to pitch in on practical desktop support and device issues when the team needs a hand.
- Own day-to-day identity and access management — joiner/mover/leaver processes, least-privilege access and quarterly access reviews across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, GCP and other SaaS tools.
- Monitor security alerts and logs, escalate promptly, and help investigate and document security events (suspicious logins, compromised credentials, device loss, cloud misconfiguration).
- Support compliance evidence collection in Vanta for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, working alongside the Head of Security & Trust rather than owning audit strategy yourself.
- Help gather evidence for vendor and customer security questionnaires, and flag anything that needs escalating.
- Identify and implement practical improvements to monitoring, alerting and access control across cloud and endpoint tooling.
Your background:
- A background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role, now moving into (or already doing blended IT/security) work.
- Hands-on experience with endpoint management (Intune or similar MDM) and Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 administration.
- Comfortable with cloud basics (GCP, AWS or Azure IAM) — you don't need deep cloud engineering experience, but you're curious and capable of learning fast.
- Some exposure to compliance or audit evidence gathering (Vanta or similar) is a bonus, not required.
- A security certification such as CompTIA Security+, ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity or Microsoft SC-900 — or clear evidence of self-directed learning if you don't have one yet.
- A genuinely helpful, practical approach — you don't mind switching between security work and helping a colleague with their laptop.
You’ll Thrive Here If You…
- You enjoy being hands-on and don't mind switching between strategic security work and practical, in-the-moment IT problems (Human).
- You're hungry to grow a career in security and want to learn from the audits and questionnaires you'll be exposed to (Owners).
- You take ownership of problems end-to-end and don't wait to be told what to do (Owners).
- You can explain technical issues simply to non-technical colleagues (Simple).
KPIs & Success Measures
- Access reviews and joiner/mover/leaver tasks completed within SLA, with zero access-control audit findings.
- Endpoint compliance rate (encryption, patching, MDM enrolment) across the device fleet.
- Time-to-close on security incidents and IT/device issues you support.
- Quality and completeness of evidence you contribute to Vanta and vendor reviews.
Benefits:
- 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme
- Health insurance / private medical cover
- Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development
- Remote - work from anywhere in your home country
- Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy
- Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for UK employees
- Flexible working hours
Deep Dive About Pencil

We don’t have any hard cutoffs for years of experience, you’d be a great fit if you like building products but want a lot more freedom to do so with a large leeway to define your own role.
REASONS WHY THIS MAY BE THE JOB FOR YOU:
- We’re aiming to build an engineering team with high a weight to power ratio. As a result, we aren’t going to be in meetings 7 hours a day, there is no daily scrum, you will not be writing design documents. Our goal is to produce quality software, and to get it into the hands of our users as soon as it’s ready. If you agree with this then we’d love for you to press apply.
- If you’ve got a pretty broad exposure to technology and ideally a Computer Science degree (not a hard requirement). We’re looking for a capable generalist who can move between frontend/backend/dev ops but if you’ve not done it before you look at a task and say “I can figure this out easily”.
- We’re laissez faire on whether you use AI tooling; if you want to hotspot cursor on the Avanti West Coast line back from Warrington in order to solve a clients issue, we 100% back you (It just better be good code).
- We believe that years of experience is a poor metric for discovering quality. If, ideally, you’ve worked a job before, even more ideally you’ve shipped a product from start to end solo. This is the job for you if you want to ship, get it right first time.
⏳ PLINTH:
💞 WHAT WE DO
The charity sector is huge. In total income, it’s twice the size of the advertising, fashion and restaurant industries, combined. But it’s also extremely underserved by tech platforms to support the work they do.
That’s what we’re solving. An AI platform for all charities, particularly the smaller, local organisations. That saves them from millions of hours of bureaucracy, helps more people access their services, and supports them to get more funding.
🛠️ THE PRODUCT
We’re not a simple point solution. It’s a comprehensive platform, solving everything from safeguarding information, writing funding applications, taking bookings for venues/activities, giving grants and statutory reporting on Government contracts.
It becomes the system of record for the organisations we work with. On top of this record, we’re building tools to allow charities to deeply understand their impact (with mapping, visualisation and analysis) and to use this information to get more funding — through generating impact reports and funding applications with AI.
As a result of this, one day you could be working on changes to our grant management system for large grant makers or the next you could be figuring out how to improve the onboarding flow for small charities wanting to run events. It’s a broad product with plenty of room for you to define what you’d like to work on.
📈 WHERE WE’RE UP TO
We’re a team of 15 and growing fast. We have over 1,500 charities and 45 foundations using the platform, and we’re working with funders powering £55 million worth of charitable funding annually, which is growing 4x every year.
🪧 OUR VALUES
- Charities come first. While they don’t pay us, they are the people we need to be focusing on: supporting them to work towards their own missions more effectively. Being trusted by them is the most important thing.
- Childish enthusiasm is better than professional cynicism.
- Open and transparent. Better to be appear dumb than pretend you understand.
- Never the delay. Things move slowly in our sector, but we're not going to be responsible for it. We need to be unreasonably fast.
- Driven by the mission. We're going to work hard, because getting this right could be massive.
- There are no ninjas, there is no door. We need to figure out how to solve the tricky problems ourselves, because no one else is going to.
📋 THE ROLE
- Writing front-end and back-end code in Typescript.
- Shaping the architecture for new and existing features.
- Building tools to support onboarding new customers, as we help more and more people migrate off existing systems.
- Fixing bugs, and supporting the customer success team to handle user issues.
🤳 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
- Someone who can build reusable infrastructure with sensible interfaces that’s easy for team members (both human and AI) to build on top of.
- Willing to take on complex features from the initial idea to maintaining them in production.
- Multiple years experience shipping code and managing complex systems.
- Familiarity with React, ideally some experience of Elasticsearch.
- All of the standard stuff: Git, agile, testing, etc etc
- Ideally, some experience with the charity sector, either in employment, or as a volunteer/trustee.
💸 LOGISTICS
- Location: London (we work regularly from our Old Street office)
- Salary: £90-110k, with meaningful equity

TLDR: Plinth builds software for charities, foundations and funders. 2,000+ UK organisations use us, we add 7+ clients a month, and we ship constantly. HR, security, legal and finance currently sit with one person. That stops working at our next size. We're hiring someone to own a chunk of it: recruitment operations, contracts and invoicing, and the paperwork behind our ISO 27001 certification. You don't need to have done security or legal work before. You need to be the kind of person who picks up something unfamiliar, works out how it should run, then runs it properly.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
- Recruitment operations. The pipeline end to end. Keeping our tools current, booking interviews, wrangling schedules, first-pass CV screening, and working with team leads to build the tasks candidates get set. Candidates never wait on us
- Contracting and invoicing. Contracts out, chased, signed and filed. Invoices raised and paid. Unglamorous, and it matters that someone holds it
- Security administration. We're going through ISO 27001 now, and keeping a certification is more work than getting one. Reviews on a schedule, evidence that has to exist, paperwork that has to be generated. You own that calendar and it doesn't slip
- Security questionnaires. Customers send long ones and they hold up deals. You'll answer them with support from the team and our internal tooling, and build a reusable answer bank so the tenth takes an hour instead of a day. You don't need to be a security expert. You do need to be confident enough to learn out loud
- Automating the repeatable bits. A lot of this job is the same task on a loop, and a lot of it shouldn't be. Doing something by hand for the tenth time is a bug you're responsible for. You'll build the templates, automations and AI workflows that take it off your plate, then move on to harder work
- Making the role bigger. Ops is four functions and one and a half people. As we grow, you're first in line for whatever you've shown you can hold
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- You're the organiser. The one who books the group holiday, runs the spreadsheet and gets everyone to actually pay. That instinct is most of this job
- You'll have a go at unfamiliar work. We'll hand you a contract, a security review, or a process nobody has written down. You won't be on your own with it, but we need someone whose instinct is to attempt it, ask a colleague to check it, and be better at it next time, rather than wait to be shown
- You've probably done this shape of job. EA, team assistant, ops coordinator, office manager, practice manager. Somewhere you were the reliable centre of a lot of moving parts
- Nothing gets quietly dropped. Interviews, invoices, an ISO review and a half-finished questionnaire, all live at once, none of them missing
- You write clearly and fast. To candidates, to customers' IT teams, to a lawyer. Warm, plain, no waffle
- Discretion. You'll be close to salary data, contracts and personal information from day one
- You use AI properly. You've used Claude or similar beyond chatting: drafting, summarising, first passes at questionnaires, small workflows you built yourself. If you've touched Claude Code or automation tools, say so. It's how a small ops team keeps up with a company doubling every six months
NICE TO HAVE
- Exposure to ISO 27001, SOC 2 or Cyber Essentials, from any angle
- Experience with recruitment
- Experience with contracts, procurement or finance admin
- Charity, funder or local government background

- Recruitment runs without the Chief of Staff touching the logistics
- ISO reviews and evidence are on schedule and audit-ready, with no scramble the week before
- Security questionnaires come back in days, from a library you built, and stop blocking deals
- The tasks you did by hand in month one are automated, templated, or gone
- You own things outright that nobody else needs to think about
LOGISTICS

- Hours: Full time

CUSTOMER SUCCESS MANAGER
🌍 ABOUT US
Plinth is a fast-growing tech startup working with charities, foundations and local government. Small and local charities are highly effective but largely hidden. They have no spare time and no spare money. We're building the tools these organisations need and shining a light on the work they do. Read more on our blog.
🚀We're growing fast. 3-4x this year. We get 7+ new clients a month and we're shipping new features every few days. This means things move quickly and your work directly shapes how we scale. You'll have real responsibility from day one.
❤️It's really impactful work. Our clients are charities and grassroots organisations across the UK, and soon internationally. When you help them succeed with our platform, you're directly amplifying their impact. Every successful onboarding means a charity spends less time fighting with their systems and more time on their actual mission.
🤝You'll work with impressive people. Our team is talented, collaborative and slightly strange(?). We value impact, speed and openness. We work in person in our office in Old Street because we genuinely enjoy each other's company (most of the time). It’s a high trust, creative space where if you think something's a good idea, you just go do it.
💼 YOU NEED TO BE ABLE TO:
- Work both fast and slow: You'll navigate slow public sector procurement cycles one minute, then help us ship a new feature over lunch the next. The whiplash is intense but it keeps things interesting.
- Keep it real: You'll be getting the train to community centres and youth clubs where the heating doesn't work and where the paint is peeling off the walls. It’s rarely glamourous. You need to be willing to meet clients where they are, literally and figuratively.
- Listen to problems, ignore solutions: Clients will tell you exactly what they think they need. Your job is to understand the actual problem and guide them to what will really work, even when they're convinced they already know the answer. This requires self-confidence, understanding of the platform and genuine listening in equal measure.
- Teach people: Most of our clients don't love shiny gadgets. If you're the kind of person who enjoys teaching your gran to use a smartphone, this is ideal. You need to explain some fairly complex systems clearly without being condescending and still getting user adoption
- Automate and document yourself away:🤖 We're small and growing fast. Build systems and processes that make your job increasingly redundant. There’s always plenty more to do.
- Understand the difference between "urgent" and 🚨 URGENT — When you're managing 4-8 concurrent client projects and everyone thinks their issue is critical, you need to distinguish between what must happen for launch versus what can wait. This is harder than it sounds.
- Grow with the role: we need someone who is comfortable with our clients and team doubling every 6 months. Your role will rapidly change to reflect that, but it leaves you with lots of room to grow in responsibility.
🧩 WHAT KIND OF BACKGROUND DO WE THINK WOULD BE A GOOD FIT?
We’d expect a few years experience in something like the following:
- Coaching / Tutoring: You know how to meet people where they are and guide them to better outcomes
- Hospitality management: Service mindset, de-escalation skills, managing expectations when things don't go to plan, letting the customer think they’re right when they aren’t
- Event/production management: Used to juggling moving pieces, keeping stakeholders calm, making last-minute pivots when things go wrong
- Community organising/activism: Already comfortable in the spaces you'll be visiting, get the mission, used to working with limited resources
- Consulting: You're used to parachuting into chaos, extracting actionable tasks, and keeping multiple clients calm simultaneously
- User research/UX: Good at understanding what people actually need versus what they say they need, synthesising feedback into actionable insights
- Knowledge of the charity sector is a significant advantage, whether that’s as an employee, consultant or as a long term volunteer.
- It would also definitely be helpful if you have any technical experience to help with managing data migrations.
Importantly, This is a list of suggestions.
If you have experience in only some of this, or have only some of these skills, please do apply anyway.
📈 HOW CAN YOU MEASURE YOUR SUCCESS?
- Speed of getting customers successfully using Plinth: From signed contract to actively using the platform and seeing value.
- Positive recommendations: Clients recommending us positively to their networks — it’s a big source of our growth.
- Increasing use of Plinth: Clients expanding how they use the platform over time, not just maintaining baseline usage
🧠 THE ROLE
Client Onboarding (70%) — Lead onboarding from kick-off to go-live. Break down complex projects into clear phases. Manage timelines, priorities, and expectations across 7+ new clients per month. Stay on top of new features we ship every few days. Push back when needed and teach anyone regardless of background.
Operations & Process Improvement (30%) — Audit and optimise our support systems (expect to manage Intercom chat a couple of days a week). Refine onboarding workflows. Keep documentation current. Work with engineering to communicate what's urgent versus what's just a problem. Track feature requests across clients and synthesise them into product improvements.
💵 WHAT WE OFFER
- Salary: £42,000 - £75,000 depending on experience
- Equity as part of your package
- Location: In-person, Old Street, London
☎️ INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Quick (20-30 min) call with Chris as a sanity check
2. First interview with Chris and a co-founder
3. Long (2-3 hour), quite intense, in-person interview — meet the team, do tasks, respond to case studies, be challenged
4. Decision
