Certa (certa.ai http://certa.ai) is an AI-native third-party risk management platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle, from onboarding through continuous monitoring and offboarding. Enterprises from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups use our no-code platform to manage vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. Trusted by Honeywell, Uber, MARS, and Boeing, we've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries.
The Solution Architect is the primary functional lead on Certa implementations, sitting at the intersection of business consulting and technical delivery. You'll translate complex client requirements into scalable platform solutions, own the solution design from discovery through go-live, and serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders ranging from procurement leads and risk officers to CIOs and CPOs. It's a high-impact, client-facing role for an experienced consultant who combines deep domain expertise in TPRM, vendor management, or procurement with hands-on implementation skills and a passion for solving complex operational challenges through technology.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Lead solution design & delivery: Lead end-to-end solution design for Certa implementations, translating client TPRM frameworks, risk processes, and business requirements into scalable, best-practice configurations, and own the solution blueprint and technical design documentation for each engagement.
- Configure & integrate: Design and build workflow automation, intake forms, approval routing, risk scoring models, reporting, and integration patterns (APIs, SSO/SAML, ERPs, GRC tools, procurement systems), driving to a high-quality, on-time go-live.
- Advise clients: Lead discovery workshops and requirements-gathering sessions across procurement, compliance, legal, IT, and risk, acting as a trusted advisor on TPRM, supplier onboarding, and procurement automation best practices, and facilitating process-mapping and gap-analysis exercises.
- Manage the engagement: Manage client expectations proactively around scope, feasibility, and trade-offs, and produce high-quality solution documentation, configuration guides, and knowledge-transfer materials that enable long-term client self-sufficiency.
- Mentor & build the practice: Support and mentor junior Implementation Consultants through technical guidance and design reviews, and contribute reusable accelerators, templates, and playbooks while staying current on platform releases and emerging TPRM, ESG, and procurement trends.
WHAT YOU'LL NEED
- Domain experience: 5+ years in TPRM, vendor/supplier management, procurement, GRC, or supply chain operations, with a solid understanding of the enterprise vendor lifecycle (onboarding, due diligence, risk assessment, contract management, off-boarding) and familiarity with frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, or DORA.
- Implementation consulting: 3+ years of hands-on implementation consulting delivering enterprise SaaS or workflow automation (ideally TPRM, procurement, or related domains), with a proven track record leading full-cycle implementations from discovery through go-live at complex enterprise clients, across Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid methodologies.
- Technical skills: Proficiency configuring no-code/low-code workflow or BPM platforms (Certa, Appian, Pega, Salesforce, or ServiceNow), working knowledge of integration patterns (REST APIs, webhooks, SSO/SAML, data import/export), and the ability to read JSON/XML (basic scripting or query experience a plus).
- Landscape & tooling: Awareness of the TPRM/procurement technology landscape (Coupa, Ariba, ServiceNow, Archer, OneTrust, or comparable), and proficiency with project and documentation tooling (JIRA, Confluence, Visio, Lucidchart, or equivalents).
- Communication & mindset: An exceptional communicator who translates technical concepts for business stakeholders and business context for technical teams, a structured analytical thinker comfortable with ambiguity, highly organized and self-directed in a fast-paced, remote-first environment, with a client-centric commitment to delivering value and building long-term trusted relationships.
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
- Compensation: Top of market salary + bonuses and equity
- Time off: 49 days paid time off
- Benefits: PTO, full benefits, retirement and wellness plans
- Growth: Professional development support, remote workspace setup bonus
- Team building: Annual company offsites in exciting locations around the world
LOCATION
Certa is a remote-first company and we hire globally. We believe strongly in each team member working from the location that they choose. Should Certers wish to meet and work in person, they have 3 lively office locations they can travel to:
- London
- San Francisco
- Jaipur
The perfect place for Certers to collaborate, co-work, and have face-to-face meetings.
WHY CERTA
- Category leadership. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools - recognition that we're defining the category, not following it.
- Industry recognition. We've been honored across the analyst and awards landscape, including Top Tech and Customer Value distinctions in The Hackett Group's 2026 Risk Management SolutionMap, the ProcureTech100 (Advanced AI and Risk Management categories), and Best Overall eProcurement Software in the FinTech Breakthrough Awards.
- A top place to work. Certa was named one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers in the US. We're a fast-growing company where you'll wear many hats, ship quickly, and shape decisions that matter.
- Real scale with strong backing. We've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries. We're well-funded by leading investors including Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures, on the back of an oversubscribed Series B, headed towards Series C.
We're excited to meet you!

We're hiring a VP of Professional Services, reporting to the CEO, to own delivery end to end. Our PS team is full of strong operators, but the function has outgrown its structure - no single leader unifies delivery, engagement management, and AI-enabled implementation into one operating model. You'll unify the function under one delivery model, be the firm hand on customer escalations, build engagement-management excellence, and formalize how we deliver with partners. This is a hands-on, delivery-focused leadership role - you'll own scope, quality, timelines, margin, and the people who execute - not a Chief Customer Officer, sales-carrying, or figurehead seat.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Build a unified delivery model: Stand up a single PS operating model - repeatable methodology, resourcing, utilization and margin discipline, quality gates, and clear ownership across delivery, EM, and AI-enabled implementation - unifying the EMEA and US regions under one framework while preserving regional accountability.
- Own escalations & commercial discipline: Be the senior, decisive presence on escalation calls, taking the heat off ICs, and bring commercial backbone to delivery - scoping and charging for change appropriately and holding the line without damaging relationships.
- Build EM excellence: Give engagement managers the leadership layer they lack — standardization, a coaching cadence, and a durable EM operating standard that sticks where earlier, part-time efforts didn't.
- Formalize partner delivery: Define how Certa delivers with partners (e.g., Sayari and others) - what each side owns, SOWs, change orders, and new-business tracking - while keeping relationship ownership with the relationship owner and ensuring quality across every partner-led engagement.
- Govern the Managed Services transition: Partner with the Managed Services operational owner to govern the PS-to-MS handoff post-go-live, with pricing discipline, a clear handoff protocol, and safeguards against MS being offered as a concession on distressed accounts.
- Surface expansion & design with data: Build a light-touch process for surfacing expansion signals early and routing them to Sales/CSM, and use real delivery data (including utilization) to drive organizational design, SOW recalibration, and decisions on where the team should grow or become more efficient.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/keyrock/d21747c4-510c-4.description_excerpt:
SENIOR DATA ENGINEER
ABOUT KEYROCK
Since our beginnings in 2017, we've grown to be a leading change-maker in the digital asset space, renowned for our partnerships and innovation.
Today, we partner with over 250 team members around the world. Our diverse team hails from 42 nationalities, with backgrounds ranging from self-taught DeFi natives to PhDs. Predominantly remote, we have hubs in London, Brussels, and Singapore, and host regular online and offline hangouts to keep the crew tight.
We are trading on more than 80 trading venues, and working with a wide array of asset issuers. As a well-established market maker, our distinctive expertise led us to expand rapidly. Today, our services span market making, options trading, high-frequency trading, OTC, and DeFi trading desks.
But we’re more than a service provider. We’re an initiator. We're pioneers in adopting the Rust Development language for our algorithmic trading, and champions of its use in the industry. We support the growth of Web3 startups through our Accelerator Program. We upgrade ecosystems by injecting liquidity into promising DeFi, RWA, and NFT protocols. And we push the industry's progress with our research and governance initiatives.
At Keyrock, we're not just envisioning the future of digital assets. We're actively building it.
ABOUT THE TEAM AND WHY THE ROLE EXISTS
The Central Data Team (CDT) is only a few months old, but data has been Keyrock's lifeblood since day one. We're now building the Keyrock Data Platform to give Keyrockers, and the AI agents working alongside them, the data and context they need to act fast and autonomously within agreed boundaries and aligned with our shared goals. Doing that means taking data from across the company and making sense of it in real time for all the functions that depend on it: trading desks, wealth and asset management, product, risk, finance, compliance, and research to name a few.
You'd be one of the early hires in CDT and we expect you to contribute to most of the bigger decisions and build work. The standards we settle on and the way the team ends up working are still open.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Build streaming and batch pipelines that ingest, normalise, and distribute market, trading, and portfolio data, resilient to feed and exchange failures.
- Build the self-serve tooling (SDKs, patterns, templates, AI agents) so other teams publish, consume, and build on data products without waiting on us.
- Own data contracts and schema evolution. Keep schema changes from turning into multi-team coordination events.
- Design the lakehouse and time-series layer around consumer query patterns.
- Build and evolve the Data Governance and Data Quality Framework: stale-feed detection, schema validation, range checks, idempotent writes, lineage, ownership, self-healing.
- Build the derived analytics the business runs on: cross-exchange spreads, VWAP at depth, order book microstructure for the desks; portfolio views, exposure, performance for wealth and asset management.
- Make observability, cost, and performance first-class from day one.
- Treat infrastructure as code (Docker, Terraform, CI/CD) alongside our Central Infrastructure Team.
- Work in the open: write things down, partner closely with Architecture, Infrastructure, Platform, and the rest of the teams.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
Tools matter less to us than how you think about problems. That said, here's the shape of the person we have in mind.
Engineering Craft
- 8+ years of building production data systems that other people rely on.
- Strong proficiency in Python and SQL: not just being able to write a query, but being able to reason about what the engine is doing with it.
- Code that's easy for someone else to read, test, and delete later.
- Strong understanding of data modelling for both streaming and analytical workloads.
- Efficiency, quality, idempotency, and observability are taken seriously by default.
Systems Design
- You've designed and operated streaming systems on Kafka, Redpanda, MSK, or Kinesis, and you have opinions about partitioning, consumer groups, offsets, and schema registries.
- You've used a time-series store in production (ClickHouse ideally; TimescaleDB, QuestDB, or similar are fine too) and can talk about table design as a function of query patterns.
- You've worked with a lakehouse architecture and reason about table layout, partitioning, and compaction as design choices that shape query performance and storage cost.
- You build for self-healing and idempotency. Reprocessing is safe, retries don't double-write, and the system recovers without a human in the loop.
Operational Readiness
- Docker, Terraform, and CI/CD are how you work, not a separate "DevOps" thing.
- You think about cost and performance early.
- You instrument as you build: logs, metrics, and traces are part of the system from day one.
- You design for data quality and governance up front covering contracts, validation, lineage, and ownership
How You Think and Work
- You reason from first principles when a problem is new, stay pragmatic when it isn't, and update your view when you learn more.
- You treat the trading desks, wealth and asset management, product, risk, finance, compliance, and research as customers of what you build, and communicate with them that way.
- You optimise for outcomes over output. A smaller, simpler thing that ships and works beats a bigger thing that doesn't.
- You take ownership end-to-end: design, ship, operate, improve.
- You say what you think including when it's an unpopular take. You change your mind when the argument is better.
- You make the people around you better. Reviews are real, juniors grow from working with you, and peers want to work with you again.
- You're curious about how markets work. Data engineering on its own won't keep you interested here.
- You're honest about what you know and what you don't, and quick to close the gap.
- You understand financial market data: order books, trades, reference data, portfolios, exposures. Crypto, TradFi, or both are a strong plus.
NICE TO HAVE
- Lakehouse experience with Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake.
- Familiarity with DataHub or similar metadata/lineage platforms.
- Rust. Some of our performance-critical services are written in it. Interest is welcome; fluency isn't required.
WHAT YOU’LL GET
- A from-scratch mandate. You'll be among the first hires in CDT, and the platform, the standards, and the team culture are yours to shape with us.
- Strong partners. Close working relationships with Architecture, Infrastructure, Platform, and the desks themselves. You won't be building data in a vacuum.
- Autonomy on how you work. Flexible hours, remote-first, business-hours on-call shared across the team.
- A competitive salary package, with various benefits.
- A team that likes each other. Regular online get-togethers and a yearly onsite where everyone's in the same room.

MISSION STATEMENT
We are seeking a Senior Rust Engineer with deep trading systems experience and strong AWS knowledge to join our core Capital Markets division. Candidates with a passion for the Rust ecosystem and a proven track record designing, building, and operating mission-critical trading systems will be at a significant advantage.
As part of the engineering team in Capital Markets, you will take ownership of high-impact trading infrastructure, set technical direction in your domain, and drive continuous improvement in system performance, reliability, and operability. You will join a highly-profitable, fast-paced division within Keyrock, where you will be expected to make a senior individual-contributor impact while collaborating with a global, fully-remote team. This role is open to candidates located in European time zones.
JOB DESCRIPTION
- Design, develop, and optimise low-latency, mission-critical trading systems
- Own key trading stack components end-to-end — from architecture through to production operation
- Collaborate closely with quants, traders, and engineers to deliver solutions that improve trading performance and resilience
- Maintain and evolve trading infrastructure with a focus on performance, stability, observability, and operational excellence
- Troubleshoot complex production issues across exchange connectivity, execution, and market data handling
- Drive engineering standards through technical leadership, code reviews, and mentoring
- Embrace agentic engineering principles: leverage AI-assisted workflows, drive automation of operational tasks, and help evolve the team's agentic tooling
- Contribute to functional, component, and production-readiness testing for critical trading components
BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE

We are an AI research lab building foundational intelligence for the physical world.
Our models are designed to solve complex real-world challenges, powering everything from intelligent robots to next-generation wearables and media.
We work at the intersection of world models, video generation, and robotics, building systems that represent complex environments, reason about objects and dynamics, and translate high-level AI intentions into smooth, efficient, safe, and responsive actions across a variety of robotic embodiments.
You will collaborate closely with ML researchers developing multimodal world models and generative systems, and with hardware teams and partners to ensure robotic platforms, sensing, and system dynamics behave optimally in real-world operation.

- Build the Foundation: Collaborate with our world model team to build state-of-the-art training and simulation platform for robotics.
- Build the "World": Develop persistent 3D/4D scene representations that maintain temporal consistency.
- Drive Intelligence: Unlock advanced robotics planning and decision making through our in-house, cutting-edge world models.
- Sim2Real: Ensure sensing and system dynamics perform reliably in high-stakes, real-world operations, where models think, simulate, and act.
- Push Boundaries: Partner with top ML researchers to innovate on generative models and physical AGI.
AREAS OF INTEREST

About Abound
We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.
And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.
Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.
About the role
We are hiring a Chief of Staff to act as the CTO’s right hand, responsible for building the operating discipline and execution leverage required to scale the technology organisation.
This is a high-impact leadership role focused on execution, clarity and accountability. You will ensure the organisation is working on the right priorities, making clear commitments, and delivering at pace without introducing unnecessary process or bureaucracy.
Your mission is simple: build a high-performing engineering organisation that consistently delivers.
What you'll be doing
Execution & Delivery Discipline
- Ensure engineering teams are aligned to the company’s most important priorities
- Drive clear commitments, realistic timelines and predictable delivery
- Surface risks early and ensure fast, decisive resolution
Operating Cadence
- Run the core operating rhythm of the technology organisation
- Own planning cycles, delivery reviews, leadership forums and executive reporting
- Improve decision-making clarity and ensure follow-through
Roadmap & Visibility
- Create end-to-end visibility of the technology roadmap across product and central teams
- Provide clear insight into progress, risks, dependencies and trade-offs
- Enable leadership to focus attention where it matters most
Cross-Team Execution
- Manage dependencies across engineering, product, risk, compliance and commercial teams
- Remove bottlenecks and ensure coordinated delivery across a complex organisation
Organisation & Performance
- Strengthen accountability, performance management and leadership discipline
- Help scale hiring, onboarding and organisational capacity
- Act as a visible driver of a high-performance culture
Operating Model
- Improve how central teams (Platform, FinOps, AI, Security, IT) support product teams
- Establish clear ownership, interfaces and expectations to increase speed and clarity
CTO Leverage
- Reduce the CTO’s overhead on coordination, planning and follow-up
- Create space for focus on technology strategy, architecture and innovation
Who you are
- Proven experience scaling engineering or product organisations in high-growth environments
- Strong track record driving execution, delivery discipline and operational clarity
- Experience running planning cadences, portfolio visibility and cross-team coordination at scale
- Ability to work credibly with senior engineers and technology leaders
- Commercial mindset: understands how technology drives growth, customer outcomes and risk management
- High standards, strong judgement and a bias for action
You are structured but pragmatic, demanding but focused on outcomes. You know how to raise performance without slowing teams down.
What we offer
- Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity
- Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office
- 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays
- 2 paid volunteering days per year
- One month paid sabbatical after 4 years
- Employee loan
- Free gym membership
- Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

jobs.ashbyhq.com/abound/27c3af73-4041-4f.description_excerpt:
About Abound
We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.
And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.
Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.
The role
We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.
You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.
You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.
What you will own:
1. Third-party security assurance
- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.
- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.
- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).
- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.
2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance
- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.
- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).
- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.
3. The assurance calendar
- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.
- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.
- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.
4. Risk and control administration
- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.
- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.
- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.
- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.
5. Vulnerability and findings management
- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.
- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.
- Own the reporting on remediation performance.
6. Security awareness
- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.
- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.
What you will contribute to:
- The ISO 27001 ISMS, which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.
- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.
- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).
- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.
- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.
- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.
What success looks like:
First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.
Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.
Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.
Essential experience:
- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.
- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.
- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.
- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.
- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.
- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

THE ROLE
A modelling residency puts you in the center of a frontier lab. You'll be embedded in real work: placed on key production and research projects and mentored directly by our modelling team. We're building our frontier innovation around efficiency, gradient-free exploration, real-time learning, and interface design. By the end of this 8-month residency, our hope is that you leave with a track record you're proud to put on your resume and experiences that meaningfully upskill you.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Innovation: Build the future of adaptive algorithms that continuously learn. Co-design algorithms that react in real-time to product signal and feedback, and explore new ways of capturing feedback that make those algorithms better
- Cross-Stack Optimization: Collaborate across software, hardware, and algorithmic domains to drive system-wide efficiency gains
- Measure What Matters: We believe the ultimate signal of value is real-world impact. The smartest algorithm is one capable of interacting with the world — that's why product signal matters so much to how we work.
QUALIFICATIONS
We value impact over credentials. Above all, we're looking for great teammates who make work feel lighter and aren't afraid to go out on a limb with bold ideas. You don't need to check every box - but you do need to be adaptable.
- A degree or equivalent research/engineering experience in a computer science field.
- Genuine interest in, and at least one project touching: model efficiency, synthetic data, interfaces, real-time alignment, or algorithmic optimization
- Systems thinking — the ability to understand and optimize across the full ML stack
- Strong Python skills and experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow)
- Familiarity with model optimization techniques such as RLHF and fine-tuning
- Strong communication and self-awareness — you know how to collaborate in a remote environment and you're open to feedback
- You care about technical excellence and last mile impact. We value impact more than effort, and about owning outcomes end to end.
ABOUT US
Most AI is frozen in place - it doesn't adapt to the world. We think that's backwards. Our mandate is to build efficient intelligence that evolves in real-time. Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, personalized, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible - it's how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few. We believe in talent density: bringing together the best and most driven individuals to push the boundaries of continual adaptation. We're looking for builders and creative thinkers ready to shape the next era of intelligence.

OUR RESEARCH PRINCIPLES
Sweat the details. Technical excellence requires obsessing over every detail. We co-design serving, algorithms, and interface as one system to maximize efficiency and enable real-time adaptation.
Move with conviction. Extraordinary results require extraordinary effort. We operate with urgency as a unified team, concentrating resources on a few high-conviction bets where research and impact intersect.
Metrics that matter. The most intelligent system will increasingly be defined by building an algorithm that can interact with the world. Research ideas are tested through working products. If it doesn't improve what users can do, we question whether it matters. We share what moves the field; we don't optimize for paper count.
THE ROLE
This is a research role which is focused on real world impact. We care about building our frontier innovation around efficiency, gradient free exploration, real time learning and interface design. A revolution is underway where the cost of generating synthetic data is now low enough that we can treat the data space as malleable and something which can be optimized. We can steer synthetic data towards desirable properties and make previously invisible worlds with limited data coverage more visible. The most intelligent system will increasingly be defined by building an algorithm that can interact with the world. This means for the first time researchers who care about intelligence need also be obsessed with how a model interacts. If any of these statements resonate with you, we would like to hear from you.

- Innovation: innovate on our product to co-design algorithms that react real-time to product signal and feedback. Design new ways of giving feedback that drive better algorithms.
- Cross-Stack Optimization: collaborate across software, hardware, and algorithmic domains to achieve system-wide efficiency gains

Metrics that matter. The most intelligent system will increasingly be defined by building an algorithm that can interact with the world. Research ideas are tested through working products. - 4-5+ years of industry experience

About Adexis
Adexis is a London-based frontier research lab solving dexterous manipulation. Our mission is to bring machines the power of touch on the path to physical general intelligence, bringing about a future of abundance.
We are building a lean, talent dense organisation, inspired by history's great groups — the Manhattan Project, Apollo, Bell Labs, Skunkworks — where aggregating outlier individuals drove collective output that changed history.
We are backed by leading investors, and researchers from Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Google Deepmind and more.
Member of Technical Staff — Research
As a founding research hire, you could work across pre or post-training for our visuo-tactile foundation model. This might include:
- Own the model architecture end to end: how visual and tactile signals are tokenized, fused or kept separate, and learned jointly.
- Make the hard representational calls: what a contact signal is at the token level, how it aligns in time with vision, and how the two modalities trade off when they disagree.
- Own the post-training stack: how we adapt a pretrained model into a control policy using teleoperated demonstration data.
- Design the recipe: demonstration collection strategy, imitation and any reinforcement or self-improvement stages, and the full sequence from foundation model to deployable policy.
- Close the sim-to-real and human-to-robot gaps: make a policy learned from human demonstration survive contact with the real world.
- Define what good behaviour is and build the evaluation that catches a policy that looks good offline and fails on hardware.
You might be a fit if you
- Have trained large multimodal or sequence models from scratch and owned the recipe — the data mix, curricula, ablations, debugging silent failures.
- Have strong instincts for multimodal fusion.
- Have trained manipulation policies and put them on real hardware — you know the specific pain of a policy that demos well and dies on contact.
- Know imitation learning deeply and know when reinforcement is worth the instability.
- Have a point of view on learning dexterous, contact-rich skills rather than pick-and-place.
- Bonus: teleoperation systems, learning from human demonstration, real-world RL.
We seek a high ownership individual up to the task of defining this vision. This is a founding research role and will be compensated accordingly with equity.
Compensation & benefits
- Salary: £150–225k
- Equity: 0.5-2.5%
- Private healthcare with AXA
- Top of the line equipment

We’re looking for an Enterprise Account Executive to join Aibidia’s London team and play a key role in accelerating our growth across the UK and Europe.
This is a high-impact, new business role for an enterprise seller who knows how to navigate complex organisations, engage senior Finance and Tax leaders, and build momentum across multi-stakeholder sales cycles.
You’ll own opportunities from prospecting through to close, working with CFOs, Heads of Tax, Transfer Pricing leaders and other senior stakeholders at some of the world’s largest multinational organisations. With our average customer generating $7B+ in annual revenue, these are complex, high-value conversations where strong discovery, commercial acumen and the ability to build a compelling business case matter.
You won’t be doing it alone. You’ll partner closely with our SDRs, Transfer Pricing Subject Matter Experts, Marketing, Customer Success and Leadership teams to win strategic accounts and expand Aibidia’s presence across the region.
Aibidia, founded in 2018, provides the technology that enables multinational enterprises to make more considered transfer pricing decisions. Our connected, end-to-end platform provides organizations the ability to take full control of their business and implement considered tax strategies across the entire group. With over 5,000 legal entities managed on our platform and an average revenue of 7 billion Euros among our clients, we are dedicated to helping the world’s largest enterprises transform their cross-border business management, leading to healthy global business.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Own complex enterprise sales cycles from initial engagement and discovery through to negotiation and close.
- Build and manage a pipeline of strategic multinational accounts across the UK and European markets.
- Sell £100k+ enterprise opportunities into Finance and Tax organisations, engaging stakeholders including CFOs, Heads of Tax and Heads of Transfer Pricing.
- Develop relationships across multiple levels of an organisation and effectively multi-thread complex buying committees.
- Lead consultative discovery to understand customers’ business challenges and translate them into compelling commercial cases for Aibidia.
- Navigate enterprise procurement, security, legal and commercial processes to move opportunities towards close.
- Build account and territory strategies that identify where Aibidia can have the greatest impact.
- Collaborate with SDRs, Subject Matter Experts, Customer Success, Marketing and Leadership throughout the sales process.
- Represent Aibidia at industry events, executive meetings, webinars and roadshows across your territory.
- Maintain strong pipeline discipline, forecasting accuracy and deal management, and play an active role in shaping our enterprise sales motion as Aibidia continues to scale.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
- 3+ years of B2B SaaS sales experience, with meaningful experience selling into enterprise organisations.
- A track record of owning and closing six-figure, complex enterprise deals.
- Experience navigating long sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, functions and decision-makers.
- Confidence engaging and building credibility with C-level and senior executive buyers.
- Strong discovery skills and the ability to uncover business problems, quantify value and develop compelling business cases.
- A demonstrable record of achieving or exceeding sales targets.
- Strong prospecting skills and a willingness to create opportunities rather than relying solely on inbound or SDR-generated pipeline.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, negotiation and presentation skills.
- Experience using a structured enterprise sales methodology such as MEDDPICC.
- A collaborative mindset and comfortable owning your number while bringing the right internal experts into opportunities.
- Comfortable operating in a fast-growing environment where you’ll have autonomy and the opportunity to influence how we sell.
NICE TO HAVE
- Previous experience selling into CFO, Finance, Tax or other enterprise financial functions.
- Experience selling enterprise software involving transformation, compliance, data or workflow change.
- Additional language skills.
WHY AIBIDIA?
You’ll be joining at an exciting stage of our growth, with the opportunity to:
- Sell a sophisticated enterprise platform to some of the world’s largest multinational companies.
- Own meaningful, high-value opportunities and build senior relationships within global organisations.
- Work alongside experienced Transfer Pricing specialists who bring deep domain credibility to the sales process.
- Help shape our enterprise GTM motion rather than simply inherit an established playbook.
- Build your career within an international, fast-growing SaaS company transforming a traditionally underserved technology category.
Benefits & Perks:
- 💰 Share in Aibidia’s success – Enjoy a competitive compensation and incentive package that rewards your contribution.
- 🏡 Flexible, hybrid working – Flexible working hours and a hybrid policy designed to support how you work best.
- 🩺 Comprehensive healthcare – A healthcare package to support you and your wellbeing.
- 💚 Wellbeing that matters – A genuine focus on physical and mental wellbeing, supported by our internal Health & Wellbeing Committee.
- 🎉 Time to celebrate together – Regular team socials, including our much-loved summer and winter parties.
- 💻 The best tools for the job – Access to the latest technology to help you do your best work.
- 🚀 Invest in your growth – Performance-based development is part of our culture, with a dedicated learning budget for every employee.
- 🌍 Make an impact globally – Join a fast-growing global SaaS company using technology to transform a traditionally complex industry.
- 🤝 Low hierarchy, high collaboration – Work in an open, collaborative environment where ideas are valued and everyone has the opportunity to make an impact.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity, we want you to bring you, no matter your background, gender, race or sexual orientation!

About Us
At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.
We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building and scaling companies, and the other a leader in retail data and shopper analytics. Together, they have brought together frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.
The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.
The Role
This role reports to our Head of Design, Andrea. Working with him and our Product and Engineering teams, you'll design the interfaces, interactions, and systems that will shape how millions of shoppers experience algo1 in-store.
You'll tackle a unique design challenge at the intersection of digital interfaces, physical environments, and human behaviour, turning complex AI capabilities into experiences that feel simple, useful, and natural. You'll take ideas from concept to live experience quickly, test them with real shoppers, and use what you learn to make the product better.
This isn't a role maintaining an established product or polishing an existing design language. From first flows to shipped screens, you’ll define how our product looks, feels, and works, and see your work in the hands of shoppers.
What You'll Own
- Shopper experience end-to-end. Own the design of what shoppers actually see and use, from first sketch to shipped interface, making the thousands of small decisions that decide how effortless the product feels.
- Interaction and simplicity. Turn complex user problems into elegant, intuitive flows that shoppers can use instinctively, in a store, while distracted, without a manual.
- Rapid prototyping. Prototype relentlessly to answer difficult product questions before they're written in code, so engineering builds against something real rather than a spec.
- Visual craft. Set the bar for typography, layout, hierarchy, and detail. You're the person who decides what "good" looks like on the design side.
- The design system. Evolve the components, tokens, patterns, and documentation that let the whole team move faster and ship more consistently.
- Motion and micro-interactions. Use motion intentionally, to guide attention, provide feedback, and add moments of delight, not to decorate.
- Real-world validation. Observe real shoppers in real stores, translate what you see into better designs, and iterate on the loop that most product teams never build.
About You
Must Have
- Product design craft. A track record of designing and shipping digital products that customers use regularly, with a portfolio demonstrating both sharp UX thinking and exceptional visual detail.
- Motion design. Meaningful animation and interaction experience, with a clear sense of when movement improves clarity and when it gets in the way.
- Simplification instinct. Ability to take complex user journeys and reduce them to something that feels obvious in hindsight, without losing the substance.
- Design system fluency. Experience building or meaningfully evolving a design system that engineering teams actually adopted and used, including familiarity with Tokens Studio, design-to-code workflows, and modern frontend collaboration.
- Figma and prototyping depth. High proficiency with Figma and modern prototyping tools, and the judgement to know when a static frame is enough and when a working prototype is required.
- Accessibility as default. You design for the full range of shoppers who'll use the product, including those with visual, motor, or cognitive differences. Accessibility is part of your craft, not a compliance afterthought.
- Judgement under constraint. You know when to hold the line on design quality and when to ship, and can defend either call to product and engineering.
- AI-native design. You already use frontier AI tools every day to explore concepts, generate options, prototype faster, and sharpen your work. You can talk credibly about where they help and where they don't.
- Level. 4+ years of product design experience.
Nice to Have
- Brand and identity. Experience contributing beyond product into brand systems, visual identity, or design leadership across the wider surface area.
- Adjacent domain experience. Background designing AI-powered, consumer-facing, or retail technology products.
- Observational research. Experience conducting ethnographic or observational research in real-world environments, not just usability sessions in a lab.
- Startup experience. Background working at an early-stage startup.
How We Work
We're a startup, so this is a high-intensity environment. The people who thrive here are curious, proactive, and love building. If you're happiest when you're creating, experimenting, and moving fast, you'll love it here.
We draw our energy from being together, so this is an office-based role. It suits someone who enjoys the quick conversations and shared momentum that comes from building together. Our office is on what we think is the best garden square in London, just a couple of minutes from Tottenham Court Road, so it's easy to get to and a great place to build.
What We Offer
- Direct access to our founders and a real voice in the calls that shape the product and the company.
- Competitive salary and meaningful equity.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Team offsites.
- Cycle to work scheme.

The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the engineering culture, and what algo1 becomes.
The Role
We are looking for a Staff Engineer to own the full-stack development of algo1’s retailer- and brand-facing product suite.
You will be the primary engineering partner to our Head of B2B Product, James, turning ambitious and sometimes ambiguous product ideas into software that retailers and consumer brands rely on to create, launch, and measure campaigns.
This is a product engineering role, not an infrastructure or platform architecture role. You will be responsible for building the core B2B experience that enables retailers and brands to bring their campaigns onto algo1’s in-store product.
The quality of this software directly impacts the shopper experience. It is the layer through which offers and campaigns move from retailers and brands onto the in-store product. Getting this right means helping shoppers discover more relevant content while giving retailers and brands the tools to understand what works.
You will own the customer-facing web application and the backend systems that power it, including campaign creation, offer management, retailer onboarding, permissions, reporting, performance measurement, and the integrations that allow promotional and EPOS data to flow into and out of the platform.
You will work closely with product, design, and platform engineering teams, but you will be accountable for taking the B2B product from early concepts through to customer adoption, continuously improving it as we scale with retailers and brands.

The most important requirement is clear evidence that you have personally built and shipped complex, customer-facing B2B software used by real customers.

- Design reliable integrations using APIs, webhooks, authentication, and data synchronisation patterns.
- Build responsive product experiences, including asynchronous and bi-directional interactions where they create meaningful customer value.
- Establish strong engineering standards within the B2B product area while remaining pragmatic about what needs to be built now and what can evolve over time.
- Use modern AI development tools to accelerate prototyping, implementation, testing, and iteration while maintaining strong engineering judgement and quality.

Must Have

- API design and evolution. You've designed APIs that other teams and clients depend on, and you understand the trade-offs between clean design, backwards compatibility, and speed.
- Database and schema fluency. Practical experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar), including schema design, indexing, migrations, and query optimisation. Working knowledge of at least one non-relational store.
- Distributed systems experience. You've designed or meaningfully contributed to distributed backend systems, and understand event-driven patterns, asynchronous messaging, and the trade-offs at scale.

- AI-native engineering. You've shipped production code with frontier AI tools (Cursor, Claude Code, or similar) and push further into agentic workflows rather than push back on them.
Nice to Have (or We Can Teach)
- B2B or enterprise product experience. Background building for business or enterprise customers, where reliability, integrations, and data pipelines matter as much as the interface.
- Frontend craft. Comfort with a modern frontend framework (React, TypeScript, or similar) and an eye for interfaces that feel considered rather than merely functional.
- Cloud infrastructure. Experience deploying and operating distributed services on AWS, GCP, or Azure.
- Containers and orchestration. Docker and Kubernetes in production.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/artemis/fb1d3ee5-b507-4.description_excerpt:
Artemis is building the future of AI-driven cybersecurity, helping companies defend themselves effectively in an era where AI is fighting AI on the cyber battlefield.
Our platform brings a new approach to the $100B security operations market, building a live model of each customer's environment and using AI agents to detect, investigate, hunt, and respond to threats at machine speed. Just one year after our founding, Artemis is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies of all time, with customers including multiple Fortune 500 companies, Global 2000 enterprises, and AI innovators like Cursor.
We have raised $70M from Felicis, First Round Capital, Theory Ventures, Two Sigma Ventures, Lockstep VC and Brightmind. We are also backed by some of the most prominent operators in cybersecurity, including the CEO of Crowdstrike, the former CEO and CTO of Splunk, and the founders of Abnormal AI and Demisto.
Artemis's founders have built and scaled security products used by tens of thousands of customers. Shachar Hirshberg (CEO) led Amazon GuardDuty, the world's largest cloud detection product, was an early employee at Demisto, the company that invented the SOAR category, was an engineering leader at Palo Alto Networks, and holds an MBA from Harvard. Dan Shiebler (CTO) led all AI and machine learning at Abnormal AI, the pioneer of behavior-based detection, spent five years building analytics using machine learning and vector databases at Twitter, and holds a PhD in machine learning from Oxford.
Our team of software engineers, AI researchers, security engineers, and product designers comes from Google, Meta, AWS, Wiz, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Abnormal AI, Perplexity, Bridgewater, Mercor, CERN, and more.
We're growing fast and looking for builders who want to help us serve our rapidly expanding customer base.
The Role
As an SDR at Artemis, you'll be the first point of contact for prospects. You'll research target accounts, run outbound campaigns, qualify inbound leads, and set meetings for our Account Executives. You'll work with a small but sharp sales team to build pipeline and help close enterprise security deals.
This is a high-impact role—every meeting you set, every qualified lead, and every conversation directly feeds our growth.
Responsibilities
- Run targeted outbound prospecting campaigns via email, LinkedIn, and phone to security leaders (CISOs, VPs of Security, Security Engineers)
- Research prospect companies, identify decision-makers, and understand their security posture and needs
- Qualify inbound leads and route to Account Executives with clear context
- Have discovery conversations to understand prospect pain points and determine fit
- Set meetings with qualified prospects, brief AEs on context before calls
- Build and maintain accurate pipeline in Salesforce
- Hit monthly activity targets (outreach, conversations, qualified meetings)
- Work closely with Account Executives to understand what makes a qualified lead and refine your targeting
- Provide feedback to the team on market trends, common objections, and competitive intel
Qualifications
- 1-3 years in sales development, inside sales, or similar prospecting role (cybersecurity is a plus but not required)
- Comfortable making cold calls and sending cold emails without getting discouraged
- Research and research skills-you can dig into a company and find the right person to talk to
- Genuine curiosity about cybersecurity and how companies defend themselves (you'll learn fast)
- Strong communication skills
- Self-motivated and competitive-you own your pipeline and your numbers
- Comfortable with CRM (Salesforce) and sales tools (LinkedIn Sales Navigator, etc.)
- Organized and detail-oriented
Nice to Have
- Background in cybersecurity, security operations, or technical roles
- Experience prospecting to security buyers or IT decision-makers
- Familiarity with SIEM, EDR, or other security tools
- Experience at an early-stage SaaS or security company
Right to Work & Visa Sponsorship
You must have the right to work in the UK.

You'll architect proofs-of-value, navigate procurement and security reviews, and serve as the trusted technical advisor from first call through close.
This is also an opportunity to shape how we build our technical go-to-market practice in the UK market—you'll help establish playbooks, best practices, and messaging that scales as we grow in the region.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead technical deep dives, tailored demos, and solution walkthroughs for enterprise security teams across the UK and Europe
- Run structured technical discovery to understand customer security posture, existing tooling (SIEM, EDR, SOAR, identity), and integration needs
- Design and validate customer-specific solutions that meet technical, security, compliance, and business requirements
- Serve as the primary technical owner in pre-sales, partnering closely with Account Executives on deal strategy
- Answer complex questions around product architecture, detection logic, scalability, data handling, and deployment
- Support pilots, POVs, and technical validation efforts in customer environments
- Address technical objections and advise on best-practice deployment, rollout, and detection tuning strategies
- Lead responses to security questionnaires, RFPs, and vendor risk reviews (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA where relevant)
- Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Security Research, and customer teams to unblock deals and share field insights
- Build and evolve UK-specific technical sales playbooks, demo narratives, and positioning
- Contribute to pre-sales resources and messaging that serve the broader go-to-market team
What We're Looking For
- 5+ years in Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or similar pre-sales technical role in B2B cybersecurity
- Comfortable leading technical conversations with security practitioners, architects, and CISOs in complex enterprise sales cycles
- Strong understanding of modern security architecture: identity, endpoint, network, and cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP)
- Strong knowledge of SIEM, EDR/XDR, SOAR, and common log sources (CloudTrail, Okta, endpoint telemetry, etc.)
- Familiarity with detection frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK) and threat modeling
- Comfort with APIs, scripting (Python, Bash), and query languages (KQL, SPL, SQL)
- Able to clearly explain complex technical and security concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
- Trusted, credible, and customer-oriented in high-stakes sales environments
- Comfortable managing multiple deals and stakeholders simultaneously
- Experience supporting enterprise or technically complex security sales motions
- Background in security implementations, technical program management, customer onboarding, or post-sale handoffs is a plus
- Relevant certifications (OSCP, GCIA, GCIH, CISSP, cloud security certs) is a plus
Nice to Have
- Prior experience as a software engineer
- Hands-on cybersecurity background (SOC/detection engineering, incident response, offensive security, cloud security, security engineering)
- Experience in the UK or European security market
- Experience building technical sales motions in early-stage SaaS/security companies
Right to Work & Visa Sponsorship
You must have the right to work in the UK. We're licensed to sponsor Skilled Worker visas for candidates who don't already have working rights.
Compensation & Benefits
- Salary: £180,000 - £200,000 per annum (depending on experience)
- Equity: Top-of-market equity component
- Pension: Auto-enrollment pension scheme
- Location: Remote
- Other benefits: Health insurance

jobs.ashbyhq.com/augur/541d984a-2679-4df.description_excerpt:
About Augur
Augur transforms legacy sensor systems into real-time operational intelligence. We help organisations act before threats escalate – not after damage is done. Everything we build is privacy-first by design.
Our platform connects to existing cameras and sensors to detect threats, retrace events, and surface real-time insights – all without replacing a single device. Augur helps teams reduce risk, cut costs, and grow revenue through better visibility, faster decisions, and fewer blind spots.
Our culture is built on a foundation of radical candor and mutual trust. We recognise that being an industry leader requires more than just building exceptional products – it requires empowering a team of exceptional people. Individually, we operate with high autonomy; collectively, we’re unified by a shared drive to achieve our mission through a commitment to excellence.
We are looking for an ML Researcher to join our Machine Learning team in London.
This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge research and mission-critical deployment. You will own research directions end-to-end, developing novel algorithms at the intersection of computer vision, deep learning, metric learning, 3D geometry, and vision-language modelling.
You will formulate problems, design experiments, and drive your work from prototype through to production-grade systems that power real-time spatial intelligence across complex environments. We aim to publish at top venues and deploy at scale, and we're looking for researchers who want to do both.
The role includes opportunities to shape Augur's research roadmap, mentor junior researchers and interns, and strengthen our presence in the research community. Work on-site at least two days weekly, specifically one day being a Thursday.
Key Skills
- Academic Track Record: PhD (or Master's with equivalent research experience) in Computer Vision, Machine Learning, or a related discipline. Published work at leading journals or conferences is considered a strong plus.
- Core CV & Spatial AI: Deep expertise in areas such as metric learning, multi-view geometry, depth estimation, 3D scene understanding, rendering techniques, feature-based tracking, self-supervised learning, or learning-based mapping and localisation.
- Engineering Rigor: Strong Python and PyTorch skills; ability to write testable, production-quality code and participate actively in code reviews.
- Autonomy: Capable of independently formulating research problems, defining technical direction, and communicating findings clearly in both writing and discussion.
Accessibility and inclusivity
At Augur, our culture is built on radical candor and mutual trust. To solve the complex, physical-world problems our customers face, we need a team that thinks differently.
Whether you’re self-taught, have a non-traditional background, or are returning to the workforce, if you have the grit and the experience we’re looking for at Augur, we’d love to hear from you.
We are committed to fostering a diverse workplace and ensuring an accessible hiring experience - please let us know if you require any accommodations during the interview process to help you do your best work.

Our data platform powers Beamery’s reporting and underpins our AI strategy. We’re hiring a Staff Data Engineer to set its technical direction.
This is our most senior individual contributor role in data engineering. You’ll own the platform’s long-term architecture, make the calls that are expensive to reverse, and lead the work that follows. You’ll also partner with EPD leadership (Engineering, Product, and Design) on work that crosses team boundaries, and on keeping the platform aligned with company strategy. The platform exists so everyone at Beamery can make faster decisions with data they trust. The role suits someone energised by ambiguity who measures impact by what the organisation can do rather than what they personally shipped.
WHAT WILL YOU BE DOING AT BEAMERY?
- Own the technical strategy for the data platform. Define the multi-quarter architectural vision, build the case for investment with EPD leadership, and sequence delivery incrementally rather than as a big-bang migration. You take on the work with no established playbook and turn it into designs the team can execute. Expect challenges around multi-tenant consistency, correctness at scale, performance ceilings, and data modelling for AI and agentic workloads.
- Architect the analytics, semantic, and AI data layers. Define how core business metrics, feature usage signals, and skills and task intelligence data are modelled, governed, and exposed as trustworthy products to BI, self-service, and AI consumers.
- Set standards that scale beyond your team. Establish the architectural patterns, modelling conventions, and data contracts other teams adopt, favouring guardrails over review gates. Grow senior engineers into stronger technical decision-makers through design review, pairing, and mentorship.
- Own reliability and trust at the platform level. Set our approach to observability, data quality, SLAs, and incident response; lead RCAs on the most serious failures and drive the systemic fixes that prevent recurrence.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
You’re a staff-level data engineer who has built and run data platforms for internal and external consumers. You’ve built architectures that held up as they grew with a focus on data warehousing, data lakes, and both real-time and batch processing.
Teams bring you their hardest data problems. You’ve made the hard tradeoffs in distributed, multi-tenant systems and lived with the consequences. You’re just as comfortable in production: tracing how one upstream failure ripples through to customers, and making sound calls under pressure.
Your impact isn’t measured in code alone. You’ve led initiatives across team boundaries without formal authority, working directly with principal engineers, platform teams, and data scientists, and treating their constraints as part of your design problem. You’ve made architectural decisions others built on for years, and driven modernisation while balancing new technology against real delivery risk. You work with minimal direction, explain tradeoffs and risks credibly to executive audiences, and change your mind as readily as you defend a position.

- Data transformations using dbt, including patterns for large, complex projects
- Data storage (SQL / NoSQL): schema design, modelling at scale, and multi-tenant isolation
- Back-end engineering: Python (nice to have: Typescript/Node.JS)
- Pipelines: streaming, CDC, correctness, replayability, and evolution over time
- Data quality and observability: validation, testing, data contracts, monitoring, alerting, and incident response
- Infrastructure as code and containerisation (Terraform, Kubernetes)
OUR DATA STACK
Our stack will change as we grow, and you’ll be shaping those changes. The ability to learn new tools matters more than experience with any specific one.

- BigQuery data warehouse
- Kafka for data streaming between systems
- PostgreSQL & MongoDB for databases
- Typescript/Node.JS on the backend

We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own Beamery's Data Foundry end to end. The Data Foundry is our proprietary data platform, powering existing and emerging product lines including our Talent CRM and Workforce Suite. Through this, we provide data-as-a-service to customers through channels such as MCP/API. This is an emerging commercial channel. Its core capabilities span the data models, taxonomies and integrations that underpin talent and workforce decisions across our platform.
The Senior Product Manager, Data Foundry will treat data both as infrastructure embedded within our products and as a product that customers buy in its own right. Beyond internal embedding and direct commercial sales, the platform is open — customers and partners can build on top of it through MCP and API access. You will work with product leadership to set the strategy, agree what the platform provides internally, decide what becomes customer-facing, and define how the platform opens up for customer and partner innovation.
You will work at the centre of the platform, creating a balance between two essential initiatives. On one side, you serve the Talent CRM and Workforce Suite product managers as your customers, agreeing the data contracts they build on. - Build the case for Data Foundry as a new commercial channel, defining and proving the standalone commercial model alongside its role as platform foundation, quantify the value it unlocks for specific customers and deals, and measure success against value and usage metrics.
Partnership and delivery
- Lead your team to deliver solutions our customers can’t imagine working without and that deliver measurable customer and business outcomes
- Agree and maintain the data contracts with the CRM and Workforce Suite product managers, treating them as internal customers with real commitments.
- Prioritise across data science, data engineering and integrations engineering, translating tribe needs into a clear and deliverable plan.
Communication & alignment
- Communicate transparently and create alignment between peers and leadership on priorities, trade offs and progress
- Manage customer and sales expectations through well managed structured cadences

At Beam, we’re building AI that serves society.

THE OPPORTUNITY AT BEAM
Beam builds AI tools for frontline public services in the UK, US, Australia and the EU: local authorities, health services, police forces, and state, federal and central government agencies. Our products handle some of the most sensitive data governments hold, and our customers' security teams hold us to the standards they hold themselves.
The Security Operations Lead is Beam's first dedicated operational security role. You run security operations across six deployments in four regions: detection and response, vulnerability management, penetration testing, cloud security posture, external attack surface, third-party security assessment and adversarial testing of our AI products. You are also the assurance owner for the platform security controls Engineering operates: you check they work, hold the evidence, and answer for them to auditors and customers in every region. You report to the Chief Information Risk Officer and support them on security incidents.
Day to day: tuning the SIEM and working with the MDR; triaging vulnerability findings and holding remediation to SLA with Engineering; scoping and running pen tests with our external partner; reviewing Engineering's platform controls and gathering evidence; running incident response exercises; answering the security half of customer and auditor questions.
What you’ll be doing
- Running detection and response. Owning the SIEM and detection stack (a SIEM is in place but not deeply embedded; you decide whether it stays), owning detection rules, managing alert triage and noise, and selecting and managing the 24/7 MDR service so that out-of-hours compromise in any of our four regions is seen and acted on.
- Owning the vulnerability programme end to end. Detection, triage, remediation to SLA with Engineering and IT Ops, and reporting that matches what we tell customers. Includes cloud security posture (GCP, AWS), configuration drift across deployments, and the external attack surface (domains, DNS, TLS, security ratings).
- Scoping and coordinating penetration testing across all products and regions with our external partner, and owning the vulnerability disclosure programme.
- Assuring Engineering-owned platform controls: encryption and key management, network segmentation, workload hardening, privileged and non-human identity, secrets lifecycle, supply-chain integrity, audit-trail integrity, and data residency across regions. You check they operate, hold the evidence, and answer for them in ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP and IRAP assessments.
- Making Beam incident-ready. Incident response plans and runbooks, exercises with Engineering, forensics readiness, and hands-on support to the CIRO during security incidents.
- Leading AI threat modelling and adversarial testing (prompt injection, jailbreak, data extraction, caller-side attacks on telephony products) with our red-team partner, and providing security assurance for new product surfaces (desktop clients, browser extensions, integrations, public API).
- Running third-party security assessment of sub-processors and suppliers, delivering role-based security training to engineers and administrators, and reporting security metrics to the CIRO and leadership.
Who we’re looking for
- A security operations lead who has built or run detection and response in a cloud-native environment. You have written and tuned detection rules, lived with the noise, and led incidents from first alert to post-incident review.
- Experienced running a vulnerability management programme to SLA where remediation sat with engineering teams that did not report to you.
- Comfortable in GCP and Kubernetes at the level needed to assess a control, read a configuration, and know when to dig deeper with Engineering.
- Familiar with what auditors need. You have evidenced controls under ISO 27001, SOC 2 or NIST 800-53 and can tell a control that operates from one that is just documented.
- Able to influence without authority. Engineers act on your findings because you have made the case in their terms, not because you escalated.
- Precise about claims. You say what is true about the security posture, including when it is uncomfortable, and you do not let a customer answer overstate the control behind it.
- Ideally, literate enough in application security to review an SDLC gate or a code-level finding; if not, clear about that boundary and ready to buy the depth in.

£90,000 - £100,000 base salary depending on experience and performance during interviews + equity and amazing benefits (see our careers page)

WHY JOIN BITE
The problem is genuinely hard. A tender pack is thousands of pages of drawings, specifications, contracts and bills of quantities, with a tight deadline for bids. Turning it into a structured risk register, then into a defensible bid price checked against similar completed internal and external projects, is the core of our product. Every number has to show its working, because contractors won't trust things they can't interrogate and deeply understand.
You'll own engineering outright, not a slice of it. There's no engineering organisation to inherit and no layer of management to negotiate with. What exists today is a working platform and a small team; the architecture, standards, hiring bar and the shape of the function as it grows are yours to decide.

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING

Through delivery, an AI auditor tracks risks and treatments, and every completed project improves the next tender.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own the technical direction of the platform, from tender-pack ingestion to the risk engine, and write and review code on the critical path yourself.
- Turn messy tender packs and contractors' project archives into structured, citable data the risk model can trust.
- Take the risk model from research to production with Phil: reference class forecasting, Monte Carlo pricing, and the evals proving accuracy.
- Hire and grow the engineering team, and set the bar every subsequent hire is measured against.
- Establish how engineering operates as it scales: standards, code review, release, on-call, and how work gets prioritised.
WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
- A love of learning a new domain, and shipping something quickly that actually fixes what was broken.
- A track record of shipping and owning production systems end to end. Years matter less to us than evidence you've done it.
- Experience hiring, growing and leading a small engineering team.
- Strong backend depth, ideally Python in production, and comfortable working across a React/TypeScript frontend.
- Experience owning architecture for data-heavy systems: ingestion pipelines, queues, workers and storage.
- Experience putting LLM or ML features into production, and measuring whether they're actually right.
- Genuine product sense so you can independently weigh technical trade-offs against customer value.
- The instinct to keep things simple under pressure, and the judgement to know when a tactical shortcut is right and when it isn't.
- Clear communication across deeply technical, semi-technical and plain-language conversations. Contractors buy outputs they can audit, so explaining the working matters.
WHAT WILL MAKE YOU STAND OUT
- Probabilistic modelling or forecasting in production: Monte Carlo simulation, reference class forecasting, regression on messy real-world data.
- Structured extraction from long, document-heavy inputs such as contracts, specifications and drawings.
- Per-client or on-premise deployment for enterprise customers with sensitive data.
- Background in construction, tendering, estimating, cost or risk management, or document-intensive vertical SaaS.

- A seat at the table on product direction: how the risk model works, and what we build next, are still being decided.
- A supportive team: founders who want to be argued with and nobody between you and shipping.
- A domain you'll learn deeply: how contractors price and manage risk, and how AI and statistical models hold up against real project outcomes.
- Direct access to customers: you'll be invited to all product discovery calls.
- Tight feedback loops: you'll see how a change performs on real customer data within days.
- A clear path to CTO: we'll agree up front what it takes to own the whole domain.

ABOUT CARIBOU
International tax is a rigged system. Tax rules get ever more complicated, compliance gets more expensive, and the Big Four controls the expertise. They charge fees that only giant companies can afford, while smaller businesses are left flying blind.
